en.name: Farmers and sharecroppers at Munchar with their families
names: Société des Fermes Françaises de Tunisie
short_description: French agriculture in Tunisia began either through the establishment of large properties by private initiatives, or the introduction of settlers by the public authorities. This photograph shows an example from the "first phase" - one of the "companies" (of "French farms") had purchased a large plot of land, and employed a number of (largely Arab and Italian) workers to cultivate the land. The number of people in this photograph - many of whom are pitifully dressed - shows us that those employed were often large families, searching for work in an attempt to escape the poverty of their home countries.
keywords: Immigration; agriculture; colonies; Tunisia

fr.name: Métayers et chefs de culture de Munchar et leur famille
names: Société des fermes françaises de Tunisie
short_description: L'agriculture française en Tunisie a deux origines différentes: des grandes propriétés établies par initiative privée, puis des colons installés par les pouvoirs publics. Il s'agit ici de la première phase, avec une des sociétés (les "Fermes françaises") qui ont acheté de vastes domaines dont la culture est assurée par une main d'oeuvre d'origine arabe et italienne. On voit sur cette photographie au nombre de personnes, vêtues pour certaines misérablement, qu'il s'agit de grandes familles,  qui cherchent par le travail en Tunisie, à échapper à la pauvreté de leur pays d'origine.
keywords: Immigration; agriculture; colonies; Tunisie

ar.name: مصباح رمضان
description: خلال رمضان يصبح الليل نهارا وإن منارات المساجد تسطع بضوء النيون وكل القاهرة تنار والشهر التاسع من التقويم القمري الإسلامي هو مهرجان الأضواء . إنه وقت الصوم والتفكر الديني ويذّكر بالوقت الذي أنزل فيه القرآن على البشر. ومن بزوغ الفجر إلى غروب الشمس يطلب من المؤمنين الامتناع عن الأكل و الشرب والتدخين وعدم ممارسة الجنس. وعند غياب الشمس يتم الإفطار بشكل احتفالي ضمن دائرة العائلة التي تجتمع حول مائدة  الطعام الغنية. وقبل حلول موعد السحور وهي الوجبة الأخيرة قبل الصيام فإن كل بيت ومسجد ومقهى تزين بمصابيح مبهرجة. وبعد ذلك يبدأ الصيام ثانية حتى المساء. والأشياء الفردية التي كانت تصنع من المعدن من علب التنك والزجاج الملون قد استبدلت حاليا بمنافسات لها من البلاستيك من صنع الصين.

en.name: Ramadan lamp
description: During Ramadan, night becomes day. The silhouettes of the mosques shine with neon light. All of Cairo is lit up. The ninth month of the Islamic moon calendar is a festival of lights. It is the time of fasting and of religious reflection, of commemorating that at this time the Qur'an was sent down to man. From sunrise to sunset, believers are called upon to refrain from eating, drinking, smoking, and sexual activity. At sunset, the breaking of the fast is celebrated within the family circle with a lavish celebratory meal. Up until the final mealtime before sunrise, every house, mosque, and café is decorated with garish lamps. Afterwards, fasting begins again until evening. Individual objects which were once made of metal from tin cans and coloured glass have meanwhile been replaced by cheap plastic competitors "made in China."

en.name: Kazak (fragment)
description: Roughly two-thirds of this Kazak's original total size is preserved. Most notably, the border is almost entirely missing on three sides – the central field is for the most part preserved. The fragment is striking for its wonderfully preserved, fleshy wool pile. In addition to diamond and hook designs, there are depictions of animals and humans among the varied scattered motifs. A numerical inscription is highlighted on a white ground, legible against the grain of the carpet. The numbers 1323 are most likely Hejira dating, which seems credible in light of the piece's overall impression. According to our calendar, the carpet would thus have been woven in 1905. Even though the fragment is not one of the outstanding pieces of the Dresden carpet collection in terms of classical, qualitative aspects, it was shown in 2018 in the Dresden exhibition "Museum of Untold Stories" of the Dresden State Art Collections. Discovered by a carpet enthusiast in 1980, during GDR times, dirty on a building site and left to the museum, it refers to a piece of contemporary history and is quite presentable. Such finds from bulky waste containers or demolition sites in the GDR are still called "container carpets" by their collectors today.
holder: Museum für Völkerkunde Dresden (Ethnological Museum Dresden), Dresden State Art Collections
keywords: Fragment
partner: Dresden State Art Collections, Museum für Völkerkunde Dresden (Ethnological Museum)

de.name: Ehem. Wohnhaus der Malerfamilie Zeiller
description: Die Bemalung des Zeiller-Hauses, in dem Johann Jakob Zeiller seinen Wohnsitz und seine Werkstatt hatte, steht stilistisch der Art seines Vetters Franz Anton näher, weswegen es gewöhnlich diesem und nicht Johann Jakob zugeschrieben wird. Es ist ein besonders reiches Beispiel der im Außerfern verbreiteten Lüftlmalerei. Da das Außerfern zum Bistum Augsburg gehörte, dürften die stilistischen Quellen wie auch die graphischen Vorlagen vor allem von dort her stammen. Die Besonderheit der Malereien am Zeiller-Haus ist ihre virtuose Komposition aus religiösen wie profanen Motiven unter Einbeziehung von Exotismen.

Das berühmteste unter den zahlreichen Wohnhäusern mit Fassadenmalerei im Tiroler Lechtal war der Wohnsitz der bekannten Malerfamilie Zeiller. Die Fassaden des langgestreckten Hauses sind an drei Seiten mit „Lüftlmalerei“ (Außenmalerei) dekoriert, wobei die besonders reich gestaltete Giebelseite mit Erker die Hauptschauseite bildet. Sehr schönes Beispiel für die künstlerische Selbstdarstellung dieser Zeit.
dates: Das Haus mit Giebelfassade wurde im 16. Jahrhundert errichtet und später mehrfach verändert. Die Fassadenmalereien des späten Rokoko stammen aus der Zeit um 1770/75.
artist: Fassadenmalereien: Franz Anton Zeiller (1716-1794) oder Johann Jakob Zeiller (1708-1783)
history: Das Zeiller-Haus, auch „Schönes Haus“ genannt, wurde bereits im 16. Jahrhundert errichtet. Es liegt im Nordteil von Reutte am sogenannten „Untermarkt“. Von den Großbränden der Jahre 1703 und 1704 blieb es verschont. Schon Paul Zeiller (1658–1738), der Vater Johann Jakobs, der als Begründer der Außerferner Malerschule gilt, hatte hier seine Werkstätte. An der Südseite des Gebäudes sind noch Malereifragmente erhalten, die wohl um 1600 zu datieren sind. Die Fassadenmalereien der anderen Seiten sind um 1770/75 entstanden und stammen entweder von Johann Jakob oder seinem Neffen Franz Anton Zeiller.
keywords: Fassadenmalerei; Lüftlmalerei; Freskomalerei; Profanbau; Wohnhaus; Künstlerfamilie

en.name: Former residence of the painter family Zeiller
names: Former Residence of the painter family Zeiller
description: The paintings adorning the Zeiller House, in which Johann Jakob Zeiller had his home and workshop, are closer stylistically to the work of his cousin Franz Anton which is why they are usually attributed to the latter. It is an especially rich example of the “Lüftlmalerei” common in Außenfern. As Außenfern belonged to the diocese of Augsburg, the stylistic sources as well as pictorial models are primarily to be sought there. The special features of the paintings on the Zeiller House are their virtuoso composition featuring religious and profane motifs and exoticisms.

The most famous of the numerous residential houses with façade paintings in Lechtal, Tyrol, was the home of the famous family of painters Zeiller. The façades of the elongated house are decorated on three sides with “Lüftlmalerei” (outside paintings), with the especially richly decorated gable end with bay window forming the main visible face. A very pretty example of the artistic self-presentation of this period.
dates: The house with a gable-end façade was built in the 16th century and subsequently altered numerous times. The Late Rococo façade paintings originate from the period around 1770/75.
artist: Façade paintings, attributed to: Franz Anton Zeiller (1716–1794) or Johann Jakob Zeiller (1708–1783)
history: The Zeiller House, also called “Schönes Haus”, was erected in the 16th century. It is situated in the north of Reutte on the so-called “Untermarkt” (Lower Market). It survived the major fires of 1703/04. Paul Zeiller (1658–1738), the father of Johann Jakob and founder of the Außerfern school of painting had his workshop here. On the south side of the building fragments of paintings are preserved which date from around 1600. The façade paintings on the other sides originate from around 1770/75 and are either the work of Johann Jakob or his nephew Franz Anton Zeiller.
keywords: Façade paintings; Lüftlmalerei; fresco paintings; secular building; residential house; family of artists

en.name: Jewish Cemetery and Museum
description:
The cemetery of the Jewish community in Fez was one of the most important institutions of the community and was managed by the *Hebra qadicha*, the congregation in charge of the burial of the dead, who were also in charge of fire fighting.  
In fact, the Jewish community of Fez did have, according to ancient texts, three cemeteries. The first, not a single trace of which remains today, was situated outside the Bab al-Guissa and was abandoned, in the 7th/13th century, at the time when the Merinids had begun the construction of the *Fas Jdid*. The second, situated to the west of the Mellah, established itself on a plot of land offered by a Merinid princess in 869/1465. The third, still in use today, is located in the extension of the second, south of the Mellah. A number of people who played a major role in the town of Fez are buried there.  
This cemetery is distinct for its tombs, which have vaulted rooftops and are whitewashed.  
At the far end of the cemetery stands an ancient synagogue, which today houses a museum. The walls of the prayer hall are decorated with mosaics and chiselled plaster in the purest Andalusian tradition.

es.name: Cementerio y museo de la Sinagoga
description:
El cementerio judío de Fez era una de las instituciones más importantes de la comunidad y estaba administrado por la *Hebra qadicha*, congregación encargada de enterrar a los muertos así como de la lucha contra los incendios.  
De hecho, según rezan los antiguos textos, la comunidad judía de Fez tuvo tres cementerios. El primero, del que no queda ningún vestigio, estaba en el exterior de la puerta al-Guissa y fue abandonado en el siglo VII/XIII cuando los meriníes iniciaron la construcción de *Fas-Ydid*. El segundo, al oeste del Mellah, está situado en un terreno donado en 869/1645 por una princesa meriní. El tercero, todavía en funcionamiento, constituye la prolongación del anterior al sur del Mellah. En él están enterradas numerosas personalidades que han desempeñado un papel relevante en la ciudad de Fez.  
Este cementerio se distingue por sus tumbas de techos abovedados recubiertas de cal. En el extremo del mismo se alza una antigua sinagoga, hoy convertida en museo. Las paredes de la sala de rezos están decoradas con mosaicos y yeso cincelado en la más pura tradición andalusí.

fr.name: Cimetière et musée de la Synagogue
description:
Le cimetière de la communauté juive à Fès constituait une des plus importantes institutions de la communauté et était géré par la *Hebra qadicha*, la congrégation chargée de l’enterrement des morts, mais aussi de la lutte contre les incendies.  
En fait, la communauté juive de Fès a eu, selon les textes anciens, trois cimetières. Le premier, dont il n’existe aujourd’hui aucune trace, était situé à l’extérieur de la porte al-Guissa et fut abandonné, dès le VIIe/XIIIe siècle, lorsque les Mérinides entamèrent la construction de *Fas Jdid*. Le second, situé à l’ouest du Mellah, s’est établi sur un terrain offert par une princesse mérinide, en 869/1465. Le troisième, encore en fonction aujourd’hui, se situe dans le prolongement du second, au sud du Mellah. De nombreuses personnalités ayant joué un rôle de premier plan dans la ville de Fès y sont enterrées.  
Ce cimetière se distingue par ses tombes aux toitures voûtées, et recouvertes à la chaux.  
À l’extrémité du cimetière s’élève une ancienne synagogue, aujourd’hui aménagée en musée. Les murs de la salle de prière sont décorés de mosaïques et de plâtre ciselé dans la pure tradition andalouse.

it.name: Il cimitero e il museo della Sinagoga

ar.name: فردتا الباب الكبير
description:
قبل إنشاء طريق (مسقط – مطرح) عام (٤۷-١٣٤٨هـ/١٩٢٩م)، كان الباب الغربي لمدينة مسقط القديمة يُعرف باسم (باب الطويان)؛ نسبة للوادي المؤدي إلى حلة الطويان.  
  
بعدها اكتسب الباب أهمية خاصة؛ إذا أمر السلطان السيد تيمور بن فيصل البوسعيدي بإعادة بنائه، وترميمه، واستمر العمل على توسعته وتجديده، حتى أيام السلطان السيد سعيد بن تيمور البوسعيدي؛ وهذا ما تُشير إليه العبارة المنقوشة على اللوح التذكاري المصنوع من الرخام الأبيض، والذي رُفع فوق الباب:  
  
"بسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمِنِ الرَّحِيمِ  
"جُدِّدَ بِأَمْرٍ مِنَ السُّلْطَانِ سَعَيدِ بن تَيْمُورَ  
سُلْطَانِ مَسْقَطَ، وَعُمَانَ، وَظَفَارَ، وَجَوَادِرَ  
عام 1354هـ".

en.name: al-Bab al-Kabir
description:
Until the construction of the road between Muscat and Mattrah in Hegira 1347–48 / AD 1929, the western gate in the Muscat Wall was usually called the at-Tuyan Gate, after the *wadi* leading to the at-Tuyan Quarter of Muscat. As the gate became more important, Sultan Sayyid Said bin Taimur al-Busaidi had it rebuilt in Hegira 1354 / AD1935–36. As a result, the gate was renamed *al-Bab al-Kabir*, literally meaning "the Big Gate".  
The marble plaque that was placed over the outside entrance has an Arabic black-incised inscription that reads:  
*In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful  
Rebuilt by order of Sultan Said bin Taimur  
Sultan of Muscat, Oman, Dhofar, and Gwadur  
in the year 1354 AH*

en.name: Postcard of “Mecca-Pilger in der Eisenbahn, Jerusalem“. (Mecca-Pilgrims on the Railway)
description: The photograph shows three passengers through the open windows of a wooden railway carriage on their journey to the annual Hajj, one of the largest recurrent pilgrimage movements of people in the Islamic world. Before the construction of the Hijaz Railway, pilgrims travelling toward the Holy Cities usually spent several weeks crossing many regions by walking and camel caravans. The opening of the railway between 1900 and 1908 reduced this journey to only a few days, making the pilgrimage faster, safer and more accessible for many travellers. At the same time, railway travel transformed the social experience of the pilgrimage. Shared railway carriages brought together pilgrims from different provinces, languages and social backgrounds, replacing much of the traditional rhythm of caravan travel with a new form of collective mobility that reflected the technological and administrative reforms in the late Ottoman period.
keywords: Hijaz Railway; Hajj; pilgrimage; passenger carriage; Mecca; Medina; Jerusalem

en.name: St. Vitus Cathedral, Rijeka
description:
The basic characteristic of the Church of St. Vitus is its centralisation, expressed both in the spatial proportions and in the way the architectural units interconnect. The central octagonal space under the dome opens up with arcades towards lower, oval domed chapels, those serving the chancel distinguished by only slightly greater depth. The enduring Renaissance-informed static concept is apparent in the articulation of dark-marble Tuscan pillars and arches that continue along all eight sides of the central space. According to the still-extant Briano plan, an evenly lit space required a coffered dome with a lantern, however, in the building, not only was the lighting enhanced but the plastic articulation of the exterior elaborated with freestanding Tuscan pillars at the central entrance projection. Furthermore, there was another step towards the introduction of the Baroque by way of the gallery extension, characteristic of the 18th century, and, in addition, the exterior received a new vertical accent in the shape of a high tambour and a dome encompassed by a conical roof.  
The architectural quality seen in St. Vitus Church (today St. Vitus Cathedral) was never repeated in the Bay of Kvaerner area. This unique building with its parallel in the contemporary Santa Maria della Salute in Venice originates, via Sebastiano Serli, with the Brunelleschi-prototype octagonal Church of Santa Maria degli Angeli in Florence. All these influences might be a direct reflection – not only within architecture – of the international religious sensibility of the time, as shown, for example, in the never-realised plan for a central Jesuit church in Dubrovnik.

Today the Cathedral, once the Jesuit Church of St. Vitus in Rijeka, is the only Baroque Jesuit central-plan church in Croatia. Its spatial organisation, accomplished in 1638, is characterised by a regular octagon originally surmounted by a high dome and surrounded with oval chapels, an architectural solution influenced by the famous Italian architects, Andrea Palladio and Baldassare Longhena. The entire oeuvre of the designer Giacomo Briano, however, suggests even older origins related to his work in the framework of Renaissance Florence, suggested by the two colours used in the articulation of the interior: dark-grey marble pillars and arches in front of white walls. The church obtained its Baroque stamp only with the building of the gallery above the chapels in 1725, and with the execution of a new dome at a higher level.
type: Religious architecture, an Early Baroque central octagonal church with side chapels and dome
artist: Designer: Giacomo Briano (1589–1649); builder and carver: Francesco Oliviera; master builder: Bartol Winterleiter [n.d.]; gallery extension: Bernardin Martinuzzi [n.d.]; painter: Valentin Metzinger (1699–1759); sculptors: Pasquale Lazzarini (1667–1731), Antonio Michelazzi (? –1772)
history: The Jesuits arrived in Rijeka in 1626 prompted by Archduke Ferdinand II. According to the original plans, the intention was a large church with a nave and two-aisles, built alongside city walls on the sea (1633). However, because of groundwater, they opted for a dominant position alongside the *castello* (1636), which led in turn not only to the church having a central ground plan – not at all typical of the Jesuits – but for defensive reasons, a limitation on the height also. Giacomo Briano of Modena drew up both plans. Although the foundation stone was laid in 1638, construction continued into the 17th century (it was not until 1659 that the church was consecrated). In the 18th century, some adjustments to the original plans saw a gallery extension and a new dome, this time according to plans by the Friulian builder, Bernardino Martinuzzi.
keywords: Rijeka, Church of St Vitus (Vid), Jesuits, Renaissance, Early Baroque, Giacomo Briano, octagonal rotunda with side chapels and dome
tags: Rijeka, Church of St Vitus (Vid), Jesuits, Renaissance, Early Baroque, Giacomo Briano, octagonal rotunda with side chapels and dome

en.name: Neptune Fountain
description: The Neptune Fountain is perhaps one of the most remarkable pieces of 17th-century Baroque stonework in Portugal. Originating during the period of the Castelo Melhor, the fountain was commissioned in Rome shortly after 1675 , 1675 by Luis de Meneses, Count of Ericeira and Portuguese Ambassador in Rome, and made specifically for his Lisbon palace of Anunciada where it was installed in the gardens. After the earthquake of 1755, the fountain fell into the hands of other owners and ended up in several different locations. It was finally purchased by the state and placed in the gardens of Queluz in the first half of the 20th century. Today we know it was probably commissioned from Gian Lorenzo Bernini (the *“vernino*” as he is referred to in Portuguese documentation) who delegated work on it to Ercole Ferrata.
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Fonte de Neptuno
description: A Fonte de Neptuno é uma das mais notáveis peças de escultura barroca seiscentista existentes em Portugal. A sua origem remonta ao tempo dos Castelo Melhor, e foi encomendada em Roma pouco depois de 1675, por D. Luis de Meneses, Conde da Ericeira e Embaixador de Portugal naquela cidade, destinada aos jardins do seu palácio em Lisboa (o Palácio da Anunciada), onde esteve efectivamente instalada. Após o Terramoto de 1755, a fonte mudou várias vezes de mãos e de lugar, até ser adquirida pelo Estado e colocada, em 1945, nos jardins de Queluz. Sabe-se hoje que se trata de uma escultura encomendada, provavelmente, a Gian Lorenzo Bernini (o Vernino, como é referido na documentação portuguesa), de cuja execução se encarregou Ercole Ferrata.

en.name: Mosquée Sidi Boumediène
description:
The actual mosque consists of a square outer courtyard enclosed on both sides of the entrance door by two *balatas* (naves) and two raised galleries. The beautiful solid marble basin in the centre is used for ablutions.  
  
The prayer hall has five naves perpendicular to the *qibla* (eastern) wall separated by pointed horseshoe arches on pillars with rectangular or gabled bases. The naves are designed with coffered vaults of geometrically patterned plaster. They are covered by a two-sided sloped roof of curved tiles.  
  
The decorated semicircular arch of the *mihrab* (niche) is in a square frame composed of an epigraphic band above and on either side. These straight bands and the curved band decorating the arch enclose spandrels of a floral interlacing pattern. All the decoration is done in coloured stucco that highlights the contrasting pattern of short flat columns and the spaces between them in the arching band.  
  
Inside the hexagonal niche the sides are rectangular wall panels without any ornamentation; these are surmounted by small decorative arches on thin columns that give the illusion of supporting the honeycombed vault.

fr.name: Mosquée Sidi Boumediène
description:
La mosquée proprement dite est constituée d’une cour carrée extérieure entourée de part et d’autre de la porte d’entrée de deux *balata*s (nefs) et de deux galeries surélevées. La belle vasque en marbre massif au centre sert aux ablutions.  
La salle de prières compte cinq nefs perpendiculaires au mur de la *qibla* séparées par des arcs outrepassés brisés reposant sur des piliers à base rectangulaire ou à redents. Les nefs sont rehaussées de voûtes à caissons en plâtre à motifs géométriques et couvertes d’une toiture à double pente en tuiles canal.  
L’arc du *mihrab*, en plein cintre légèrement outrepassé, s’inscrit dans un encadrement composé de trois bandes (deux verticales et une horizontale) à décor épigraphique. Ces bandes et les faux claveaux qui soulignent l’arc enserrent des écoinçons à entrelacs floral. L’ensemble de ce décor est en stuc rehaussé de couleurs et met particulièrement en valeur l’alternance des claveaux. Les côtés de la niche à base hexagonale sont constitués de panneaux rectangulaires dépourvus de décor et surmontés de petits arcs forant l’assise d’une coupolette à stalactites.

ar.name: سجادة صلاة.
description: سجادة صلاة، وهي نمطية من بين تلك التي أُنتجت في قرية لاديك، قرب مدينة قونية وسط الأناضول. تحتوي السجادة على نطاق مركزي محاط بثلاثة أطر مزخرفة. وفي وسط النطاق يوجد رسم تجريدي لشجرة الحياة منبثق من إناء ماء مبسَّط؛ وفوق الإناء ثمة مستطيل يشتمل على نص غير مقروء، وفي أعلى قمة النطاق يوجد هلال ومستطيل آخر مدون فيه تاريخ حسب التقويم الهجري، '1217' (1802) منسوج بشكل جانبي. إن تصميم سجادة الصلاة هذه، الذي نفَّذته نساء القرية على نول منزلي، مستوحى من مجموعة سجادات الصلاة في القصور، في القرنين العاشر- الحادي عشر / السادس عشر- السابع عشر. وكانت النسوة يربين الأغنام ويجززن الصوف ويغزلنه ثم يصبغنه. تقع لاديك على الطريق الرئيسي للحج، المتجه من الشمال إلى الجنوب، حيث كان صنع السجاد يؤمِّن مورداً إضافياً للقرية، إذ كان يقدَّم للمساجد والمزارات في المنطقة وخارجها على شكل صدقات دينية. تظهر إحدى هذه السجادات في لوحة أوروبية في القرن السابع عشر، كصورة زيتية ساكنة رسمها نيكولاس فان غيلدر عام 1664.

ليست سجّادة الصلاة هذه، إلا أنموذجاً لتلك المُنتجة في قرية "لادك" القريبة من قونية، في الأناضول. وهذه السجّادات المصنوعة من قبل نساء القرية على أنوال يدوية، كانت تباع للحجّاج العابرين في طريقهم إلى مكة. وهؤلاء الأخيرون كانوا بدورهم يتبرعون بها للمساجد والمزارات، عند العودة.
keywords: حياة القرية؛ تجارة؛ زخرفة نباتية؛ قطعة ذات استعمال ديني؛ حج.
materials: صوف (غلاف، غطاء، وبر)؛ منسوج على نول يدوي.

en.name: Prayer rug.
description: A prayer rug that is typical of those produced in Ladik, a village near the city of Konya in central Anatolia. The rug has a red, central niche surrounded by three decorated frames. In the centre of the niche is an abstract tree-of-life motif springing from a stylised water-vessel. Above the vessel there is a rectangle with illegible text; above the tip of the niche there are a crescent and another rectangle with the date according to the hegira calendar, '1217' (1802) woven sideways. Made by the women in the village on a domestic handloom, the design for this type of prayer rug is inspired by the columned, court prayer rugs of the AH 10th–11th / AD 16th–17th centuries. The women also reared the sheep, sheered the wool, spun it and dyed it. Ladik lay on the main pilgrimage route from north to south, and these rugs were made to supplement the villagers' income, and were, subsequently, presented to mosques and shrines in the area and beyond as pious offerings. One such rug appears in a 17th-century European painting, a still life by Nicolaes van Gelder, dated 1664.

This prayer rug is an example of those produced in the village of Ladik near Konya in Anatolia. Made by the women in the village, on a domestic handloom, the rugs were sold to pilgrims who passed through on their way to Mecca. They in turn donated them to mosques and shrines on their return.
keywords: Carpet; commerce; floral decoration; religious objects; pilgrimage
materials: Wool (warp, weft and pile); woven on a handloom.

es.name: Alfombra de oración.
description:
Típica alfombra de oración de Ladik, pueblo cercano a Konya (Anatolia). Tiene un nicho central con tres marcos decorados. Un árbol de la vida abstracto que brota de una estilizada vasija de agua es el motivo ornamental central del nicho. Encima de la vasija hay un rectángulo con un texto ilegible, mientras que sobre el vértice del nicho aparecen una media luna y otro rectángulo con la fecha de la Hégira, “1217” (1802), tejida en vertical.  
Esta alfombra fue hecha por mujeres de Ladik en un telar manual doméstico, y su diseño está inspirado en las alfombras cortesanas con filas de nichos de los siglos X-XI / XVI-XVII. Las mujeres se ocupaban también de criar las ovejas, trasquilarlas, hilar y teñir la lana. Ladik estaba situada en la principal ruta de peregrinación de norte a sur y la venta de estas alfombras completaba los ingresos de los habitantes, ya que los peregrinos las donaban a mezquitas y santuarios como ofrendas piadosas. Una de estas alfombras aparece en una pintura europea del siglo XI / XVII, concretamente en una naturaleza muerta de Nicolaes van Gelder de 1664.

Esta alfombra de oración es un buen ejemplo de la producción de Ladik,  pueblo cercano a Konya (Anatolia). Las mujeres del pueblo tejían estas alfombras en telares manuales y luego las vendían a los peregrinos que pasaban por la localidad camino de La Meca. A su vuelta, estos peregrinos las donaban a mezquitas y santuarios.
keywords: vida en el mundo rural; comercio; decoración floral; objetos religiosos; peregrinación
materials: Lana (urdimbre, trama y pelo) tejida en telar manual.
tags: Lana (urdimbre, trama y pelo) tejida en telar manual.

fr.name: Tapis de prière.
description: Tapis de prière typique de la production de Ladik, village proche de la ville de Konya en Anatolie centrale. Il se compose d'une niche centrale rouge entourée de trois cadres ornés. Au centre figure un bouquet stylisé partant d'une minuscule aiguière reposant sur un cartouche qui contient un texte illisible. Au-dessus de la niche, apparaissent un croissant et un second cartouche donnant une date, 1217, tissée dans le sens de l'axe longitudinal. Reproduit par les femmes du village sur des métiers domestiques, le dessin s'inspire des tapis de prières de cour à colonnes des Xe-XIe siècles H (XVIe-XVIIe siècles J.-C.). Ces femmes tondaient également les brebis, filaient la laine et la teignaient. Ladik était situé sur la principale route de pèlerinage du nord vers le sud et les tapis étaient tissés et vendus pour compléter les revenus des villageois. Ils étaient ensuite offerts en geste pieux à des mosquées ou des tombeaux de la région ou d'ailleurs. Un tapis de ce genre figure dans une peinture européenne du XVIIe siècle, une nature morte de Nicolaes van Gelder, datée de 1664.

Ce tapis de prière est un exemple des pièces réalisées dans le village de Ladik près de Konya en Anatolie. Exécutés par les femmes au village, sur des métiers domestiques, les tapis étaient vendus aux pèlerins qui passaient par là sur leur route pour La Mecque. Ils les offraient à des mosquées ou des lieux de pèlerinage à leur retour.
keywords: vie de village ; commerce ; décoration florale ; objets religieux ; pèlerinage
materials: Laine (trame, chaîne et poil), tissage sur métier.
tags: Laine (trame, chaîne et poil), tissage sur métier.

ar.name: وعاء
description:
إن هذا الوعاء الخزفي الأبيض مزخرف بلونين على خلفية بيضاء. يمكن التعرف بوضوح على الطائر الموجود في المنتصف، حيث تتجمع حوله اللفائف. يُنسب المصدر إلى شرق إيران بسبب وجود عناصر خطية واضحة بشكل خاص في جسم الطائر الذي تم رسمه بخطين فقط في حركة واحدة. الطائر بلا شك طاووس، وهو رمز فارسي قديم. تشير الزخرفة الجذابة التي تم تنفيذها على عجل إلى حد ما إلى أن الوعاء قد تم صنعه في القرن الحادي عشر.  
  
تُعد الأواني المطلية والمزخرفة بالألوان نموذجًا لإيران والعالم الإيراني الشرقي في القرنين العاشر والحادي عشر. وتتميز بزخارفها المتعددة الألوان في كثير من الأحيان، وأجسامها الرفيعة للغاية، والاستخدام الشائع للزخارف الحيوانية.
materials: خزف، طبقة بيضاء مع زخرفة بطبقة بنية وصفراء تحت طلاء زجاجي شفاف
tags: خزف، طبقة بيضاء مع زخرفة بطبقة بنية وصفراء تحت طلاء زجاجي شفاف

en.name: Bowl
description:
The earthen white bowl has a two-coloured decoration on a white background. The bird in the centre is clearly recognisable, with tendril patterns grouped around it. Provenance has been ascribed to Eastern Iran due to the presence of calligraphic elements, particularly evident in the bird’s body, which has been drawn with only two lines traced in one movement. The bird is undoubtedly a peacock, an ancient Persian symbol. The attractive but somewhat hastily executed decoration suggests that the bowl was made in the 11th century.  
  
Slip-painted ware with coloured decoration are typical of Iran and the eastern Iranian world of the 10th and 11th centuries. They are characterised by their often multi-coloured decoration, very thin bodies and the common use of animalistic decorations.
materials: Earthen ware, white slip with brown and yellow slip decoration under a transparent glaze
tags: Earthen ware, white slip with brown and yellow slip decoration under a transparent glaze

ar.name: قسم من كسوة الكعبة
description: يتألف النموذج من عصابات متعرجة  تحيط بشكل متناوب بالشهادة (لا إله إلا الله محمد رسول الله) والتضرع "" يا الله ، فليتمجد في علاه "" والأخيرة مكتوبة بخط معكوس. ومن الممكن أن التخطيط قد صمم من قبل المعلم الخطاط ، عبد الله زهدي والذي كان يعرف بكاتب الحرمين .وقد كانت مصر تورد الكسوة للكعبة كل عام وجرى هذا تقريبا دون انقطاع ولكن منذ بداية 1970s فقد تم حياكة الكسوة في ورشة خاصة في مكة.

en.name: Section from the *kiswa* of the Ka‘ba
description:
The pattern consists of zigzag bands alternately enclosing the *shahada* (‘There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God’) and the invocation ‘O! God, May his Majesty be exalted’, the latter in mirrored script. It is possible that the calligraphy was designed by the master calligrapher, ‘Abdallah Zuhdi, who was known as *katib al-haramayn* (‘the calligrapher of the two holy sanctuaries’).  
Egypt had been supplying the *kiswa* of the Ka‘ba on a yearly basis, and almost without interruption, since Fatimid times. Since the early 1970s, however, the *kiswa* has been woven in a special workshop in Mecca.

en.name: Curtain for the door of the Ka‘ba, with the name of Sultan Ahmed I
description:
In her study of the Ka‘ba door curtains in the Topkapı Sarayı, Hülya Tezcan has identified four main styles. The earliest is that of a curtain bearing the name of Sultan Süleyman the Magnificent and the date AH 950 / AD 1543–4. The second style, to which this curtain belongs, apepars to have been popular for a long period, as known examples date from the late 16th to the late 18th century.  
  
Characteristic features of this style include the five arches at the top, as well as the zigzag panels and the reciprocal ogival cartouches at the bottom. The commisioning order and date are in the two panels immediately above the latter. This curtain was commisioned and presented to the Ka‘ba by Sultan Ahmed I.

de.name: Deckenfresko
description: Die Ausmalung der großen ovalen Chorkuppel bedeutete einen wichtigen Schritt in der Entwicklung der barocken Freskomalerei Tirols. Der Heiligenhimmel der  Augustiner mit den Ordensangehörigen und -heiligen, die die hl. Dreifaltigkeit verehren, ist als reine Figurenkomposition behandelt und knüpft darin an die von Correggio in Parma begründete Form der Kuppelausmalung in Untersicht an. Auf gemalte Architektur wird dabei ganz verzichtet. Die ringförmig angelegte Gruppe der Augustiner wird von den himmlischen Heerscharen fortgesetzt bis zur Laterne, in der die Trinität erscheint. In den hochovalen Zwickelfeldern erscheinen die vier Evangelisten.

en.name: Ceiling fresco
description: The painting of the great oval choir cupola represents an important step in the development of Baroque fresco painting in the Tyrol. The heaven of the saints of the Augustinians, with the order’s members and saints venerating the Holy Trinity, has been executed as a pure figure composition and thus establishes a link to the form of cupola painting founded by Corregio in Parma designed for viewing from below. Painted architecture is completely absent.

ar.name: قفطان.
description: ينتمي هذا النموذج إلى مجموعة تعرف بقفطانات الطول الكامل. القفطان مزوَّد بأكمام ذات حواشٍ مزخرفة وبشقوق للجيوب. لون النسيج بني، مصنوع من خيوط موشاة بالذهب ومشغولة باليد، تعرف بالقماش الحريري المقصب الفاخر. القفطان ذو ياقة مدوَّرة، ومنسوج على شكل جلباب مفتوح من الأمام يضيق عند الخصر. يتسع القسم السفلي من القفطان من فوق الأوراك مثل تنورة. القماش مزين بأزهار اللوتس وعود الصليب وأوراق كالريش. والسمة الأبرز فيه استخدام أشكال غير متكررة من الأزهار، وهذا كثيراً ما نجده في الأنسجة الخاصة بهذه المجموعة التي تبين أنها نسجت كنماذج استثنائية. إن أقمشة الحرير المقصبة والمطرزة تعتبر الأكثر أبهة في المنتجات العثمانية؛ فتفصيلة القفطان غاية في الأناقة والدقة. والرسوم متواصلة تماماً كما يُرى في القسم الأمامي والقسمين الجانبيين، وقد نسجت البطانة من خيوط الحرير الأحمر وزوّدت بخطوط متوازية. وعلى الجهة الأمامية، في الزاويتين السفليتين للقفطان يرى اسم "محمد" –  ربما خياط البلاط –  بالخط الكوفي على مربعات مضافة على النسيج. ويعتقد بشكل مرجَّح أن القفطان صنع خصيصاً للأمير بايزيد الذي قتل في عام 968 / 1561.

تبقى أثواب القفطان، وهي جزء لا يتجزأ من حياة البلاط، في الحقبة العثمانية، رموزاً للسلطنة والقوة. وهذا القفطان المصنوع من قماش فاخر خاص، مُزيَّن برسوم نباتية مُفضلة، غير مُتكررة، ويوثِّق للمرحلة، لأنه يحمل اسم معلم التفصيل والخياطة.
artist: يوجد على القسم الأمامي للقفطان اسم

en.name: Kaftan.
description:
This is an example belonging to a group known as full-length kaftans. It features hem-length decorative sleeves and slits for pockets. The fabric is brown in colour and made of threads with gilded metal wound round them by hand, a luxurious cloth known as *kemha*. The kaftan has a round collar and is woven in the form of an unfastened crossover garment; the waist is indented. It has a lower section which widens like a skirt beginning above the hips. The fabric is decorated with lotuses and peonies as well as leaves which resemble feathers; its most interesting feature is its use of a floral design with no repeat. This is frequently encountered in the textiles which belong to this group and shows that they were woven as unique examples.  
  
The *kemha* textiles are the most ostentatious in the Ottoman repertory. The cut of the kaftan is also highly careful and painstaking. The pattern is not interrupted, as can be seen in the front section and the side sections. The lining is of woven red silk with parallel lines on it. On the front of the kaftan, in the corners, the name 'Muhammad' – probably a court tailor – can be read in *kufic* script on appliqué squares. It is thought most likely that the kaftan was made for Prince Bayezid, who was killed in AH 968 / AD 1561.

Kaftans, an inseparable part of Ottoman period court life, are also the symbols of sultanate and power. This kaftan of *kemha*, a luxurious fabric, is decorated with non-repeating favourite floral motifs and is a document of the period for it bears the name of the master tailor.
dates: Second half of hegira 10th / AD 16th century.
artist: The kaftan has on the front the name ‘Muhammad’ who may have been a court artisan and the maker of this garment.
keywords: Kemha; kaftan; textile; costume

es.name: Caftán.
description:
Prenda perteneciente a un conocido grupo de caftanes largos. Tiene mangas decorativas de la misma longitud que la prenda y aberturas para bolsillos. El tejido es de color marrón y está hecho con hilos sobre los que se ha enrollado a mano hilo de oro, dando lugar a un lujoso paño conocido como *kemha*. La prenda, de cuello redondo, tiene corte de bata cruzada sin abrochar, con la cintura marcada. Desde la cintura hacia abajo se ensancha como una falda. La tela está decorada con lotos y peonías, y con hojas que parecen plumas. Lo más interesante es que no se ha aplicado un diseño floral repetitivo, característica común en los tejidos de este grupo que demuestra que fueron fabricados como prendas únicas.  
Las telas de estilo *kemha* son las más exquisitas del repertorio otomano. El corte del caftán también refleja un trabajo muy minucioso. El patrón no se interrumpe, como se puede ver en la parte delantera y en los costados. El forro es de seda roja con líneas paralelas. En los ángulos de la parte frontal del caftán aparece el nombre de "Muhammad", posiblemente fuera un sastre de la corte, bordado en caracteres cúficos en recuadros de tela. Lo más probable es que este traje fuera fabricado para el príncipe Bayezid, asesinado en 968 / 1561.

Los caftanes, indispensables en la vida cortesana del periodo otomano, simbolizan el poder del sultanato. Este caftán de *kemha*, un lujoso tejido, está decorado con motivos florales no repetitivos y es un testimonio histórico, pues lleva el nombre de su sastre.
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo X de la Hégira / XVI d. C.

keywords: Kemha; caftán; tejido.

fr.name: Caftan.
description:
Ce modèle appartient à un groupe appelé caftans longs. Il est doté de manches décoratives de la même longueur que l'habit et de fentes pour l'accès aux poches. Son tissu à dominante brune est en soie et fils dorés, selon la technique *kemha* utilisée pour les tissus de luxe. à col rond, il est coupé en forme de manteau à taille marquée et partie inférieure élargie en jupe à partir des hanches. Le tissu est orné de motifs de fleurs de lotus et de pivoines ainsi que de feuilles évoquant des plumes, mais sans répétition de motifs, ce qui est souvent le cas des vêtements de ce groupe tissés en exemplaires uniques.  
Les textiles *kemha* sont parmi les plus luxueux du répertoire ottoman. La coupe est également très raffinée. La composition tournante n'est pas interrompue, comme on le voit sur le devant et les côtés. La doublure est en soie rouge à fines rayures parallèles. Sur le devant, dans les angles, le nom de “Muhammad” se lit en écriture coufique sur des carrés appliqués. On pense que ce caftan a été réalisé pour le prince Bayézid, tué en 968/1561.

Les caftans, éléments inséparables de la vie de cour durant la période ottomane, sont aussi les symboles du sultanat et du pouvoir. Ce caftan en *kemha*, un tissu de luxe, est orné des plus prisés motifs floraux selon un agencement non répétitif ; il constitue un document sur cette période car il porte le nom du tailleur.
dates: seconde moitie de Xe siècle de l’Hégire (XVIe siècle J.-C.).
place: Probablement palais de Topkapi à Istanbul.
artist: Présence sur le devant du vêtement du nom “Muhammad”, qui pourrait avoir été artisan de la cour et créateur de ce vêtement.
keywords: kemha ; caftans ; textiles

tr.name: Kaftan.
description: Tam boy kaftan olarak isimlendirilen gruba ait bir örnektir. Etek boyunda dekoratif kollukları ve cep yarıkları bulunmaktadır. Yaldızlı metal ipliklerin sarılmasıyla elde edilen ve kemha adı verilen kahverengi ipek kumaştan yapılmıştır. Yuvarlak yakalı ve bağsız kruvaze tarzında dikilen kaftanın bel oyuğu bulunmaktadır. Basenin üzerinden itibaren genişleyen etek bölümüne sahiptir. Nilüfer ve şakayık desenleri ve tüyü andıran yapraklarla süslenen kumaşın en ilgi çekici özelliği tekrarı olmayan çiçek desenlerine sahip olmasıdır. Bu gruba ait kumaşlarda sık karşılaşılan bu durum, söz konusu kumaşların özel olarak dokunduğunu göstermektedir. Osmanlı kumaşları içinde en gösterişli olanlar bu tür kumaşlardır. Kaftanın kesimi de çok özenli ve bilinçlidir. ön taraf ve yan parçalarda desenlerin kesintiye uğramadığı görülmektedir. İç kısımdaki astar, üzerinde paralel çizgiler bulunan kırmızı ipekten dokunmuştur. Kaftanın ön tarafında, köşelerde, aplike kareler üzerinde kufi yazı ile muhtemelen bir saray terzisine ait olan “Muhammed” ismi okunmaktadır. Büyük bir olasılıkla 1561'de öldürülen Şehzade Bayezid için yapıldığı tahmin edilmektedir.

Osmanlı Dönemi saray yaşantısının ayrılmaz bir parçası olan kaftanlar, aynı zamanda saltanatın ve gücün de sembolleridir. Tekrara yer verilmeden dönemin en gözde çiçek desenleri ile süslenmiş kemha kumaştan dikilen bu kaftan, üzerindeki usta kitabesi ile de dönemi için bir belge niteliğindedir.
artist: Ön tarafında bir usta kitabesi olarak değerlendirilebilecek “Muhammed” ismi yer almaktadır.
keywords: Kumaş; Kaftan; İşleme; Kemha

en.name: Banknote
description: The Syrian banknote depicting the Norias of Hama presents one of the country’s most iconic water monuments. The great wooden water wheels, rising above the Orontes River, symbolise traditional hydraulic ingenuity and the centrality of water in Syrian urban life. Rendered with fine engraved detail, the image links national identity to heritage, memory, and the enduring relationship between society and river landscapes.
keywords: Water; banknote; Syria.

en.name: A collection of beads, curios and pendants from the Galloway Hoard
description: This collection of glass beads, curios, and heirloom objects were bundled and strung together and placed at the top of carefully packed lidded vessel within the Galloway Hoard. Everything at the top of the vessel was wrapped, but the evidence has only partly survived, with some textiles preserved in corrosion on the silver brooch-hoop this collection of beads rested on. This collection consists of: a rattlestone, a rock crystal ball in a broken silver pendent frame, five glass beads, and a ‘relic’ bead pendent capped with a perforated coin. The rattlestone and the rock crystal ball may have been used as charms or amulets. The rock crystal ball and the coloured and decorated beads are more normally found in furnished Anglo-Saxon graves from several centuries earlier than when the Galloway Hoard was buried circa AD900. Several of the larger ‘melon’ beads are heavily worn from use. The clearest clue that this unusual collection was handed down as heirlooms comes from a ‘relic’ pendant made from a damaged bead enclosed in a silver frame and capped with a perforated coin. The coin was minted for Coenwulf, the King of Anglo-Saxon Mercia (died AD821). It is likely the coin was minted several generations before the Hoard was buried. Old and well-worn, it seems that all these objects were valued for their age or past ownership.
keywords: glass; bead; Galloway hoard

en.name: Convento de Cristo
description:
"The Convent of Christ dates back to the end of the 12th century, when the Knights Templar was installed in the castle after abandoning the neighbouring hill at Ceras. The Master of the Order, Gualdim Pais, and his troops defended this hill in 1190, against the Muslim invasions of Al-Mansur. The church was built in this period, on a centred plan in the shape of a central octagon, surrounded by an *ambulatory* or circular nave, marked on the outside by a polygon with 16 sides. During this first phase, it also served as a defensive tower to which other convent buildings were linked, particularly after the Order of Christ succeeded the Order of the Knights Templar in 1315. The Ablutions and Cemetery Cloisters were built in the mid-15th century when Prince Henry was Administrator General of the Order. The former cloister has two storeys and was built in a very simple style; the latter is smaller and has one storey only, but the decoration is more interesting. Both cloisters were the work of master builders trained at the Monastery of Batalha. The name of one, Fernão Gonçalves, is inscribed on the base of one of the columns in the second cloister, which also contains the luxuriantly naturalist Manueline tomb of D. Diogo da Gama, chaplain to the king.  
The rotunda was extensively altered during the Manueline period, not only by a decorative programme that included paintings and sculptures, but also by linking it to the terrace and opening an arch giving onto the large choir. In 1510, Diogo de Arruda began work on the wide, deep main vessel, which is remarkable for the unusual, if not unique, Baroque naturalism of the façade, an explosion of foliate forms turned into architectural elements, the frame of the frontal window being particularly exuberant. High up, four kings in armour recall the attributes of D. Manuel I, though they are often erroneously identified as the Kings D. Afonso Henriques, D. Dinis and D. Manuel I, himself, as well as Prince Henry the Navigator.  
The lateral window by the Royal Cloister is fantastic in outline and the frame very naturalistic, although less intensely so. Diogo de Arruda was responsible for the vaulting that divides this part of the building into two levels, although he never finished the work. In 1515, João de Castilho, who made the curved rib vaulting with naturalistic corbels and also introduced an important heraldic and emblematic component, replaced Arruda. He also produced the exterior door very much in the Castilian style of the time and embellished it with fine sculptures of the Virgin, prophets and saints.  
Castilho was also responsible for the incomplete Chapter House and the cloisters next to these constructions, as the Royal Cloister, a masterpiece of Portuguese Classical architecture that substituted his original, was the work of Diogo de Torralva.  
The *charola*, or rotunda, has an extraordinary pictorial heritage that has been rediscovered and conserved over recent years. The filling up of surfaces almost seems to be the result of a dislike of emptiness but, over the years, the significant works also highlight the essential function of painting: the symbolic qualification of architecture. The geometric patterns, the successive repainting of Oriental-style decoration, in the “Byzantine manner”, certainly took place during the Manueline period, and was combined with various figurative themes that were adapted to the difficult structure of the walls and covering of the Knights’ Rotunda.  
Changes introduced at the beginning of the 16th century began with the impressive decoration of the vaulting that surrounds the central octagonal. Executed in *grisaille* on a large figurative scale, and re-covering the 16 trusses of the vaulting, the painting simulates architectural elements combined with recurrent themes in the painting of the time, some of which were clearly designed to promote the sovereign image of the king. Heraldry, basically the royal shield, the cross of Christ, and the armillary sphere, and some expressive human and animal figures, appear on the most varied, fantastic architectural forms that are interwoven by ropes, branches and ribbons. A programme centred on Christ, formed by the instruments of the Passion and displayed by 16 angels, is visible on the upper walls of the central tambour.  
Another programme, dating from 1510 to 1515, relative to the Life of Christ but executed in oil on wood, was conceived for the large paintings in the blind arches of the facing walls.  
Paintings by Gregório Lopes dating from about 1536 to 1538 occupied the same wall but at a lower register. His panels of *St Anthony Praying to the Fish* and *St Bernard* are still in the convent, though *The Virgin of the Angels* and *The Martyrdom of St Sebastian* are now to be seen in the National Museum of Ancient Art in Lisbon.  
The rotunda of the Convent of Christ also has a series of superb 16th-century polychrome wood sculptures around the walls, quite unique in European terms. The 16 images, each about 2 m. in height, and representing in the central figures Our Lady and St John, as well as the Apostles, the Doctors of the Church and the Prophets, were executed between 1511 and 1514 by Oliver of Ghent (Olivier de Gand) and Fernan Muñoz.  
Also part of this ensemble, were choir stalls that were destroyed in the early years of the 19th century during the Peninsula War; now only two angels remain, one of which bears the coat of arms of Portugal and the other the arms of the Order of Christ. These sculptures demonstrate the three main facets that distinguished Northern European artists in Portugal during the Manueline period: painting, seen in the polychrome of the statues, sculpture and woodwork, and which are highly visible in the central structure of the building. All these aspects harmonise in a magnificent, iconographically significant discourse.  
The statues along the walls of the rotunda, around a central group representing Our Lady and St John, have an extraordinary dignity emphasised by the plastic quality of each one and the careful polychromy they still show.  
The rotunda and the sculptures form a fundamental document for the understanding of Manueline artistic production not only for their exceptional quality and excellent state of conservation, but essentially for the artistic and cultural postulate that is revealed, placing them squarely in the Northern sphere of influence." In 1510, Diogo de Arruda began work on the wide, deep main vessel, which is remarkable for the unusual, if not unique, Baroque naturalism of the façade, an explosion of foliate forms turned into architectural elements, the frame of the frontal window being particularly exuberant. High up, four kings in armour recall the attributes of D. Manuel I, though they are often erroneously identified as the Kings D. Afonso Henriques, D. Dinis and D. Manuel I, himself, as well as Prince Henry the Navigator.  
The lateral window by the Royal Cloister is fantastic in outline and the frame very naturalistic, although less intensely so. Diogo de Arruda was responsible for the vaulting that divides this part of the building into two levels, although he never finished the work. In 1515, João de Castilho, who made the curved rib vaulting with naturalistic corbels and also introduced an important heraldic and emblematic component, replaced Arruda. He also produced the exterior door very much in the Castilian style of the time and embellished it with fine sculptures of the Virgin, prophets and saints.  
Castilho was also responsible for the incomplete Chapter House and the cloisters next to these constructions, as the Royal Cloister, a masterpiece of Portuguese Classical architecture that substituted his original, was the work of Diogo de Torralva.  
The *charola*, or rotunda, has an extraordinary pictorial heritage that has been rediscovered and conserved over recent years. The filling up of surfaces almost seems to be the result of a dislike of emptiness but, over the years, the significant works also highlight the essential function of painting: the symbolic qualification of architecture. The geometric patterns, the successive repainting of Oriental-style decoration, in the “Byzantine manner”, certainly took place during the Manueline period, and was combined with various figurative themes that were adapted to the difficult structure of the walls and covering of the Knights’ Rotunda.  
Changes introduced at the beginning of the 16th century began with the impressive decoration of the vaulting that surrounds the central octagonal. Executed in *grisaille* on a large figurative scale, and re-covering the 16 trusses of the vaulting, the painting simulates architectural elements combined with recurrent themes in the painting of the time, some of which were clearly designed to promote the sovereign image of the king. Heraldry, basically the royal shield, the cross of Christ, and the armillary sphere, and some expressive human and animal figures, appear on the most varied, fantastic architectural forms that are interwoven by ropes, branches and ribbons. A programme centred on Christ, formed by the instruments of the Passion and displayed by 16 angels, is visible on the upper walls of the central tambour.  
Another programme, dating from 1510 to 1515, relative to the Life of Christ but executed in oil on wood, was conceived for the large paintings in the blind arches of the facing walls.  
Paintings by Gregrio Lopes dating from about 1536 to 1538 occupied the same wall but at a lower register. His panels of *St Anthony Praying to the Fish* and *St Bernard* are still in the convent, though *The Virgin of the Angels* and *The Martyrdom of St Sebastian* are now to be seen in the National Museum of Ancient Art in Lisbon.  
The rotunda of the Convent of Christ also has a series of superb 16th-century polychrome wood sculptures around the walls, quite unique in European terms. The 16 images, each about 2 m. in height, and representing in the central figures Our Lady and St John, as well as the Apostles, the Doctors of the Church and the Prophets, were executed between 1511 and 1514 by Oliver of Ghent (Olivier de Gand) and Fernan Muoz.  
Also part of this ensemble, were choir stalls that were destroyed in the early years of the 19th century during the Peninsula War; now only two angels remain, one of which bears the coat of arms of Portugal and the other the arms of the Order of Christ. These sculptures demonstrate the three main facets that distinguished Northern European artists in Portugal during the Manueline period: painting, seen in the polychrome of the statues, sculpture and woodwork, and which are highly visible in the central structure of the building. All these aspects harmonise in a magnificent, iconographically significant discourse.  
The statues along the walls of the rotunda, around a central group representing Our Lady and St John, have an extraordinary dignity emphasised by the plastic quality of each one and the careful polychromy they still show.  
The rotunda and the sculptures form a fundamental document for the understanding of Manueline artistic production not only for their exceptional quality and excellent state of conservation, but essentially for the artistic and cultural postulate that is revealed, placing them squarely in the Northern sphere of influence.

en.name: Fachralo Kazak
description:
Kazak rugs were made in the south central Caucasus, between Tbilisi in Georgia and Erivan in Armenia. The area is bordered by the Ganja area on the northeast and Karabakh area on the southeast.  
Fachralo or Fekhraly is a town 40km southwest of Tbilisi. This decagon medallion is one of the most common Kazak motifs and it is often found in the prayer rug format.  
The central field has a double niche on a red background. The double niche is surrounded with a white zig-zag border and in the centre there is a *fachralo* medallion on a blue-green background. The decagon *fachralo* medallion has another decagon medallion inscribed. The outer one is decorated with a small white geometric pattern on a red background and the inner one with small blue and red geometric motifs on a white background. In the centre of the white decagram there is a *kaikalak* (four opposing ram's horns) motif. The central field is covered with stylized human figure filler motifs. There are also, on the right side of the carpet, two animal motifs. Double niche is surrounded with a *kochak* (ram's horns) pattern border on a red background. Three borders surround the central field. The main border is the common Caucasian "leaf and calyx" border on a white background. Minor borders meander on dark blue and light blue backgrounds.
keywords: Caucasus; Fachralo; Kazak

ar.name: المطرزين في دار الكسوة في القاهرة
description: بدأت دار الكسوة حياتها باسم ورشة الخرنفش – وهي مصنع كبير تأسس من قبل محمد علي باشا في عام 1817 في القاهرة. ويوجد 4000 شاب من القاهرة تجمعوا للعمل هناك كصناع في مجموعة من المهن والصنائع. ولكن في 1880s أصبحت الورشة مخصصة إنتاج الأقمشة المكية. والورشة أغلقت في أواخر 1990s. وفي أيام عزها كان هناك ما يصل إلى مئات النساجين والفنانين والمطرزين الذين عملوا في دار الكسوة. وإحدى أقسام الورشة : قسم الزركشة كان مسؤولا عن تطريز الأقمشة التي ترسل لمكة كل عام. والعديد من أعضاء نفس العائلة غالبا بدؤوا العمل هناك كصبية صغار وبقوا حتى تقاعدوا. وفي 1930s كان هناك على الأقل 60 شخصا  بعمر متوسط يبلغ 65 عاما.والصور هي لبعض العاملين الذين يعملون في قسم التطريز في دارة الكسوة ومن غير المعلوم متى التقطت الصورة ولكن من المحتمل أنها حوالي 1940s – بداية 50s .

en.name: The embroiderers of Dar al-Kiswa in Cairo
description:
Dar al-Kiswa started life as *warshat al-kharanfash* – a large factory established by Muhammad ‘Ali Pasha in 1817 in Cairo. 4000 young men from Cairo were assembled to work there as apprentices in a variety of crafts and trades. But by the 1880s, it had become a workshop dedicated to the production of the Meccan textiles. The workshop was closed down in the late 1990s.  
  
At its heyday, up to a hundred weavers, artisans and embroiderers were known to have worked in Dar al-Kiswa. One section of the workshop, the *qism al-zarkasha*, was responsible for embroidering the textiles that were sent to Mecca every year. Many were members of the same family and often started work there as young boys, remaining until they retired. In the 1930s thre were at least 60 there, with an average age of about 65.  
  
The photographs are of some of the employees working in the embroidery section at Dar al-Kiswa. It is not known when they were assembled, but it is likely to have been sometime around the 1940s–early 50s.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection

en.name: Telegraph transmitter
short_description: The primary reasons for the Ottoman Empire adopting the telegram earlier and more easily than railroads were the telegram's convenience and lack of cost. American scientist Lawrence Smith – using tools sent by Samuel Morse – made a successful trial in front of the Sultan Abdulmecid, who was interested in technological innovations and science, and began modernization of the empire. Due to the outbreak of the Crimean War, the first underwater telegraph line was established between Crimea and Istanbul. This telegraph transmitter (1912, Siemens & Halske) was used in Istanbul in World War I.
keywords: architecture; Vedat Tek; postal service; communication

ar.name: قارورة جلد عثمانية
description: هذه القارورة الجلدية العثمانية (مطرة) مصنوعة من عدة طبقات من الجلد القوي. ويتألف التزيين الخارجي من جلد محبب وحبل من الحرير الأصفر لحملها. والقارورة مزينة بشكل مزهر وخاتم سليمان وهي إشارة حماية بلون بني أفتح. وقوارير المياه الجلدية كانت جزءا أساسيا من تجهيزات الفرسان للجنود العاديين أو الضياط التي كانت شائعة بين العثمانيين. والمجموعات في ألمانيا ، النمسا وهنغاريا تستند لغنائم من حروب بين العثمانيين وهابسبورغ  فيها  قوارير مشابهة.
dates: القرن العاشر الهجري / القرن السادس عشر الميلادي

en.name: Ottoman leather flask
description:
This Ottoman leather bottle (*matara*) is made of several layers of sturdy leather. The outside decoration consists of grained leather and a yellow silk cord for carrying. The bottle is decorated with a floral motif and a seal of Solomon, a protective sign, in a lighter brown.  
Leather water bottles were a standard part of equestrian equipment for ordinary soldiers or officers and were popular among the Ottomans. Collections in Germany, Austria, and Hungary based on spoils from the Ottoman-Habsburg wars possess similar flasks.
keywords: Leather

ar.name: إبريق
description: إبريق بشكل نموذجي يستخدم غالبا لصب الماء، له جسم إسطواني مفصص وقاعدة عريضة وعنق رفيع أسطواني الشكل وكتف مسطح وفوهة ومقبض.  الجسم يتكون من تقسيمات بحجمين، الأجزاء العريضة مزخرفة بأشكال نباتية مطعمة بالفضة والنحاس، أما الأجزاء الأضيق عليها كتابات بالخط الكوفي مع بعض الزخارف النباتية.  هناك الكتابات بالخط الكوفي على الكتف والقاعدة  وهي عبارات تفاول لجلب الحظ الطيب لصاحب الإبريق. يوجد على العنق زخرفة حيوانية محفورة بالطرق لأسد محاط بشرائط كتابية، وتتكرر هذه الزخرفة على الفوهة.
dates: القرن السادس الهجري/ الثاني عشر الميلادي
materials: خليط النحاس، فضة، نحاس، مطروق، محزز، مطعم

en.name: Ewer
description: A typically shaped ewer, mostly used for distributing water, with a cylindrical ribbed body, resting on a flared base with a tall cylindrical neck rising from a flat shoulder. At the top of the neck is a spout with a curved handle fixed to the opposite side. The body ribs are of two sizes. The narrower ribs are inscribed with *kufic* bands with floral motifs. The wider ribs are engraved with rosettes inlaid with silver and copper in the centre of each circle and cartouches of vegetal designs. Both the base and the shoulders are enhanced with auspicious blessings in *kufic* script. The neck features a hammered, stylised lion encased within calligraphic bands and the lion motif is repeated on the spout.
materials: Copper alloy, silver, copper; hammered, incised, inlaid

en.name: Citadel at Tavira Castle
names: Ruins of the Citadel at Tavira Castle
description: For many years, the replacement of old abandoned citadels by either gardens or cemeteries was common practice. Tavira was no exception to this rule. Next to the Church of Santa Maria do Castelo (probably a former mosque) are some sections of wall, which are difficult to date and now provide the backdrop for a small garden. The memory of the city’s mediaeval fortifications is kept alive by an octagonal tower that has been rebuilt on various occasions and which hypothetically stands on the base of an earlier construction from the Almohad period.

es.name: Ruinas de la alcazaba del castillo
description: La sustitución de antiguas *alcazabas* abandonadas por jardines o cementerios fue una práctica corriente durante muchas décadas. Tavira no fue una excepción. Al lado de la iglesia de Santa Maria do Castelo (una más que probable antigua mezquita) quedan hoy algunos lienzos de muralla difícilmente encuadrables en términos cronológicos y que sirven de escenario a un pequeño espacio ajardinado. Como recordatorio de la fortificación medieval queda aún una torre octogonal rehecha varias veces y que, hipotéticamente, utilizó el basamento de una construcción de época almohade.

en.name: Glazed tile 'Butterflies'
short_description: The glazed tile or azulejo is a particularly expressive component of Portuguese art that is constantly being renovated. Between the end of the 19th century and beginning of the 20th century, it is strongly influenced by art nouveau, as is shown by this tile by Rafael Bordalo Pinheiro, made in one of Portugal’s main ceramic centres, the town of Caldas da Rainha.
keywords: Azulejo; glazed tile; butterflies; Portuguese culture

en.name: Glass Mosque Lamp
short_description: This mosque lamp may have been made in 19th century Hebron, a century-old Palestinian centre for glass manufacture that managed to survive despite the increasing influx of cheap, mass-produced goods from Europe. While its shape continues a style already popular in Mamluk times, its etched and gilt decoration relates closely to other neo-Mamluk artefacts produced for European tourists at the time.
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
dates: Hegira late 13th – early 14th century / AD late 19th – early 20th century
materials: Etched and gilt, light green glass

en.name: A tumbrel with knockers
description: This wooden vehicle is among the most important objects belonging to the museum.  Being both a local and traditional toy, this tumbrel is handmade (produced in a carpentry workshop) and coloured with natural madder roots. This toy can be pulled with the help of a rope tied to the front side, which thanks to a mechanism incorporated into the rear wheels induces the knockers to make sounds.
type: Toys and games; wooden toy; local toy; vehicle; toy making sound

ar.name: جزء من كتان منسوج.
description: قطعة نسيج مزخرفة بشريطين أفقيين تفصل بينهما مساحة فارغة. زخارف الشريطين متطابقة تمثل ضفيرة باللون الذهبي المصفر على أرضية زرقاء، وقد تم ملء المساحات المركزية ضمن فتحات الضفيرة بسعف النخل الملونة بشكل خفيف على أرضية إما حمراء أو سوداء. يحيط بالضفيرة من الأعلى والأسفل قلمان أحمران يضم كل منهما نقشاً كوفاًة ملوناً بشكل خفيف تزينه نماذج ملتفة ذهبية اللون، متوضعة بشكل منتظم، أما الإطار الخارجي فيتألف من تصميم متداخل موجي الشكل.يذكر النقش العبارة التالية: "نصر من الله". تقع أخميم في مصر على الضفة الشرقية من نهر النيل، وقد كانت صناعة الكتان هامة فيها، وما تزال أخميم تنتج حتى اليوم المنسوجات والصناعات التقليدية.

تمَّ العثور على الكثير من قطع القماش في مقابر قريبة من أخميم الذي هو مركز مصري مُهمّ للنسيج مُتميّز بحياكة الكتّان. ومن اللافت أن تاريخ أخميم وثيق الارتباط بتاريخ الطائفة القبطية في مصر، ويحتفظ بكتلة سكانية قبطية ذات شأن، إلى يومنا هذا.
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
dates: أواخر القرن الخامس- أوائل القرن السادس/ الثاني عشر.
keywords: أخميم؛ حرير؛ خط كوفي؛ كتان.

en.name: Fragment of woven linen.
description: A fragment with two superposed decorative bands separated from each other by an area of plain weave. Both bands are identical in design: guilloches rendered in a yellowish gold colour, set against a blue background. The central areas of the guilloche’s loops have light-coloured palmette-leaves in them, which are set against either a red or black background. The guilloche band of is flanked above and below by two red stripes, each containing a light-coloured *kufic* inscription enhanced by regularly disposed, gold-coloured scrolling motifs; the outer borders of these are formed by a system of interlocking wave-like designs. The inscription has been deciphered as: ‘victory comes from God’. Akhmim in Egypt lies on the east bank of the River Nile. The linen-weaving industry was an important one there, and textiles and handicrafts are still produced in Akhmim today.

Many Fatimid and Mamluk textiles have been found in burials around Akhmim, an important Egyptian textile centre with a famous linen-weaving industry. Interestingly, the history of Akhmim is closely linked with that of the Coptic community in Egypt and retains a sizeable Coptic population to this day.
type: Fatimid textile, woven linen and silk
keywords: Akhmim; silk; linen; kufic script; Coptic; workshop; textile; Fatmid textiles

es.name: Fragmento de tejido de lino.
description:
Fragmento con dos cenefas decorativas y una parte central de tejido liso. Ambas cenefas presentan el mismo diseño: líneas entrecruzadas de color amarillo dorado sobre fondo azul y, en los huecos del trenzado, palmetas de color claro contra un fondo alternativamente rojo o negro; enmarcan la cenefa de trenzado dos franjas con una inscripción cúfica de color claro realzada con roleos dorados; finalmente, dibujos de olas encadenadas forman los bordes exteriores. La inscripción dice: “La victoria viene de Dios”.  
La ciudad de Ajmim se encuentra en la orilla oriental del río Nilo. La industria del tejido de lino fue muy importante en esta zona e incluso hoy en día se siguen produciendo telas y artesanía.

Ajmim era un importante centro textil egipcio, famoso por su industria de tejidos de lino. Se han hallado muchos restos textiles fatimíes y mamelucos en tumbas de los alrededores de esta ciudad. La historia de Ajmim está también estrechamente unida a la comunidad copta, aún hoy muy abundante.
dates: Finales del siglo V-principios del VI de la Hégira / siglo XII d. C.
keywords: Ajmim; seda; lino; escritura cúfica

fr.name: Fragment de lin tissé.
description: Fragment de lin tissé fait de deux bandes décoratives séparées l'une de l'autre par une zone de tissage sans ornement. Toutes deux sont de dessin identique : effet de guillochis en tresse de couleur jaune d'or sur fond bleu. L'espace délimité par le croisement des deux parties de la tresse est occupé par une palmette de couleur pâle sur fond rouge ou noir. Chaque bande est comprise entre deux frises rouges contenant chacune une inscription en coufique de couleur claire rehaussée de volutes dorées de disposition régulière. Leur bordure externe est constituée par un motif de vagues imbriquées. L'inscription affirme : “La victoire vient de Dieu.” L'industrie du tissage du lin était importante à Akhmim, où tissus et objets artisanaux sont encore produits de nos jours. L'histoire d'Akhmim est étroitement liée à celle de la communauté copte d'Égypte et conserve une appréciable population adepte de cette religion.

De nombreuses étoffes fatimides et mameloukes furent découvertes dans des sépultures aux environs d’Akhmim, important centre textile égyptien dont l’industrie du tissage du lin était renommée. Il est intéressant de noter que l’histoire d’Akhmim est étroitement liée à celle de la communauté copte d’Égypte, une cité qui  compte encore une population copte assez importante.
dates: Fin Ve siècle-début VIe siècle de l’Hégire (XIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Akhmim ; soie ; lin ; écriture coufique

ar.name: كتاب التصريف لمن عجز عن التأليف في الطب
description: أبو القاسم خلف ابن العباس الزهراوي الأنصاري، المعروف أكثر باسم الزهراوي، ذاع صيته بفضل الاكتشافات التي حققها في مجال الجراحة. وتمثّل هذه المخطوطة المجلد الأخير من موسوعته الطبية المؤلَّفة من ثلاثين جزءًا، والتي تناولت الطب والجسم البشري، وجمعها الزهراوي على مدى خمسين عامًا. وفي هذا المجلد، يقدّم الجرّاح العربي الأندلسي شرحًا تفصيليًا لتقنيات الجراحة والأدوات المناسبة لإجراء مختلف التدخلات الطبية، وقد ابتكر العديد منها بنفسه. وتحتوي هذه المخطوطة على نحو 158 رسمًا لأدوات جراحية، ويبدو أن الغاية منها كانت توضيحية بالدرجة الأولى. ويمكن استنتاج ذلك من طريقة تنفيذ هذه الرسوم، التي تشير إلى أن إدراجها كان بدافع عملي أكثر منه فني. ومع ذلك، وعلى الرغم من هذا النقص الظاهري في العناية بالرسم التقني، فإن هذه المخطوطة تُعد ذات قيمة لا تُقدَّر بثمن نظرًا للأثر العميق الذي تركه نصّها في تاريخ الطب عمومًا. فقد كان الزهراوي رائدًا في مجاله، ومهّد الطريق لقيام الجراحة الحديثة.
dates: أواخر القرن الحادي عشر الهجري / أواخر القرن السابع عشر الميلادي
keywords: الزهراوي; كتاب التصريف; الطب
materials: حبر أحمر وبنفسجي وأسود على ورق. خط مغربي، مكوَّن من 20سطرًا في كل صفحة.
tags: حبر أحمر وبنفسجي وأسود على ورق. خط مغربي، مكوَّن من 20سطرًا في كل صفحة.

en.name: *Kitab al-Tasrif li-man 'ajiza 'an al-ta'lif fi al-tibb* (The arrangement of manifold medical knowledge for one who is not able to compile a book for himself: on surgery and instruments)
description:
Abu al-Qasim Khalaf ibn al-'Abbas al-Zahrawi al-Ansari, more commonly referred to as Al-Zahrawi, made a name for himself through the discoveries he made in the fields of surgery. This manuscript is the last volume of Al-Zahrawi's 30-part encyclopaedia on medicine and the human body that he compiled over the course of 50 years. In this volume the Arab-Andalusian surgeon goes into great detail about the techniques of surgery and the suitable instruments to perform various medical interventions, many of which he invented himself.  
This particular manuscript contains some 158 illustrations of surgical equipment whose purpose seems to have been demonstrative in nature. Such an interpretation can be made due to the way in which these images were executed, suggesting that the motive for their inclusion had a more practical approach than an artistic one. Even so, despite this apparent lack of attention to technical drawing, this manuscript is of immeasurable value because of the impact its text had on the history of medicine as a whole. Al-Zahrawi was a pioneer in his field and paved the way for modern day surgery.
dates: Late 11th century AH / late 17th century AD
keywords: Al-Zahrawi; Kitab al-Tasrif; medicine
materials: Red, purple and black ink on paper. Calligraphic *maghrebi* script of 20 lines per page.
tags: Red, purple and black ink on paper. Calligraphic maghrebi script of 20 lines per page.
