fr.name: Grande Mosquée de Cordoue.
description:
La mosquée de Cordoue est le résultat d'une série d'agrandissements et de restaurations qui se sont juxtaposés du début de sa construction, à l'époque émirale, jusqu'à la chute du califat.  
Bien que les premières références en soient confuses, les travaux durent commencer autour de 169 H / 785-86 J.-C. durant l'émirat d'Abd al-Rahman Ier. Par la suite, presque tous les émirs et tous les califes sont intervenus sur la mosquée *aljama* de la capitale. Érigé sur une ancienne église wisigothique, l'édifice d'origine était un bâtiment carré qui incluait une cour et une salle de prière couverte. Dix rangées d'arcs la divisaient en onze nefs perpendiculaires au mur de la *qibla*, percé d'un simple *mihrab*. Le plus caractéristique de ce premier temple est la solution consistant à doubler les arcs en hauteur pour donner une plus grande élévation à la salle. Les arcs superposés font alterner les claveaux en pierre blanche avec d'autres en brique rouge. Bien que le matériau utilisé ait été du réemploi tiré de constructions romaines et wisigothiques et transporté sur place, les travaux ont duré de nombreuses années et le bâtiment fut terminé par Hicham Ier.  
Le premier agrandissement de la mosquée, à l'époque d'Abd al-Rahman II, a consisté à allonger la salle de prière vers le sud et à déplacer le mur de la *qibla* de quelque 26 mètres, tout en respectant l'élévationdu bâtiment primitif. C'est alors qu'apparaissent les premiers chapiteaux fabriqués *ex professo* à côtés de ceux réutilisés jusque-là. Les travaux furent achevés par Muhammad Ier, qui termina la *maqsura* et restaura la porte de San Esteban. Ses fils, al-Mundir et Abd al-Rahman III, construisirent respectivement la salle du trésor et le *sabat*.  
Au IVe siècle H (Xe siècle J.-C.), Abd al-Rahman III, premier calife de la dynastie, entreprit la construction du mur d'entrée de la salle de prière et l'agrandissement de la cour, à laquelle il adossa un nouveau minaret dont la partie inférieure subsiste dans l'actuel clocher de la cathédrale.  
Mais l'agrandissement le plus important fut réalisé dès l'accession au trône califal de al-Hakam II, successeur d'Abd al-Rahman III. De nouveau, les arcatures de la salle de prière furent prolongées vers le sud, terminées par une monumentale *maqsoura*, et c'est alors que fut dressé l'actuel mur de la *qibla* avec le *mihrab*, les portes du trésor et le *sabat*. Par la riche décoration de mosaïques, les panneaux de marbre sculpté, les arcs entrecroisés, et par la délicate structure des supports architectoniques, cette zone est la plus spectaculaire et la plus emblématique de la mosquée. Les coupoles, dont cinq sont encore en place, sont un autre élément introduit à ce moment-là. La coupole située face au *mihrab* est particulièrement belle du fait de ses mosaïques.  
C'est à la fin du IVe siècle H (Xe siècle J.-C.), à l'époque d'Hicham II, sous le gouvernement du puissant *hajib* de Cordoue al-Mansour, que fut commencé le dernier agrandissement majeur de l'édifice. Devant l'impossibilité d'agrandir encore la mosquée vers le sud, on choisit de l'agrandir à l'est par huit nouvelles nefs. L'élévation antérieure de la salle et de la cour, également agrandie, fut respectée ; le *mihrab* et la *maqsura* d'al-Hakam II sont restés intacts – mais, du coup, ils ont simplement cessé de se trouver au centre du mur de la *qibla*.

Elle fut la plus importante de l'Occident musulman. Telle que nous la connaissons aujourd'hui, elle est le résultat d'une série d'agrandissements financés par les émirs et les califes omeyyades, qui légitimèrent ainsi leur pouvoir et réussirent de surcroît à augmenter la capacité d'accueil de la mosquée, ce que l'accroissement de la population avait rendu indispensable. L'unité spatiale de la majestueuse salle de prière (de 12 000 mètres carrés) fut obtenue en répétant le système – génial – des doubles arcatures sur colonnes qui, organisées en nefs perpendiculaires à la *qibla*, produisent l'effet d'une forêt de palmiers. L'ensemble est complété par la *maqsoura* et le *mihrab*, somptueusement ornementés.

artist: Abd al-Rahman Ier (r. 139-172 H / 756-788 J.-C.) ; Hicham Ier (r. 171-179 H / 788-796 J.-C.) ; Abd al-Rahman II (r. 207-238 H / 822-852 J.-C.) ; Muhammad Ier (r. 237-272 H / 852-886 J.-C.) ; al-Mundir (r. 272-274 H / 886-888 J.-C.) ; Abd Allah (r. 274-299 H / 888-912 J -C.) ; Abd al-Rahman III (r. 299-350 H / 912-961 J.-C.) ; al-Hakam II (r. 350-366 H / 961-976 J.-C.) ; Abi Amir al-Mansour (r. 367-392 H / 978-1002 J.-C.).
history: Le 29 juin 1236 (19 *chawwal* de l'an 633 H), la ville de Cordoue est conquise par Ferdinand III le Saint. La même année, la Grande Mosquée est purifiée et consacrée comme église chrétienne. C'est à partir du Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.) que débutent à l'intérieur de la mosquée les travaux de la cathédrale Santa María qui se dresse actuellement au centre de la salle de prière.

de.name: Fresken und Stuck
description: Die hochbarocke Ausstattung mit Stuck und Fresken hat den ursprünglich konzipierten Raumeindruck deutlich verändert. Im Gewölbe wurden die Jochgrenzen durch den übergreifenden Stuck in kräftigen floralen und figürlichen Formen zum Teil verschliffen, und die Einführung der buntfarbigen Deckenbilder in 37 (davon sieben 1944 zerstört) Feldern kontrastiert deutlich mit der frühbarocken Farbigkeit aus Weiß, Gold und Schwarz. Die himmlische Zone des Gewölbes wird vom Stuck durch Putten, üppige Fruchtgirlanden und Akanthusranken ausgezeichnet, das Bildprogramm beinhaltet u. a. Szenen aus dem Leben Mariae (Chor) und der Kirchenpatrone (Langhaus).

en.name: Frescos and stucco
description: The High Baroque interior work significantly changed the original spatial impression. In the vault the bay borders were masked with overlapping stucco and the introduction of colourful ceiling pictures in small panels provided a contrast to the Early Baroque colour scheme of white, gold and black. The vault’s heavenly zone is characterised by stucco putti, garlands of fruit and acanthus vine, the series of pictures depict, amongst other things, scenes from the life of the Virgin Mary (choir) and the Church patrons (nave).

description: كان دارا شيخو الابن المفضل وولي العهد للإمبراطور المغولي شاه جهان (حكم خلال 1627- 58 ) .ولكن دارا لم يعتلي قط العرش حيث أنه في عام 1659 قتل خلال حرب على العرش التي نشبت عندما مرض والده في عام 1657. وكلا الرجلين كانا يرتديان الكثير من المجوهرات وبشكل أساسي يضعان اللؤلؤ والزمرد والياقوت. وشاه جهان بلحيته التي يداخلها الشيب جزئيا ويرتدي سترة ذات ياقة من الفرو يقدم ياقوتة كبيرة ( أو حجر البلخش ) لدارا . والملائكة المصورين بطراز أوربي ويرفرفون بأجنحتهم في الأعلى يرمزون للعظمة الإمبراطورية بينما الكرة التي يقف عليها الوالد وابنه تشير لمكانة شاه جهان المعتبر كملك للعالم ( التي هي الترجمة الإنجليزية للقب شاه جهان).

en.name: Shah Jahan and Dara Shikoh
description: Dara Shikoh was the favourite son and designated heir of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan (r. 1627–58). However, Dara never acceded to the throne, for in 1659 he was killed during the war of succession that ensued when his father fell ill in 1657. Both men are heavily bejewelled, wearing mainly pearls, emeralds and rubies. Shah Jahan, with a partially greyed beard and wearing a fur-collared jacket, offers a large ruby (or spinel) to Dara. The European-style angels hovering above symbolize imperial majesty, while the globe on which father and son stand more precisely denotes Shah Jahan’s perceived status as King of the World (which is the English translation of the title ‘Shah Jahan’).
keywords: portrait; portraiture; jewel; jewellery; symbolism; allegory; textile; royal; border decoration; arabesque; miniature painting; floral decoration; angel; arms
materials: Coloured pigments and gold on paper

en.name: In Tunis, the families of the Italian men drafted for the war waiting to get their daily allowance from the Italian government
names: *Sussidi governativi. Il pagamento del soccorso giornaliero alle famiglie dei richiamati*
short_description: According to a booklet published in 1917 by the Tunisian branch of the Dante Alighieri Society and quoted by historian Adriano Salmieri (see his contribution to the volume *Mestieri e professioni degli italiani di Tunisia* – *Métiers et professions des Italiens de Tunisie, a cura di S. Finzi, Tunisi: Finzi*, 2003), by the end of April 1917 11,146 Italians in Tunisia had been drafted for the war, and 700 had died. According to the same source, in 1917 in Tunisia the Italian government was paying daily allowances to almost 5,000 destitute families of drafted soldiers.

en.name: Henry Salt’s 1817 excavations at the Pyramids and Sphinx
short_description: On his arrival in Egypt, Salt sponsored and recorded the excavations of Captain Giovanni Battista Caviglia at the Giza pyramids and Sphinx. Caviglia discovered new chambers in the Great Pyramid and a lost chapel beneath the head of the Sphinx.
keywords: archaeology; exploration; Egyptomania; travel; traveller; collection; collector; museums

en.name: *Woman with a Branch of Dates*
description:
Faiq Hassan was among the pioneering artists in Iraq who obtained formal art education and was awarded a government scholarship to pursue studies in Paris. In AH 1356 / AD 1938, he assumed the directorship of the recently established *Ma’had al-Funun al-Jamila fi Baghdad* (Institute of Fine Arts in Baghdad), a role he held until AH 1382 / AD 1962.  
Hassan belonged to the cohort of *'al-Ruwwad'* (the Pioneers), a group of painters that integrated elements of everyday Iraqi life into their artwork and defied conventional studio methods. He followed the artistic principle of istilham al-turath, which focused on taking inspiration from heritage. This principle was developed by *Jama'at Baghdad lil-Fann al-Hadith* (Baghdad Group for Modern Art), which was founded in AH 1370 / AD 1951.  
  
'A Woman with a Branch of Dates' shows an Iraqi woman wearing a black traditional garment and holding a basket of dates , before an abstract, flattened village background. Hassan preferred to depict everyday life in rural areas. He merged the artistic traditions of ancient Mesopotamia with modernism to cultivate an awareness of Iraqi national identity.
holder: MATHAF, Arab Museum of Modern Art
keywords: woman; dates; water

cs.name: Sv. Kopeček
description: Jedním z protireformačních podniků kardinála byla stavba kostela sv. Šebestiána na Tanzberku. Poutní kostel a 13 kaplí křížové cesty přeměnily pohanskými pověstmi opředený skalnatý vrch podle vzoru v severoitalském Varallu na “Svatou horu”. Původní kostel (G. G. Tencalla) vyhořel r. 1663 a byl opraven v 18. a 19. století.

en.name: Svatý Kopeček (Holy Hill)
description: Part of Cardinal Dietrichstein’s Counter-Reformation strategy was the construction of the Church of St. Sebastian on Tanzberg Hill. This pilgrimage church, with 13 chapels of the Stations of the Cross, was intended to turn a rocky hill, redolent with pagan legend, into a “Holy Mount” modelled on Varallo in northern Italy. The original church (G. G. Tencalla) was re-established after 1663 and in 18th and 19th centuries.

de.name: Kirche (Architektur und Innenraum)
description:
Barock begann in Rein mit der Barockisierung des Turms, der Teil der romanischen Kirche war. Architektonisch war er niemals ein Turm, da Zisterzienser nur Dachreiter haben durften. Er ist auf zwei Mauern des Hauptschiffs aufgesetzt und hat keinen Unterbau. Im Frühbarock wurde die Winterkirche mit reicher Stuckdekoration der Kirche angegliedert, mit deren Barockisierung man sechzig Jahre später begann. Der Architekt Johann Georg Stengg wurde mit der Planung und dem Bau beauftragt.  
Die vor- und zurückschwingende Fassade war wie etliche dieser Epoche von Francesco Borrominis Kirche San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane in Rom beeinflusst. Sie ist in vertikaler Richtung mit Statuen, mächtigen Säulen, stark vortretenden Kapitellen und feinen Stuckrahmen dekoriert. Horizontal ist die Fassade in eine eingeschoßige Sockelzone und einen zweiten Abschnitt von Säulen gegliedert, die über eineinhalb Geschoße reichen. Diese Zone wird durch einen gebogten Architrav von der (dritten) Attikazone mit dem vorspringenden, sogenannten Hornwerk getrennt. Es sieht wie die Pfeifen einer Orgel aus, spielte aber nur einen Akkord.  
Wenn man den Kirchenraum betritt, ist man in der dunklen romanischen Eingangshalle, dem früheren Altarraum, über dem sich die barocke Orgelempore befindet. Beide öffnen sich dem weiten und hellen Kirchenschiff und dem Presbyterium, die vollständig mit Fresken von Joseph Adam von Mölck bedeckt sind. Die illusionistische Architekturmalerei hat ihren Ursprung in Andra *Pozzos Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum*, einem Anleitungsbuch für Maler. Der Hochaltar mit Säulen und Statuen füllt die Breite des Chorraums aus. Das Altarbild, eine Anbetung der Hirten, war ursprünglich für eine andere Kirche bestimmt. 1819 kam es an die Stelle des originalen Gemäldes, das die Himmelfahrt Mariens darstellt.
dates: 1650 wurde der mittelalterliche Turm (über dem südlichen/linken Teil der Kirche) durch einen frühbarocken ersetzt; 1682 Stuckdekoration in der Alten Sakristei (Winterkapelle); 1739 – 1747 Bau/Umbau und Barockisierung der Kirche; 1742 – 1747 Kirchenfassade
place: Im Nordwesten der Klosteranlage, die Hauptfassade der Kirche ist in den großen Hof gerichtet.
artist: Architektur: Fassade, Barockisierung des Turms und der gotischen Kirche: Johann Georg Stengg; Statuen an der Fassade: Johann Matthias Leitner Innenraum: Fresken an den Wänden und an der Decke: Joseph Adam von Mölck; Gemälde Hochaltar: Martin Johann Schmidt; Statuten am Hochaltar: Jakob Payer Marienkapelle (ehemalige Sakristei, Winterkirche): Stuckdekoration: Alexander Serenio zugeschrieben

en.name: Church (architecture and interior)
description:
Baroque started in Rein with the baroquization of the tower, then part of the Romanesque church. Architectonically it was never a tower itself as Cistercians were only allowed to have roof turrets. It is superimposed upon two naves’ walls and has no substructure. During the early Baroque era the winter church with rich stucco decoration was attached to the church whose baroquization started sixty years later. Architect Johann Georg Stengg was commissioned with the planning and the building. The forth- and back-swinging façade was like many others in this epoch influenced by Francesco Borromini´s church San Carlo alle Quattro Fontane in Rome. It is vertically decorated with statues, mighty columns, strongly protruding capitals and delicate stucco frames. Horizontally the façade is structured in a pedestal zone and a one and a half column storey. This zone is separated by a curved architrave from the (third) Attica zone with the protruding so-called hornwork. It looks like the pipes of an organ but reproduced only one chord.  
Going inside the church one is in the dark Romanesque entrance hall, the former sanctuary, with the baroque organ gallery above it. Both open to the wide and bright nave and presbytery, completely covered with fresco paintings by Joseph Adam von Mölck. The illusionistic architecture has its origin in Andrea Pozzo´s *Perspectiva pictorum et architectorum,* an instruction manual for painters. The high altar with columns and statues fills the width of the choir. The painting, an adoration of the shepherds, was originally made for another church. In 1819 it replaced the original painting representing the Assumption of the Holy Virgin.
dates: 1650: replacing the Medieval tower (above the Southern/left part of the church) with an early baroque one; 1682: stucco decoration in the Old Sacristy (winter chapel); 1739–47: church building, structural changes and baroquization; 1742–47: church´s façad
place: In the Northwest of the monastery complex, the church's main façade is in the great court.
artist: Architecture: façade, baroquization of the tower and of the Gothic church: Johann Georg Stengg; statues at the façade: Johann Matthias Leitner Interior: walls´ and ceiling´s fresco paintings: Joseph Adam von Mölck; painting at the high altar: Martin Johann Schmidt; statutes at the high altar: Jakob Payer Marienkapelle/Lady Chapel (former sacristy, winter church): stucco decoration: attributed to Alexander Serenio

en.name: Wedding portrait of King Aleksandar and Queen Draga of Serbia
description: At the end of the 19th and during the first decade of the 20th century Pirot kilims served as unavoidable decor in public buildings and in important public manifestations. An official wedding photo of King Alexander Obrenović of Serbia and Queen Draga, shows a royal couple standing on the Pirot kilims, used as floor coverings in this solemn occasion as distinguished national products. The official photograph, taken on 4 August 1900 by the court photographer Milan Jovanović, was issued on a poster by the bookstore of Sreten J. Djordjević and printed by the State Printing House of the Kingdom of Serbia.
keywords: Pirot; Şarköy; kilim; Obrenović dynasty; poster

en.name: The first postmaster's office in Tunis, 1892
short_description: The objects assembled in this room all date to the late 19th century and belong to a set of urban Tunisian furnishings. These articles were all part of Tunis' first municipal postmaster's office. They consist of four chairs and a bench in painted wood, centred around a two-layered desk, painted in a floral motif on a pale blue background. Behind, a shelving unit, painted in the same style. This furnishing set shows evidence of traditional Tunisian, Turkish and various European influences.
holder: Musée des Postes, Télégraphes et Télécommunications
keywords: Painted wood; floral decoration; Turkish influences; European influences
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Premier bureau du receveur de la poste de Tunis 1892
short_description: Les objets rassemblés dans cette salle et qui datent de la fin du XIXe siècle appartiennent au mobilier tunisien citadin. Objets témoins du bureau du premier receveur municipal de la ville de Tunis (1892), un banc et quatre chaises en bois peint avec au milieu une table à double plateau décorée de bouquets de fleurs sur un fond bleu clair ; au-dessus, des étagères en bois sculptées et peintes également avec une décoration florale. Les origines de ce mobilier et les influences qu’il recèle sont diverses : tunisoises traditionnelles, turques et européennes.
holder: Musée des Postes, Télégraphes et Télécommunications
keywords: Bois peint; Décoration florale; Influence turques; Influence européenne
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

ar.name: قطعة من شال
description: القطعة باللون الأسود – الأزرق من شال وهي مزينة بعصابات تشكيل المستخدمة في السجاد المنسوجة بنقوش من الخط الكوفي وأشكال أشخاص ذات طراز عالي المستوي ورباعيات القوائم وطيور. والطراز الكلي يذكّر بالأقمشة القبطية ولكنها مميزة لمنطقة الفيوم في مصر العليا والذي يؤكده الكتاب المسلمون بأنها منطقة متخصصة في نسج الأقمشة المصنوعة من الصوف.

el.name: Απότμημα περιωμίου
description: Αυτό το βαθυκύανο τμήμα εσάρπας κοσμείται με επάλληλες ταινίες που φέρουν κουφικές επιγραφές, σχηματικές  ανθρώπινες μορφές, τετράποδα και πουλιά. Η έντονη σχηματοποίηση θυμίζει τα κοπτικά υφάσματα αλλά είναι τυπική της περιοχής του Φαγιούμ στην Άνω Αίγυπτο, στην οποία υπήρχαν, σύμφωνα με τη μαρτυρία μουσουλμάνων  συγγραφέων εξειδικευμένα εργαστήρια μάλλινων υφασμάτων.

en.name: Fragment of a shawl
description: This black-blue fragment of shawl is decorated with tapestry bands woven with *kufic* inscriptions and highly stylized human figures, quadrupeds and birds. The overall stylization is reminiscent of Coptic textiles but is typical of the Fayyum area in Upper Egypt, which is attested by Muslim writers as specializing in the weaving of woollen fabrics.
keywords: Shawl; Fragment; Kufic; Wool; textile; costume; Fatimid textiles; Coptic; animal decoration; bird; human representation

en.name: Prayer rug
description: A lamp stands out against the indigo field of the prayer niche (*mihrab*) shown on this high-pile rug. Featuring a foliated scroll pattern, the olive-green spandrel is supported by two columns. Carnations decorate the upper level of the niche. A series of rosettes and palmettes interspersed with arabesques covers the ivory ground of the main border. This rug, which has 4,200 symmetrical knots per square decimetre, was made in Turkey during the first quarter of the 20th century. Positioned facing Mecca, the rug ensures the purity of the place of worship and creates a separate space for praying. Long ago, Muslims kneeled down and prostrated themselves on palm-frond mats or sheepskins. The field of a prayer rug usually shows a stylized representation of a *mihrab*, a niche made in the wall of a mosque indicating the direction of Mecca, towards which the faithful turn to pray.
keywords: Prayer rug; Ottoman textile; Islamic textile
partner: The Montreal Museum of Fine Arts

fr.name: Tapis de prière
description: Une lampe se découpe sur le champ indigo de la niche de prière (mihrab) représentée sur ce tapis de haute laine. Le tympan vert olive à motif de rinceaux est soutenu par deux colonnes. Des œillets ornent le registre supérieur de la niche. Une succession de rosettes et des palmettes ponctuées d’arabesques habille le fond ivoire de la bordure principale. Le tapis, qui compte 4200 nœuds symétriques au décimètre carré, a été fabriquée en Turquie dans le premier quart du XXe siècle. Orienté vers La Mecque, le tapis assure la pureté du lieu de culte et crée un espace isolé pour prier. Jadis, les musulmans s’agenouillaient et se prosternaient sur des nattes de palmier ou des peaux de mouton. Le champ du tapis de prière présente généralement une représentation stylisée du mihrab : niche creusée dans le mur d’une mosquée indiquant la direction de La Mecque, vers laquelle le fidèle se tourne pour prier.
dates: Fin XIXe s. ou début XXe s.
keywords: Tapis de prière; textile ottoman; textile islamique

en.name: *The Art of the Saracens in Egypt*
short_description: A publication on the history of the arts in Egypt by Stanley Lane-Poole (1854-1931). Each chapter is dedicated to one aspect of the arts: architecture, stone and plaster, mosaic, woodwork, ivory, metalwork, glass, heraldry, ceramics, textiles and illuminated manuscripts.
keywords: Book; Egypt; collecting

ar.name: جرة كبيرة بزخرفة بارزة.
description:
الجرة بيضوية الشكل، لها ثلاثة مقابض، مغطاة بطبقة سميكة من الزجاج الأخضر القاتم المعروف في صناعة الخزف في عصر الساسانيين.  
الزخرفة الرئيسية مركزة في مجموعة من الدوائر المتداخلة البارزة والمنتهية في مركز الرسم المبسط الذي يمثل(عنقود عنب)، ينتمي إلى تقاليد رمزية واسعة الانتشار. نجد تحت الفوهة زخرفة هندسية بارزة على شكل معينات صغيرة، وعلى جسم الجرة في القسم السفلي زخرفة على شكل زوايا حادة متلاحقة. هذا الأنموذج في الشكل والزخرفة والتنفيذ يدل على بقاء نوع هذا الفن من أواخر العصر الساساني إلى ظهور العصر الإسلامي. كانت هذه الجرار تستخدم لحفظ المواد الغذائية.
كانت هذه الجرة التي يمكن أن نتعرف، من خلال الشكل والزخرف وتقنية الصنع، على نماذج ساسانية تستعمل دون شك لحفظ  مواد غذائية.
holder: متحف الحضارات  | متحف الفن الشرقي جوزيبي توتشي
keywords: خزف؛ زخرفة هندسية.
partner: متحف الحضارات  | متحف الفن الشرقي جوزيبي توتشي

en.name: Large jar with relief decoration.
description:
The egg-shaped jar, with three small handles, is covered entirely with a heavy dark-green glaze, which is common in Sassanid ceramic production.  
The decoration is based on a series of concentric circles in relief finished off in the middle with a motif of a stylised bunch of grapes, which is related to a widespread tradition of symbolic figures. Below the brim there is a geometric motif in relief made up of small rhombuses, and the lower part of the body is decorated with apex motifs.  
The shape, decoration and technique used in the piece are evidence of the stylistic continuity between the late Sassanid and the early Islamic periods. The jar was probably intended to store foodstuffs.
Sassanid influences are clearly recognisable in the shape, decoration and production technique of this jar, which was probably used to store foodstuffs.
holder: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art “Giuseppe Tucci”
keywords: ceramic; geometric decoration
partner: Museum of Civilisations | Museum of Oriental Art

es.name: Orza con decoración en relieve.
description:
Esta orza ovalada está provista de tres pequeñas asas y toda su superficie aparece recubierta por un grueso vidriado verde oscuro, habitual en la producción cerámica de época sasánida. La decoración principal consiste en una serie de círculos concéntricos en relieve que terminan en el centro, en un motivo estilizado en forma de racimo de uvas que se remonta a una tradición de figuraciones simbólicas ampliamente extendida. Por debajo del borde aparece un motivo geométrico en relieve formado por pequeños rombos, mientras que la parte inferior del cuerpo presenta una decoración con motivos puntiagudos.  
Por su forma, su decoración y la técnica de fabricación, la pieza ejemplifica la continuidad estilística entre el periodo sasánida tardío y el protoislámico. Probablemente estaba destinada a contener y conservar alimentos.
Esta orza, en la que se reconocen modelos sasánidas tanto en la forma como en la decoración y la técnica de fabricación, debía de utilizarse para conservar alimentos.
holder: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”
dates: Siglo II de la Hégira / VIII d. C.
keywords: cerámica; decoración geométrica
partner: Museo de Civilizaciones | Museo de Arte Oriental

fr.name: Grande jarre avec décor en relief.
description:
Cette jarre, de forme ovoïde, pourvue de trois petites anses, est recouverte sur toute sa surface d'un épaisse glaçure vert foncé, comme c'est le plus souvent le cas dans la production de céramique d'époque sassanide.  
Le décor principal s'organise autour d'une série de cercles concentriques en relief, qui se terminent au centre par un motif stylisé en forme de grappe de raisin ; ce motif se rattache à une tradition de représentations symboliques largement répandues. Sous le bord court un motif géométrique en relief formé de petits losanges ; dans la partie inférieure de la jarre, on note un décor à motifs de hampes.  
Par sa forme, son décor et sa technique d'exécution, cette pièce illustre la continuité stylistique qui relie la période sassanide tardive et la période proto-islamique. Cette jarre était probablement destinée à conserver des denrées alimentaires.

Cette jarre, dans laquelle on peut reconnaître, au niveau de la forme, du décor et de la technique d'exécution, des modèles sassanides, devait sans doute être utilisée pour conserver des denrées alimentaires.
holder: Musée des civilisations | Musée d'art oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”
dates: IIe siècle de l’Hégire (VIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: céramique ; décor géométrique
partner: Musée des civilisations | Musée d'art oriental “Giuseppe Tucci”

it.name: Grande giara con decorazione in rilievo.
description: La giara di forma ovoidale, provvista di tre piccole anse, è ricoperta su tutta la superficie da una pesante invetriatura verde scura, come è consuetudine nella produzione ceramica di epoca sasanide. La decorazione principale è articolata in una serie di circoli concentrici in rilievo terminanti al centro in un motivo stilizzato a “grappolo d'uva”, che si ricollega ad una tradizione di figurazioni simboliche largamente diffuse. Al di sotto dell'orlo corre un motivo geometrico a rilievo formato da piccoli rombi, mentre nella parte inferiore del corpo è presente un decoro a motivi apicati. L'esemplare testimonia nella forma, nella decorazione e nella tecnica di esecuzione, la continuità stilistica che lega il periodo tardo sasanide a quello protoislamico. La giara era probabilmente destinata a contenere e conservare derrate alimentari.
La giara, nella quale sono riconoscibili nella forma, nella decorazione e nella tecnica di esecuzione modelli sasanidi, doveva essere utilizzata probabilmente per conservare derrate alimentari.
holder: Museo delle Civiltà | Museo d’arte orientale “Giuseppe Tucci”
keywords: ceramica; decorazione geometrica
partner: Museo delle Civiltà | Museo d’arte orientale “Giuseppe Tucci”

de.name: Altar der Hl. Sippe
description: Der Altar der Hl. Sippe verweist mit seinem Altarblatt auf das bayerische Herrscherhaus und die Zukunft des christlichen Bayerns. Das Bildthema zusammen mit den Heiligenfiguren des Altares und dessen Vorstellbild mit der Verkündigung Mariens sind im Hinblick auf die Geburt des Erbprinzen interpretierbar und nehmen damit erneut die Votivthematik auf, die ehemals auch das zerstörte Hochaltarblatt zeigte.

en.name: Altar of the Holy Kinship
description: The Altar of the Holy Family (or more broadly the Holy Kinship), with its altarpiece, is a reference to the Bavarian dynasty and the future of Christian Bavaria. The theme of the Annunciation of the Virgin is carried through in the imagery of the altar; the painting, the figures of saints either side, and the predella panel at the bottom. The altar can be seen therefore to indicate the birth of the Crown Prince and reiterate the dedicational background of the church. At one time the altarpiece in the choir (now destroyed) also picked up on this votive purpose.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

ar.name: مكحلة.
description:
تتكون القطعة من بدن عاجي أجوف منشوري الشكل ذي مقطع سداسي، ويوجد في طرفي البدن شكلان زخرفيان اتخذ أحدهما شكل زهرة بادئة بالتفتح. ويزخرف كل وجه من أوجه بدن القطعة الستة المتساوية ست وريدات يتكون كل منها من ست بتلات. ويفصل كل وريدة عن التي تليها مثلثان متقابلا الرأسين. ويفصل بين الوجه والآخر للقطعة شريط زخرفي رفيع.  
  
استخدمت القطعة كغيرها من المكاحل لوضع الكحل في العين. وقد استخدم الكحل لتجميل العيون ولمعالجتها، وكان يطلق على من يعالج العيون " كحّال ." وقد شاع استعمال الكحل في مصر منذ العصر الفرعوني، وكان يصنع من خامات النحاس والرصاص ومن حرق نبات العصفر. أما المكاحل، فقد صنعت من النحاس والفضة والزجاج إلى جانب العاج. وقد عثر في كثير من الحفريات في مدينة الفسطاط على أعداد كبيرة من المكاحل الزجاجية التي تحتوي على بقايا من الكحل.

اهتمت المرأة في العصر الإسلامي بزينتها، وبالتالي اهتمت بأدوات تلك الزينة، مثل تلك المكحلة التي وضعت فيها الكحل، سواء أكان للعلاج، أو تجميل عينيها. وقد تنوَّعت أشكال وخامات هذه المكاحل، فمنها ما صُنع من العاج أو النحاس أو الفضة أو الزجاج، وكان الكحل يستخرج من النحاس والرصاص واحتراق نبات العصفر.
keywords: عاج؛ كحل؛ مكحلة ؛ نلّ؛ نيلو؛ تجميل

en.name: Kohl Container.
description:
A kohl container that is composed of a stretched hollow ivory prism-like body, comprising a hexagonal cross-section divided into six planes. At both ends of the body are two decorative forms, one of which is in the shape of a flower on the brink of unfurling. Each face of the six identical sides is decorated with six rosettes, each of which is made up of six petals. Each of the rosettes is separated from its neighbour by two triangular shapes which conjoin at their tips. Each plane in turn is separated from the other, by a thin decorated band.  
This container was used as other kohl vials were during the period to put kohl in to the eyes in order to beautify them as well as to medically treat them. In fact the title of *kahhal* (eye doctor) was given to those who specialised in treating eyes. The use of kohl was widespread in Egypt from the Pharonic period onwards, and was made from raw copper, lead and from burning the saffron plant. Kohl vials were made from copper, silver and glass in addition to ivory.

Muslim women paid great attention to their appearance and tools like this kohl container were used for beautification or health of the eyes. Kohl containers were made in a variety of forms and materials such as brass, silver, and glass. The kohl itself was prepared from copper, lead and burnt saffron plant.
keywords: Ivory; kohl; container; niello; cosmetic

es.name: Frasco de kohl.
description:
Frasco de kohl con cuerpo hueco y alargado de marfil en forma de prisma de sección hexagonal. En los extremos del cuerpo hay dos adornos, uno de los cuales representa una flor a punto de abrirse. Las seis caras del hexágono están decoradas con seis rosetones formados por seis pétalos cada uno. Los rosetones están separados entre sí por dos formas triangulares que se tocan por el vértice. Como separación entre las caras también hay una fina banda decorada.  
Este recipiente se utilizaba, al igual que otros frascos de kohl de este mismo periodo, para aplicar el producto en los ojos con fines cosméticos o médicos. De hecho, el título de *kahhal* (oftalmólogo) se otorgaba a los especialistas en el tratamiento de los ojos. El uso del kolh se extendió en Egipto a partir del periodo faraónico. Se elaboraba con cobre en bruto, plomo y el resultado de quemar la planta del azafrán. Los recipientes de kohl estaban fabricados con cobre, plata y vidrio, además de marfil.

Las mujeres musulmanas cuidaban mucho su aspecto, así como los utensilios cosméticos que usaban para embellecerse los ojos, como este recipiente de kohl. Estos frascos se fabricaban en formas y materiales como el cobre, la plata o el vidrio. El kohl se hacía con cobre, plomo y alazor tostado.
dates: Siglos VIII-IX de la Hégira / siglos XIV-XV d. C.
keywords: Marfil; kohl; recipiente/frasco de kohl; niel; cosmetico

fr.name: Fiole à khôl.
description:
Fiole à khôl composée d'un corps creux allongé en ivoire de section hexagonale, aux deux extrémités duquel figurent deux ornements, l'un d'eux représentant une fleur sur le point d'éclore. Chaque pan des six côtés identiques est décoré de six rosettes composées chacune de six pétales, et séparées les unes des autres par deux éléments triangulaires venant reposer en haut et en bas sur un fin bandeau décoré séparant les pans les uns des autres.  
Ce type de fiole, qui pouvait également être en cuivre, en argent ou en verre, servait à la conservation du khôl, un fard de maquillage des yeux qui présentait également des vertus curatives. En fait, le titre de *kahhal* (médecin des yeux) était donné à ceux qui se spécialisaient dans le traitement des yeux. L'utilisation du khôl, un composé de cuivre pur, de plomb et de cendre de safran, était répandue en égypte depuis la période des pharaons.

Les femmes musulmanes portaient une grande attention à leur apparence et des ustensiles comme cette fiole à khôl étaient utilisés pour l'embellissement ou le soin des yeux. Les fioles à khôl étaient fabriquées dans une diversité de formes et de matières comme le cuivre, l'argent et le verre. Le khôl lui-même était préparé à partir du cuivre, du plomb et de la plante de safran brûlée.
dates: VIIIe-IXe siècle de l’Hégire (XIVe-XVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Ivoire ; fiole; khôl ; nielle; cosmétique

en.name: The 1861 constitution
short_description: Despite the promulgation of the fundamental pact, the new reforms did not, in practice, take effect. The French and English consuls therefore continued to remind the Tunisian sovereign of the importance of judiciary reform in particular and offered to create a senate to assist him in this. Mohamed Bey's successor, Sadok Bey, promised to complete his predecessor's work and create a deliberative assembly. On 1 July 1860, the completion of the new reforms was announced. On 17 September 1860 in Algiers, the bey solemnly handed Napoléon III a copy of the richly bound text. Proclaimed in January 1861, the constitution was put to effect the following 23 April.
keywords: Reform movement; Tanzimat
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: La constitution de 1861
short_description: Malgré la promulgation du Pacte fondamental, la rédaction des codes n’avançait pas et les consuls anglais et français rappelaient au souverain tunisien la nécessité de réformes judiciaires. Et lui proposèrent la création d’un Sénat pour l’assister. Le successeur de Mohamed Bey, Sadok, promettait l’œuvre entreprise par son prédécesseur et de créer une assemblée délibérante. Le 1er juillet 1860, on annonça que la rédaction était enfin terminée. Le 17 septembre 1860 à Alger, le bey remettait solennellement à Napoléon III un exemplaire du texte richement relié. Proclamée en janvier 1861, la constitution était mise en vigueur le 23 avril suivant.
keywords: Mouvement réformateur; Tanzimat
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

ar.name: جرة خزين.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن جرة خزين خزفية رمادية اللون ذات شكل جميل. زخرف بدن الجرة المضلع بخطوط هندسية مفردة ومتعددة. يبدو أن هذه الزخرفة نفذت قبل شي الجرة. ويبدو من الزخرفة هذه أن الجرة كانت من الأشياء الثمينة. للجرة عنق مثلث الشكل، ومقبضان كل منهما على شكل حلقة. وقاعدتها دائرية الشكل عُثر عليها مكسورة ولكن تم ترميمها.  
  
صنعت الجرة من جزأين منفصلين تم وصلهما معاً بواسطة الضغط، إذ يمكن رؤية قطعة إضافية على شكل قناة بين عنق الجرة وبدنها.
جرّة تخزين صغيرة من مزرعة أم قيس، ذات نمط هندسي مرسوم قبل الشَّيْ. كانت مؤلفة من جزأين موصولين عند الحافة، بين الكتف والجسم. من شأن المبالغة في الزخرفة أن تكون قد جعلتها حاجة ثمينة.
dates: النصف الثاني من القرن الأول الهجري/ النصف الثاني من القرن السابع ميلادي.
keywords: خزف؛ سبيل الحوريات؛ فخار؛ مواد رفاهية.

en.name: Storage jar.
description:
A small, dark-gray storage jar of beautiful form, with a ribbed body and linear geometric pattern, painted with a single and a multiple-headed brush prior to firing, which covers the entire vessel. The extent of decoration on this jar means that it was probably a costly item.  
  
The jar has a triangular rim, two loop handles and a round umbilical base. It was made of two parts joined by pressing the clay together, as there is a flange between the shoulder and the ribbed body. The jar was broken into pieces when recovered and has been subsequently mended.

A small storage jar from the nymphaeum at Umm Qays with a geometric pattern painted before firing. It was made of two parts, joined at the flange between the shoulder and body. The extent of decoration probably made it a costly item.
dates: Hegira, second half of the 1st century / AD 2nd half of the 7th century.
keywords: Luxury ware; nymphaeum; pottery.

es.name: Tinaja
description:
Hermosa tinaja color gris oscuro de tamaño pequeño, de cuerpo con canaladuras horizontales y decorada con diseños geométricos que abarcan toda la superficie y que fueron pintados con un pincel de varias cabezas antes de la cocción. Esta abundante decoración indica que probablemente fue un artículo caro.  
Tiene borde triangular, dos asas con forma de aro y base redondeada. Consta de dos partes que se unieron presionando la arcilla, prueba de ello es el cerco que se aprecia entre la parte superior y la panza. Cuando se encontró, la tinaja estaba rota en varias piezas y hubo que recomponerla.

Pequeña tinaja de los jardines de Umm Qays, con motivos geométricos pintados antes de cocerla. Se fabricó en dos partes, unidas a la altura del reborde entre la panza y los hombros de la vasija. Su profusa decoración indica que debió de ser un artículo caro.
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo I de la Hégira / segunda mitad del siglo VII d. C.
keywords: Objetos de lujo; jardín de recreo; cerámica.

fr.name: Jarre.
description:
Petite jarre de couleur gris foncé. De forme superbe, elle est ornée de motifs géométriques linéaires et a été uniformément peinte à l'aide d'une brosse à plusieurs têtes avant cuisson.  
Sa panse nervurée se termine par une ouverture triangulaire. Elle présente un fond arrondi et deux poignées en boucle. Le bourrelet entre l'épaule et la panse montre qu'elle est constituée de deux parties réunies par pression. Brisée lors de sa découverte, elle a été réparée.

Une petite jarre du nymphée d’Oum Qays ornée de motifs géométriques avant sa cuisson. Elle était constituée de deux parties, réunies par pression entre l’épaule et la panse. L’étendue de sa décoration en faisait probablement un ustensile coûteux.
dates: Seconde moitié du Ier siècle de l’Hégire (seconde moitié du VIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: marchandises de luxe ; nymphée ; poterie

en.name: Powder box
description: A powder box – a receptacle for gunpowder – decorated with geometric and floral motifs and crafted in southern Morocco in the 19th century. The decorative style is influenced by European designs, seen particularly in the suspension loops.
type: Fittings; metalwork; arms and armour; munitions
keywords: Metalwork; copper; European influence; geometric motifs; geometric decoration; floral decoration; vegetal motifs; vegeta ldecoration; applied arts; craftsmanship; traditional craftsmanship; weapons; war; warfare; military objects; Moroccan craftsmen
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate for Cultural Heritage

en.name: Bright red sun cruelly hot but the wind is of autumn
*Ships in a Harbour*
description: A finely executed Baroque painting of a harbour with ships and throngs of people on the shore. The composition is a rare example of a small size genre piece, which may have been part of a series. The execution of the painting is finely detailed, and contrary to its small size, the work is of high quality. This is an unusual representation within the iconography of this type of picture. Scenes of everyday life became common in the 17th and 18th centuries, and depictions of the “low-life” of peasants and the “high-life” of the aristocracy, featuring fashionably dressed figures in different scenes were also common. The popularity of seascapes and maritime pictures spread to Hungary by way of Flemish and Dutch painting. Small seascapes (*zeekens*) were a very popular theme representing – like this painting – imaginary views of exotic ports.

A finely executed Baroque genre painting of a harbour with ships and throngs of people on the shore. Because of these and other features, the painting represents a rare example among Baroque seascapes.
keywords: Oil painting; genre painting; Zichy family

en.name: Double niche ‘Transylvanian’ rug
description: The term “Transylvanian” rug designates 17th- and 18th-century rugs preserved in Transylvanian Saxon churches, which, once considered being of Transylvanian origin, were in fact made in western Anatolia. Some have a *mihrab* design, typical of prayer rugs, while others feature two opposing arches. Here, the red ground of this double niche is decorated with stylised floral motifs connected by geometric scrolls. A mosque lamp is featured at one end of the central field. Scalloped edge cartouches on ivory-white ground decorate the main border. At an early stage, the bright colours of this surprisingly well-preserved rug raised doubts about its authenticity. Still, a few other carpets from Transylvanian churches display a similarly vivid colour range; at the same time, over the past 100 years (ever since it was sent to Moscow in 1916) the rug has only been exhibited once, in 1994, which explains its excellent state of conservation.
holder: The National Museum of Art of Romania
keywords: Transylvanian rug
partner: The National Museum of Art of Romania

ar.name: حكام السلالة الحاكمة المغولية من بابور إلى أورانجذب مع سلفهم تيمور  منسوبة  لبهواني داس
description: يشغل تيمور مركز الوسط  في هذه البورتريه الجماعية. ومن الأمام واليسار هناك الأباطرة شاه جهان ، أكبر وبابور مع أبو سعيد حاكم  سمرقند وابن تيمور ميرانشاه. وإلى اليمين هناك الأباطرة أورانجذب ، جانجير وهومايون واثنين من أولاد تيمور الآخرين هما عمر شيخ ومحمد سلطان. والشخوص قد تم تعريفهم بعبارات مكتوبة بالذهب. ومكان اللوحة هو شرفة تطل على الحديقة ذات أشجار السرو. ويركع أشخاص على سجادة مزهرة بشكل غني عليها أشياء ثمينة تضمن مبخرتين غير عاديتين وطاولة مطلية بالمينا مع زهرتين من البورسلين الصيني. والتفاصيل في الرسم دقيقة جدا بحيث يمكن مشاهدة الدخان المنبعث من المبخرتين.بالرغم من أن التشكيل يجب أن يؤرخ من بداية حكم أورانجذب فإن طراز اللوحة يقول بأن تاريخها هو القرن الثامن عشر وأنها رسمت من قبل بهواني داس. وتوقيعه يظهر على الطاولة المسدسة المطابقة تقريبا في لوحة من مجموعة  بيني.
type: لوحة ، صفحة ألبوم ، السلالة الحاكمة المغولية
holder: عهدة عائلة الخليلي – مجموعة ناصر د. الخليلي للفن الإسلامي
keywords: الهند ، مغول ، لوحة ، حبر ، ذهب ، لون مائي ، ورق ، حديقة ، سجر سرو
tags: الهند ، مغول ، لوحة ، حبر ، ذهب ، لون مائي ، ورق ، حديقة ، سجر سرو

en.name: The rulers of the Mughal dynasty from Babur to Awrangzeb, with their ancestor Timur
description:
Timur occupies the central position in this group portrait. From the front, and on the left are the emperors Shah Jahan, Akbar and Babur, with Abu Sa‘id, ruler of Samarkand, and Timur’s son, Miranshah. On the right are the emperors Awrangzeb, Jahangir and Humayun, and two of Timur’s other sons, ‘Umar Shaykh and Muhammad Sultan. The figures are identified by legends in gold.  
The setting is a terrace overlooking a garden with cypress trees. The figures kneel on a rich floral carpet on which are precious objects, including two unusual incense burners and an enamelled table with two Chinese porcelain vases. So meticulous are the details that smoke rising from the incense burners can be seen.  
Although the composition must date from the beginning of Awrangzeb’s reign, the style of the painting suggests that it is an 18th century work, and that it was painted by Bhawani Das. His signature appears on a virtually identical hexagonal table in a painting in the Binney Collection.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art
keywords: India; Mughal; painting; ink; gold; watercolour; paper; garden; cypress
materials: Ink, gold and opaque watercolour on paper, mounted on card as an album page; panel (on the reverse) written in *nasta‘liq*

en.name: Illuminated Qur’an manuscript
short_description: This 19th-century Qur'an manuscript opens with an elaborately decorated and gilt double page giving the first chapter 'Al-Fatiha' on the right and the beginning of chapter 2 'Al-Baqara' on the right. The text, disposed in 15 lines on each page and framed by gold margins, is executed in black naskhi script, with red detailing. The chapter headings are executed in white riqa' script against a solid golden cartouche with blue floral detailing. The verse dividers are rendered as small gold discs. major subdivisions in the text are marked by small red inscriptions or elaborate, colourful medallions in the margins. The last double-page has elaborately coloured and gilt cartouches, the right giving the name of the calligrapher Hashim al-Kashafi, one of the students of Abd al Qader al-Rasmi, in the year 1286 H/ 1865 CE.
holder: Sharjah Museum of Islamic Civilisation / Sharjah Museums Department
artist: Calligrapher Hashim al-Kashafi, one of the students of Abd al-Qader al-Rasmi
keywords: naskhi; riqa'
materials: European paper, black ink, pigments, gilding, pasteboard, leather

en.name: *Moor with oranges*
description: Sorolla painted this Moor with oranges in Italy (where he lived on a scholarship), at the end of 1885 or beginning of 1886, long before he travelled to Tiwan, Morocco, in 1919. This is a typical example of Oriental painting made for sale, as Orientalist painting was very fashionable at the time. Sorolla painted mostly Moors and concubines, which conformed to Western ideals of life in the East and not necessarily with reality. Like the main character of this painting, a Moor smoking, wearing the exotic hijab and barefoot, holding an orange in his hand.
keywords: Orientalist painting; Spain; Formation of painters

en.name: *The Hunt of Diana*
description:
The work was commissioned from Domenichino by his patron, Cardinal Pietro Aldrobrandini. However, it came into the possession of Cardinal Scipione Borghese when he took it by force from the artist's study, depriving the original client, a nephew of Clement VIII (1592–1605), his traditional rival. The subject is inspired by a passage from Virgil's *Aeneid* (canto V) that describes the archery competition between Aeneas' friends: aiming at a dove tied to a post, the first archer hits the post; the second cuts the ribbon holding the bird; the third misses and the fourth shoots regardless to demonstrate his skill, and his arrow bursts into flames and ends up in the clouds. The sequence is transposed into the domain of nymph disciples of Diana, the goddess of hunting, an idyllic and luminous environment that represents the mythical Arcadia. The literary metaphors derive from the cultured Domenichino's involvement with G. B. Agucchi, secretary to the cardinal and adviser to the painter in the conception of the work.  
In the representation of the nymphs' play, the painter is attempting to paint the poetic and chronological narration of the facts, lifting pictorial art above poetic art and, in general dissolving the limit traditionally placed on different art forms; a topic that was widely discussed in the Baroque period.  
The pose and the expression of the “affections” (feelings) on the faces help to explain the succession of events, while the unbridled play is contained in a classical equilibrium. The nymph holding the greyhound shows us what will happen to the two male figures hidden amongst the bushes on the right-hand side of the canvas.  
According to the myth, Diana's terrible rage was unleashed against the hunter Actaeon who, having seen her bathing, was turned into a stag and devoured by his own dogs. One of the nymphs immersed in the water, tender and sensual, gazes at the viewer and links the internal and external spaces of the painting; another attempt to overcome limitations, in this instance spatial, that is typical of Baroque art.

The canvas was painted for Cardinal Pietro Aldobrandini, nephew of the preceding Pope Clement VIII, who had a strong dislike for the Borghese family. However, Cardinal Scipione wanted the painting for himself and had it forcibly removed from the artist's studio, imprisoning the artist for several days.  
In this painting Domenichino synthesises the colour of Bolognese painting, Roman drawings and Leonardo's theories on aerial perspective.
keywords: Mythology; Bolognese influence; Bolognese painting; Roman drawing; aereal perspective; Leonardo da Vinci; classical model; patronage

it.name: *La caccia di Diana*
description:
L'opera fu commissionata a Domenichino dal cardinale Pietro Aldrobrandini, suo protettore. Tuttavia il cardinale Scipione Borghese ne entrò in possesso sottraendola con la forza dallo studio dell'artista e all'originario committente, nipote di Clemente VIII (1592-1605), suo storico rivale. Il soggetto si ispira a un passo dell'*Eneide* di Virgilio (canto V), dove è descritta la gara di tiro con l'arco tra i compagni di Enea: mirando a una colomba legata a un palo, il primo arciere colpisce il palo, il secondo taglia il nastro che tiene il volatile, il terzo va a segno, il quarto tira comunque per dimostrare la sua bravura e la sua freccia, incendiandosi, finisce tra le nuvole. La sequenza è trasposta nella cerchia delle ninfe seguaci di Diana, dea della caccia, in un'ambientazione idilliaca e luminosa che rappresenta la mitica Arcadia. Le metafore letterarie derivano dalla frequentazione del colto Domenichino con G.B. Agucchi, segretario del cardinale e consigliere del pittore nell'ideazione dell'opera. Nella rappresentazione del gioco delle ninfe il pittore si propone di realizzare in pittura la narrazione poetica e cronologica del fatto, ottenendo così il superamento dell'arte pittorica rispetto a quella poetica e, più in generale, quello del limite tradizionalmente attribuito alle varie arti, tema assai dibattuto in età barocca.  
La posa e l'espressione degli “affetti” (sentimenti) sui volti aiuta a riconoscere il succedersi degli eventi, mentre il gioco sfrenato è contenuto in un classico equilibrio. La ninfa che trattiene il levriero fa già intendere quanto avverrà alle due figure maschili nascoste tra i cespugli sul lato destro della tela. Secondo il mito infatti la terribile collera di Diana si scagliò sul cacciatore Atteone che, colpevole di averla vista al bagno, fu tramutato in cervo e divorato dai suoi stessi cani. Una delle ninfe immerse nell'acqua, morbidamente sensuale, fissando lo spettatore fa da collegamento tra lo spazio esterno e quello interno del dipinto: una ulteriore ricerca di superamento dei limiti, questa volta spaziali, tipica dell'arte barocca.

La tela fu dipinta per il cardinale Pietro Aldobrandini, nipote del precedente papa Clemente VIII , fortemente avverso alla famiglia Borghese. Ma il cardinale Scipione volle il dipinto per sé e lo rimosse a forza dallo studio dell'artista, facendolo imprigionare per alcuni giorni. In questo dipinto Domenichino sintetizza il colore della pittura bolognese, il disegno romano, le teorie leonardesche sulla prospettiva aerea.
keywords: Mitologia; influenza bolognese; pittura bolognese; disegno romano; prospettiva aerea; Leonardo da Vinci; mecenatismo

ar.name: ثوب مردن العتبر
description:
ثوب مردن العنبر، مطرز من قماش التفا (العلم)، مردن مطرز على القبة (قبة العنبر) على شكل القوس، تأخذ شكل مربع مطرز عليها أشكال هندسية ونباتية. يوجد في الزاوية العلوية من قبة الثوب قماش مخملي على الكتفين؛ كما أن له أكمام كبيرة وطويلة مزينة بزخارف هندسية مطرزة على الساعد وحواف الكم. يعلو طرف القبة والأكتاف ردهات من قماش المخمل باللون الخمري. الأكمام مردنة على الساعد، وعند طرف الكم يوجد تطريز بأشكال هندسية. وعلى جوانب الثوب (البنايق) تطريز بأشكال نباتية، وعلى الردفة الخلفية للثوب يوجد أربع خطوط عريضة من غرزة القصب. وينطلق تميز هذا الثوب نظراً لكونه عملي جدا ومريح حيث يضمن سهولة الحركة والعمل بلونه المتميز. تقوم نساء بيت جالا في منطقة بيت لحم بتطريز وخياطة هذا الثوب بأنفسهن، وترتديه النساء المتزوجات بشكل يومي. تعتبر مدينة بيت لحم مركزًا للثقافة والسياحة في فلسطين، ولها أيضًا أهمية دينية باعتبارها مهد السيد المسيح، وتشتهر بيت لحم بالتحف التقليدية والدينية والتطريز الملون.  
تاريخ الحصول على القطعة: 1983 م.
dates: النصف الأول من القرن التاسع عشر
keywords: تقليدي، منسوجات فلسطينية، ثوب

en.name: Amber/Mardan Dress
description: Dress made of taffeta fabric (*Al-Alam*) with chest panel in *Al-Amber* style, which is a square with geometrical shapes and floral motifs on it. The top corner of the front panel has russet velveteen trim which extends along the shoulders. The dress also has large, long sleeves with geometrical motifs embroidered on the forearm and sleeve edges. The *banayeq* (side panels) show floral motifs while the back panel shows four thick braids in the style of *Al-Qasab* needlework. The women of Beit Jala (in the Bethlehem area) embroider and sew this garment on their own, and married women wear it on a daily basis. The Bethlehem area is considered to be the centre of culture and tourism in Palestine and also has religious significance as the birthplace of Jesus. Bethlehem is famous for its traditional and religious artifacts and colourful embroidery. This dress is very distinct because it is very practical and comfortable, it guarantees ease of movement and work, and it exhibits outstanding colour.
keywords: Traditional costume; Palestinian textile; Dress; Clothing

en.name: Chénini (of Tataouine)
description:
South-west of Tataouine, the region’s principal town, a Zenet troglodytic village (the Zenatas were a large Berber tribe in the glory days of the past), Chénini, occupies with its *qsar*\-citadel the summit of a rugged and harsh mountain, turning its back on the plain. Constrained in the east by the Farch plain and to the west by the Dahar plateau, the Jabal Demer is slightly narrower in this part, its morphology becoming irregular.  
Having completed their settlement in ancient Chénini, situated on one of the foothills of the Jabal facing the Farch and not far from the mosque in sight known as the “Mosque of the Seven Sleepers”, the Zenets would have built the *qsar*\-citadel towards the end of the 6th/12th century, which corresponds to the time, a little over a century, after the arrival of the first wave of Hilalians from Upper Egypt. It is most probably from this time onwards that the present village began to appear lower down, facing the Dahar, the plateau which possesses a stretch which can be cultivated as well as a few pastures.  
As in the other villages of this rocky outcrop which marks out the Jabal Demer, the *qsar* of Chénini hangs over rows of houses: it is perched on the crest and consists of several storerooms, *ghorfa*s, which are stacked one on top of the other and are reached by narrow alleyways whose paths embrace the form of the land. Now deserted, this fortress, which doubled up as a collective loft, fell into ruin. Further down, the village grew on several levels, occupying the two slopes of the creek formed by the mountain; at the centre of the upper level, a relatively recent mosque is embedded into its white mass. The houses of Chénini are troglodytic and lateral in type, set out in rows. Each house contains one or more rooms which have been excavated out of the soft alluvial layer of the mountain face. The rooms are entered through doors made of palm wood and look onto a paved, open-roofed courtyard, which includes the kitchen, the latrines, the stable … the whole built to last. Some houses possess a loft, covered by a terrace or a vault, above their entrance, as a replacement of the *ghorfa*s of the *qsar* which fell into disrepair.

es.name: Chenini (de Tatawin)
description:
Al sudoeste de la ciudad de Tatawin, cabeza administrativa de la región, un pueblo troglodita zenata (los zenata son una gran tribu beréber con un prestigioso pasado), Chenini, ocupa con su *ksar*\-ciudadela la cima de una montaña con abrupto relieve, dando la espalda a la llanura. Cerrado por el este por la llanura de Farch y al oeste por la meseta de Dahar, el Yebel Demmer se estrecha en esta parte y su morfología se hace más irregular.  
Ya instalados en la antigua Chenini, situada en uno de los contrafuertes del Yebel, de cara al Darch y no muy lejos de la mezquita (llamada de los Siete Durmientes), los zenata debieron construir el *ksar*\-ciudadela hacia finales del siglo VI/XII, es decir, un siglo después de la llegada de las primeras oleadas de nómadas hilalíes, venidos del Alto Egipto. Seguramente es a partir de esta época cuando se formó el pueblo actual en pendiente enfrente del Dahar, esa meseta que por una de sus vertientes es cultivable y por la otra sirve para pasto.  
Como en otros pueblos rocosos que jalonan el Yebel Demmer, el *ksar* de Chenini tiene varias líneas de viviendas: está situado sobre la cresta y se compone de varias celdas para guardar el grano (*gurfa*s) superpuestas y comunicadas por unas callejuelas estrechas cuyo trazado sigue el del relieve. Hoy en día esta fortaleza, a la vez granero colectivo, ha caído en ruinas y está dedicada a otras actividades. Más abajo, el pueblo se desarrolla en varias hileras y ocupa las dos vertientes de la grieta que forma la montaña; en el centro del lado superior, una mezquita relativamente reciente sitúa su blanca masa.  
Las viviendas de Chenini son de tipo troglodita lateral, con un plano que forma hileras. Cada una de ellas comprende una o varias viviendas excavadas en la pendiente, en el flanco de la montaña. Las habitaciones se abren con puertas de madera de palmeras sobre un patio enlosado a cielo abierto, que cierra la cocina, las letrinas y el establo, todo ello construido sobre piedra. Algunas casas tienen bajo su entrada un granero cubierto en terrazo o en bóveda, que reemplaza las *gurfa*s del *ksar*, actualmente en desuso.

fr.name: CHÉNINI (de Tataouine)
description:
Au sud-ouest de la ville de Tataouine, chef-lieu de la région, un village troglodytique zénète (les Zénatas constituaient une grande tribu berbère au passé prestigieux), Chénini, occupe avec son *ksar*\-citadelle le sommet d’une montagne au relief abrupt et déchiqueté, tournant le dos à la plaine. Enserré à l’est par la plaine du Farch et à l’ouest par le plateau du Dahar, le Djebel Démer se rétrécit à cet endroit, et sa morphologie devient irrégulière. Déjà installés dans l’ancienne Chénini, située sur l’un des contreforts du Djebel face au Farch et non loin de la mosquée encore visible dite des Sept Dormants, les Zénètes auraient construit le *ksar*\-citadelle vers la fin du VIe/XIIe siècle, ce qui correspond à un peu plus d’un siècle après l’arrivée des premières vagues de nomades hilaliens, venus de Haute-Égypte. C’est vraisemblablement à partir de cette époque que le village actuel s’est formé en contrebas, faisant face au Dahar, ce plateau qui comporte une frange cultivable et quelques pâturages.  
Comme dans les autres villages pitonniers qui jalonnent le Djebel Démer, le *ksar* de Chénini surplombe les lignes d’habitation: il est juché sur la crête et se compose de plusieurs cellules d’engrangement, *ghorfa*, superposées et desservies par des ruelles étroites dont le tracé épouse la forme du relief.Aujourd’hui désaffectée, cette forteresse doublée d’un grenier collectif tombe en ruine. Plus bas, le village se développe sur plusieurs rangées, occupant les deux versants de la crique que forme la montagne; au centre du palier supérieur, une mosquée relativement récente incruste sa masse blanche.  
Les demeures de Chénini sont du type troglodytique latéral, à plan en enfilade. Chacune d’elles comprend une ou plusieurs chambres d’habitation excavées dans la couche limoneuse et tendre du flanc de la montagne. Les pièces ouvrent par des portes en bois de palmier sur une cour dallée à ciel ouvert, qui ceint la cuisine, les latrines, l’étable..., le tout étant construit en dur. Quelques maisons comportent au dessus de l’entrée un grenier couvert en terrasse ou en voûte, qui remplace les *ghorfa*s du *ksar* tombé en désuétude.

en.name: *Feast at the House of Simon the Pharisee*
description:
The work was initially attributed to Veronese, a hypothesis that, although incorrect, successfully identifies the inspirations of the artist, who, in his early twenties trained in Venice.  
In the lagoon city, the painter was able to study the work of Tiziano, Veronese and Tintoretto, as well as Bassano and Schiavone, reworking the characters of Venetian painting through his strictly Ferraran training.  
The scene develops within an open loggia framed by columns, two of which appear to be inspired by the columns of Trajan and Antoninus. The representation shows a well known story from the Gospel of St. Luke (7, 36–50) which tells of a feast at the house of Simon, a Pharisee, who believed that he had fulfilled all his duties to God and that, therefore, he had the right to a tranquil, comfortable life. The feast is interrupted by the sinner Magdalene, who shocks those present by kissing Christ's feet, washing them with her tears and sprinkling them with precious scented oils.  
The episode highlights divine mercy for sinners who demonstrate humble and sincere penitence. Arranged diagonally around the table, the figures are grouped into small genre scenes characterised by lively expressions, inspired by the style of Bassano. The sky in the background, crossed by intense strips of green, fades into the distant landscape. The fulcrum of the scene has been shifted to the left-hand side of the painting where Magdalene, the jar of ointment at her feet and her hair untied, turns her head in a silent dialogue with Christ.  
The intense colours, lively gestures and unusual perspective are indicative of the taste that precluded the scenic representations of the Baroque period.

The historical reference refers to the Gospel of St. Luke: Mary Magdalene who was in the house of Simon during a banquet. Kneeling at the feet of Christ with her usual attribute, a jar of ointment, she washes His feet and dries them with her long hair. The protagonists of the scene are not in the central part of the composition, but on the left-hand side that becomes the fulcrum for the narrative.
artist: Ippolito Scarsella, also known as Scarsellino
keywords: Christian themes; perspective; architectonic perspective; theatre

it.name: *Cena in casa di Simon Fariseo*
description: La storia è nel Vangelo di Luca e narra di Maria Maddalena che si trovava in casa di Simone durante un banchetto. Inginocchiata ai piedi di Cristo con il consueto attributo del vaso con gli unguenti, lava i suoi piedi asciugandoli con i lunghi capelli. I protagonisti della scena non si trovano nella parte centrale della composizione, ma sono sul lato sinistro, che diventa il fulcro della narrazione.
keywords: Tematiche cristiane;prospettiva; prospettiva architettonica; teatro

ar.name: شمعدان نحاسي مطلي بالذهب
description: يُحتمل أن يكون هذا الشمعدان قد صُنع لهدف ديني، استنادًا إلى نقوشه الغريبة على طول الجوانب الرأسية للعنق وحول قاعدته. وبينما تبدو النقوش كما لو كانت باللغة العربية، إلا أنها عبارة عن أحرف فردية متكررة وتتابعات من الأحرف. ولم تكن مثل هذه النقوش الخيالية نادرة في الأعمال المعدنية الإسلامية وربما كان للبعض منها أهمية صوفية.
dates: أواخر القرن التاسع- القرن العاشر الهجري/ أواخر القرن الخامس عشر- القرن السادس عشر الميلادي

en.name: Gilt copper candlestick
description: This candlestick was possibly made for a religious context, judging by its curious inscription all along the vertical facets of the neck and around its base. While Arabic in appearance, it merely repeats individual letters and letter sequences. Such pseudo-inscriptions are not uncommon in Islamic metalwork, and some may have mystical significance.
dates: Hegira late 9th - 10th century / AD late 15th - 16th century
keywords: Pseudo inscriptions; calligraphy

en.name: The Cairo Electric Railways and Heliopolis Oasis Company
names: Heliopolis Oasis Company (H.O.C.); Heliopolis Company for Housing and Development (current name)
short_description: The first administrative premises of the Heliopolis Oases Company (HOC). The architecture of Heliopolis represents quite a unique and outstanding experiment with form architecture. The neighbourhood's buildings – mostly designed by French and Italian architects – followed the European styles of the time, employing the principal of Eclecticism. Features of Arab, Andalusian, Art Nouveau and Art Deco styles are characteristic of the district.
holder: Heliopolis Company for Housing and Development
history:
The HOC (Heliopolis Oases Company) was founded by decree on the 14th of February 1906. Its inception, however, came first in the 20th of May 1905 when the land was purchased and the railway concession was attained by both founders of Heliopolis: the Belgian Baron Edward Empain and Boghos Nubar Pasha.  
The company’s Neo-Mamluk premises were built in 1908, following the designs of Belgian architect Ernest Jaspar (1876–1940). Currently, the building houses the company that used to handle services in the suburbs of Heliopolis like water, gas, electricity, tramways, etc.
keywords: The Cairo Electric Railways and Heliopolis Oases Company; Heliopolis Oasis Company (H.O.C.); Heliopolis Company for Housing and Development; Moorish Architecture; Neo-Mamluk Architecture; Islamic Architecture
partner: Centre for Documentation of Cultural and Natural Heritage (CULTNAT)

en.name: Church of São Roque
description:
The church, a simple and sober construction in the mannerist style, complies with the doctrines of the Society of Jesus. The interior comprises a nave and eight side chapels, the decoration of which took place between the second half of the 16th century and the first half of the 18th century. Worth noting is the amazing contrast between the Mannerist style and the more elaborate decoration of the Baroque period. The main façade of the church is very sober: symmetrical, it has two floors, the lower one with three doors, the lateral ones surmounted by two small windows, and the upper floor with three windows. A triangular pediment with an eye-window completes the top of the façade as a result of some works that were partially undertaken after the earthquake of 1755.  
The Chapel of Our Lady of the Doctrine is a typical example of Portuguese Baroque decoration, the ceiling and side walls covered with gilt woodwork. The side walls hold some relics offered to the church by D. João de Borja – an ambassador of King Filipe II at the Imperial Court of Rudolf II in Prague – in 1588. Most of the relics are kept inside two altars situated on either side of the main chapel; it is a most remarkable collection second only to that at the Escorial in Spain.  
The most imposing of all chapels, however, is the one dedicated to St. John the Baptist. It was commissioned from Rome by King João V in 1740. Construction began in 1742, carried out by a team of high profile artists under the supervision of the architects, Luigi Vanvitelli and Nicola Salvi. An important collection of liturgical objects was produced at the same time as the interior decoration: gold-embroidered vestments, several metal objects – candleholders, reliquaries and crucifixes – and also books for the Mass. The painted ceilings of the church and the sacristy are also remarkable.

The church, a simple and sober construction in the Mannerist style, complies with the doctrines of the Society of Jesus. The interior comprises a nave and eight side chapels, which were decorated between the second half of the 16th century and the first half of the 18th century. A keynote feature is the amazing contrast between the Mannerist style and the more elaborate decoration of the Baroque period. The main façade of the church is very sober. A triangular pediment with an eye-window completes the top of the façade as a result of some works that were partially undertaken after the earthquake of 1755, and again at the beginning of the 20th century. The painted ceiling of the church, dating to the 16th and 17th centuries, is also notable. Lastly, in the sacristy, there is a large chest of drawers from the 17th century. On its wooden backboard are 20 paintings relating to the Life of St. Francis Xavier.
artist: Architects: Afonso Álvares (active 1566–1577), Filipe Térzi (active 1576), Baltazar Álvares (active 1577), Luigi Vanvitelli (1700–1773), Niccolò Salvi (1697–1751); wood carvering: José Rodrigues Ramalho (1660–1721), Matias Rodrigues de Carvalho (18th century), Bento da Fonseca de Azevedo (18th century); mosaics: Mattia Moretti (active 1730–1760), Enrico Enuo (18th century); stonemasons: Leonardo Jorge [n.d.], Gregório Luís [n.d.], Silvestre Jorge (1560–1601), Manuel Antunes [n.d.], João Teixeira [n.d.]; painters: Gaspar Dias (active 1584); Francisco Venegas (active 1588–1589); Bento Coelho da Silveira (1648–1708); Amaro do Vale (active 1602); André Reinoso (active 1619–1635); Domingos da Cunha known as "Cabrinha" (active 1630); João Gresbante (active 1630–1640); Avelar Rebelo (active 1635–1640); Inácio de Oliveira Bernardes (1685–1781); Agostino Masucci (d. 1779), Joaquim Manuel da Rocha (1727–1786); Manuel José Gonçalves (18th century); Miguel António do Amaral (18th century); André Gonçalves (1685–1762); Francisco Vieira de Matos (known as Vieira Lusitano 1699–1783); tile painter: Francisco de Matos (active 1584)
history:
The Church of São Roque was built in the second half of the 16th century to meet the demands of priests of the Society of Jesus who in 1540 (during the reign of João III; King of Portugal 1521–1557) arrived in Lisbon to preach. A chapel dedicated to the devotion of São Roque formerly stood on the site. This chapel had been commissioned by King Manuel I (1495–1521) to house a relic of the saint, protector of sufferers of the plague. The Society of Jesus received the chapel in 1553, and the first enlargement of the building was undertaken in 1555.  
João III had initially intended to build a monumental building with three naves but the Society of Jesus opposed the design in accordance with the principles of the Catholic Refor­mation, which emphasised both simplicity and functionality in church layouts. The new design changed the orientation of the building from east-west to north-south, and increased its length. In 1565 the church was enlarged for a second time according to plans brought from Rome. These plans maintained the principle of a single nave. The completion of the church took place during the reign of Philip I of Portugal (Philip II of Spain; 1580–1598). After the expulsion of the Jesuits from Portugal in 1759, São Roque Church and annexed residences were given to the Santa Casa da Misericórdia de Lisboa by a Royal Charter issued on 8 February 1768.

pt.name: *Igreja de São Roque*
description:
A igreja é uma construção simples e sóbria, de acordo com a arquitectura maneirista e em observância com os preceitos da Companhia de Jesus. O interior mostra uma estrutura formada por uma só nave e oito capelas laterais, cuja decoração foi efectuada entre a segunda metade do século XVI e a primeira metade do século XVIII. Uma das suas marcas é o espantoso contraste entre o estilo maneirista e a decoração mais elaborada do período barroco. A fachada principal é muito sóbria: simétrica, com dois níveis, o nível de baixo com três portas, sendo as duas laterais encimadas por duas pequenas janelas, e o nível superior com três janelas. O topo da fachada é rematado por um tímpano triangular, com uma janela em óculo, ao centro. Esta configuração da fachada resulta parcialmente das obras realizadas após o terramoto de 1755.  
A Capela de Nossa Senhora da Doutrina é um exemplo típico da decoração barroca portuguesa, com as paredes laterais e o tecto cobertos de talha dourada. As paredes laterais integram relicários oferecidos à igreja em 1588, por D. João de Borja - embaixador de D. Filipe II na corte de Rudolfo II, em Praga. A maior parte da sua colecção conserva-se nos dois altares das relíquias, de cada lado da Capela-mor. É talvez a colecção mais importante, a seguir à do Escorial, em Espanha. Mas a mais imponente de todas as capelas é a dedicada a S. João Baptista, que foi encomendada pelo rei D. João V, em 1740, e iniciada a construção em Roma, em 1742, por uma equipa de notáveis artistas, sob a orientação dos arquitectos Luigi Vanvitelli e Nicola Salvi. Juntamente com a capela, foram incluídos importantes conjuntos de peças litúrgicas, como vestes ricamente bordadas a ouro e objectos de ourivesaria, tais como tocheiros, relicários, crucifixos e missais. Os tectos pintados da igreja e da sacristia são também dignos de menção.

A igreja é uma construção simples e sóbria, de acordo com a arquitectura maneirista e em observância com os preceitos da Companhia de Jesus. O interior mostra uma estrutura formada por uma só nave e oito capelas laterais, cuja decoração foi efectuada entre a segunda metade do século XVI e a primeira metade do século XVIII. Uma das suas marcas é o espantoso contraste entre o estilo maneirista e a decoração mais elaborada do período barroco. A fachada principal é muito sóbria, cujo topo é rematado por um tímpano triangular, com uma janela em óculo, ao centro. Esta configuração da fachada resulta parcialmente das obras realizadas após o terramoto de 1755 e no início do século XX. O tecto pintado da igreja, do século XVI ao XVII, é também digno de menção. Por fim, a sacristia, com o seu grande arcaz, do século XVII, que apresenta, nos espaldares, um conjunto de vinte pinturas retratando a vida de São Francisco Xavier.
