es.name: Aguamanil
description:
Aguamanil de cerámica en forma de pirámide truncada invertida, con cuatro pies y hombros inclinados. El pitorro y el asa se rompieron y fueron remplazados, probablemente n el siglo XIX, por otros de plata de factura europea. Está pintada en azul y blanco bajo vidriado. Los laterales mayores están decorados con nubes blancas en un entramado de arabescos en espiral, motivo retomado en los hombros, aunque con curvas menos cerradas y sin las nubes. Los lados menores motivos florales enlazados. Los pies se dejaron en blanco.  
Esta pieza forma parte de un grupo de cerámicas que representa el declive del llamado estilo “Baba Nakkash”. A pesar de que los arabescos en espiral y las estilizadas tiras de nubes recuerdan ornamentos de etapas anteriores, el diseño se han hecho más abierto y libre, y anuncia ya el estilo clásico de Iznik.

description: Aiguière en céramique de forme rectangulaire à quatre pieds et épaule tombante. Son bec et sa poignée cassés ont été remplacés, sans doute au XIXe siècle, par des montures métalliques d'origine européenne. Elle est décorée d'une peinture sous glaçure en blanc sur fond bleu. Les grandes faces latérales sont décorées de nuages chinois formant des arabesques en spirales, qui se retrouvent sous une forme plus lâche (sans les nuages) sur l'épaule, tandis que les petits côtés sont ornés de motifs de fleurs liées. Les pieds ont été laissés en blanc. Cet objet fait partie d'un groupe de céramiques qui illustre le déclin du style “Baba Nakkash”. Les arabesques enroulées et les nuages stylisés rappellent des ornements antérieurs, mais le dessin devenu plus libre et plus ouvert annonce le style classique d'Iznik.

*The Governess*
short_description: The position of governess was one of the few professions open to middle-class women of modest means, but it was often a lonely and difficult life because the social status of a governess was ambiguous. She was not a servant in the usual sense but nor was she on equal terms with the family who employed her. Here, the young woman holds a letter which has obviously stirred memories of home. It may be news of a death in her family - letters or cards with black borders were used to announce deaths. Redgrave had a personal interest in representing the life of a governess: his sister Jane was a governess and died young.

en.name: Haram al-Sharif
description:
Contrary to opinion, the Aqsa Mosque does not cover the whole area of the Haram al-Sharif. Rather, it is the covered building parallel to the southern wall of the Haram. The current building is a result of many architectural developments, which began during Caliph ‘Umar Ibn al-Khattab’s reign. He had a humble mosque built on the site immediately after he conquered Jerusalem in 15/638 and visited the Haram, accompanied by the Patriarch, Safronius.  
Nothing has survived of this mosque. However, huge efforts were made during the Umayyad period (65/685–96/715) to build the second Aqsa Mosque. Experts differ on who commissioned it, although some maintain that Caliph ‘Abd al-Malik Ibn Marwan (65/685–86/705) – the patron of the Dome of the Rock, Qubbat al-Silsila Dome and many of the Haram’s gates and walls – built it. Others attribute it to his son al-Walid (86/705–96/715), the builder of the Umayyad palaces that have recently been uncovered south of the Aqsa Mosque. Still others believe that the project started during ‘Abd al-Malik’s reign and was finished in al-Walid’s.  
The southern wall of the mosque is the only surviving Umayyad part. Here the topography of the mosque descends sharply towards the south, which required levelling the ground through columns and arches, thus creating a platform. Today, these underground structures are called the old Aqsa, and the Marwanid prayer place. Due to the fact that many earthquakes hit Jerusalem and Palestine after the Umayyad period, the mosque was rebuilt several times. The present mosque is a compendium of many restorations and reconstructions that were carried out during the Abassid and Fatimid periods. During the Crusader period, part of it was converted into a church and a large recess was added that can still be seen today in the last aisle to the east, and part of the western division was used to house the knights.  
The restoration of the mosque to Islamic use fell on the shoulders of the Ayyubid and Mamluk Dynasties. Saladin ordered the renovation of the *mihrab* and the addition of the *minbar* in 583/1187, while al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun ordered the restoration of its dome in 728/1327–1328, as indicated by the commemorative inscription inscribed in it.  
Attempts to obliterate the Islamic character of the mosque did not stop with the Crusaders. On 21 August 1969 a fanatical Australian tourist set light to the mosque causing considerable damage to its southern part. Even though his act was clearly prompted by racist ideology, the Israeli judiciary dismissed the charges of arson by diagnosing him a psychopath. As a result of all these changes, the mosque today is very different from its original layout, which was twice its current size. The mosque is usually entered through its middle entrance portal, which is one of seven. Each of the portals leads to one of the mosque’s seven aisles. These are preceded by seven openings each topped by a pointed arch, the largest of which is the central one. The building is rectangular in plan (80 m. × 55 m.) and consists of seven aisles or porticos that stretch from north to south, the widest of which is in the middle. This ends in a semicircular dome that lies in front of the *mihrab* and stands on four large pointed arches. Hollow semicircular recesses are found in the corners of the arches, which provide a semitransition from a square-plan to an octagon and then to a circular dome. The dome is decorated with vegetal, geometric and calligraphic ornaments.

es.name: Mezquita al-Aqsa
description:
Contrariamente a una opinión muy difundida, la mezquita al-Aqsa no ocupa todo el recinto de al-Haram al-Charif. En realidad, es el edificio paralelo al muro sur de al-Haram al-Charif. El edificio actual es el resultado de una larga evolución arquitectónica, que comenzó cuando el califa ‘Umar Ibn al-Jattab fundó una modesta mezquita en ese lugar, después de la conquista de la ciudad de Jerusalén en 15/638 y su visita al recinto en compañía del patriarca Sefronio.  
A la construcción del santuario original, del que no quedan restos, le siguieron los esfuerzos realizados por los omeyas (65/685-96/715) para levantar la segunda mezquita al-Aqsa. Sin embargo, los estudiosos no se ponen de acuerdo en si esta edificación se debe al califa ‘Abd al-Malik Ibn Marwan (65/685-86/705), constructor de la Cúpula de la Roca, Qubbat al-Silsila, una serie de puertas en el recinto de al-Haram y sus murallas, o a su hijo al-Walid (86/705-96/715), constructor de los palacios omeyas recientemente descubiertos al sur de la mezquita al-Aqsa. Otro grupo de expertos sostiene que la construcción comenzó en la época de ‘Abd al-Malik pero se completó durante el gobierno de al-Walid.  
De esta época omeya no subsiste más que el muro sur. En este lugar, la topografía presenta una fuerte inclinación hacia el sur, que fue nivelada mediante pilares y arcos, creando así una plataforma. Actualmente, estas estructuras subterráneas se llaman “la antigua al-Aqsa” y “el oratorio *marwani*”. Debido al gran número de terremotos que afectaron a Palestina y Jerusalén después de la época omeya, la mezquita fue reconstruida en más de una ocasión. El edificio actual es la síntesis de múltiples restauraciones y reconstrucciones realizadas durante las épocas abbasí y fatimí. La segunda gran intervención en el edificio de este *masyid* se hizo en la época de los cruzados, que transformaron una parte de al-Aqsa en iglesia, para lo que fue necesaria la incorporación de un gran ábside en la última nave este que todavía hoy se puede apreciar, mientras que el ala oeste del edificio se transformó en lugar de residencia para sus caballeros.  
Consecuentemente, sobre los ayyubíes y los mamelucos recayó la responsabilidad de devolver a la mezquita su carácter islámico. Salah al-Din ordenó la restauración del *mihrab* y la adjunción de un *mimbar* en 583/1187, y al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun hizo restaurar la cúpula (727/1327-1328), como indica la inscripción conmemorativa que allí se encuentra. Pero los cruzados no fueron los únicos que atentaron contra el carácter islámico de la mezquita. El 21 de agosto de 1969, un turista australiano fanático la incendió y produjo daños considerables en la parte sur del santuario. Aunque el acto podría considerarse una expresión de intolerancia religiosa y nacionalista, la justicia israelí rechazó la inculpación de incendio voluntario y declaró que el acto emanaba de un psicópata. Todas estas modificaciones han alterado considerablemente la estructura inicial, cuya superficie alcanzaba el doble de la actual.  
Se accede a al-Aqsa a través de la puerta central, una de las siete puertas con las que cuenta la mezquita; cada una de ellas, coronada por un arco de medio punto —de los cuales el mayor es el central—, da acceso a las siete naves que la componen. El edificio es de planta rectangular (80 × 55 m), y consta de siete naves orientadas de norte a sur, de las cuales la central es más ancha. Ante el *mihrab* se eleva una cúpula, sostenida por cuatro grandes arcos apuntados. En los ángulos de estos arcos se abren cuatro nichos de medio punto que marcan la transición de la planta cuadrada a la octogonal y luego a la planta circular de la cúpula. La cúpula está decorada con ornamentación de motivos vegetales, geométricos y caligráficos.

fr.name: Mosquée al-Aqsa
description:
Contrairement à une opinion largement répandue, la mosquée al-Aqsa n’occupe pas l’entière superficie du Haram al-Charif. Il s’agit en réalité de l’édifice couvert qui se trouve parallèle au mur méridional du Haram.Tel qu’on peut le voir aujourd’hui, le bâtiment est le résultat de nombreux développements architecturaux qui ont commencé sous le calife ‘Omar Ibn al-Khattab, lequel, dès sa conquête de Jérusalem en 15/638 et sa visite du Haram en compagnie du patriarche Sophronios, avait fait édifier sur place une modeste mosquée.  
Il ne reste aucune trace du sanctuaire d’origine, mais des efforts considérables ont été déployés sous les Omeyyades (65/685-96/715) pour construire la seconde mosquée al-Aqsa. Les spécialistes divergent sur la question de savoir qui en fut le commanditaire: certains historiens en attribuent la construction au calife ‘Abd al-Malik Ibn Marwan (65/685- 86/705) – à qui l’on doit le Dôme du Rocher,Qubbat al-Silsila et plusieurs portes et murs du Haram. D’autres l’attribuent à son fils al-Walid (86/705-96/715), le promoteur des palais omeyyades récemment mis au jour au sud de la mosquée al-Aqsa. Pour d’autres encore, les travaux auraient commencé sous ‘Abd al-Malik et se seraient achevés sous al-Walid.  
De la partie omeyyade ne subsiste que le mur sud. À cet endroit, la topographie de la mosquée accuse une forte inclinaison vers le sud, ce qui a nécessité de niveler le sol au moyen d’arcs et de piliers, créant ainsi une plate-forme. Aujourd’hui, ces structures souterraines sont appelées “l’ancienne al-Aqsa” et “le lieu de prière des Marwanides”. En raison des nombreux tremblements de terre qui ont frappé Jérusalem et la Palestine après la période omeyyade, la mosquée a été reconstruite à plusieurs reprises. L’actuel bâtiment est la synthèse des multiples restaurations et reconstructions réalisées pendant les périodes abbasside et fatimide. Lorsque les Croisés s’emparèrent de Jérusalem, ils transformèrent une partie de al-Aqsa en église, ajoutant à l’édifice une grande abside – toujours visible dans la dernière nef orientale – et affectant une partie de l’aile occidentale au logement de leurs chevaliers.  
C’est aux Ayyoubides et aux Mamelouks qu’il reviendra de rétablir la mosquée dans son caractère musulman originel. On doit à Saladin la restauration du *mihrab* et l’adjonction de la chaire en 583/1187, et c’est al-Nasir Muhammad Ibn Qalawun qui fit restaurer la coupole (727/1327- 1328), comme le précise l’inscription commémorative qui y est apposée. Mais les Croisés n’ont pas été les seuls à attenter au caractère islamique de la mosquée. Le 21 août 1969, un touriste australien fanatique mit le feu à la mosquée, causant des dommages considérables à la partie sud du sanctuaire. Même si l’acte relevait à l’évidence de l’intolérance religieuse et nationaliste, la justice israélienne rejeta le chef d’inculpation d’incendie volontaire et déclara que l’acte émanait d’un psychopathe. Toutes ces modifications ont assez largement altéré la structure initiale de la mosquée, dont la superficie atteignait le double de ce qu’elle est actuellement.  
On accède généralement à al-Aqsa par le portail central, l’un des sept que compte l’édifice. Chacun d’entre eux conduit à l’une des sept nefs de la mosquée, toutes étant précédées d’une baie couronnée d’un arc brisé, le plus grand étant l’arc central. Le bâtiment épouse un plan rectangulaire (80 m x 55 m) et consiste en sept nefs orientées du nord au sud, la plus large étant la centrale. Reposant sur quatre grands arcs brisés, une coupole s’élève devant le *mihrab*. Des niches en plein cintre occupent les angles des arcs, assurant la transition du plan carré au plan octogonal puis au plan circulaire de la coupole. Le dôme est décoré d’ornements à motifs végétaux, géométriques et calligraphiques.

en.name: Carafe and Glass - Part of a Service for Drink
description:
This preserved part of a beverage set consists of a high-stemmed glass and carafe with a stopper. The mould-blown, colourless, thin-glass bottle with pear-shaped body and a handle is raised on a low stem and base. Both items display identical decoration, each painted with white and yellow stylized floral ornaments and a blue ribbon carrying white painted ornaments. A thin gilding strip separates the decorated fields, encircling the upper and lower body of the carafe and glass, the rims and the stems.  
This part of the set was made using a mould-blowing technique at the factory of Nacko Janković & Son in Jagodina. Preserved data and objects from the Museum of Applied Art collections testify to the higher technological level of production and application of various glass decorating techniques in this factory. The attention paid to decoration is further evidenced by participation by the factory on several occasions in world exhibitions. Nacko Janković & Son Manufactury received a bronze medal for decoration in 1900.
artist: Manufactury of Nacko Janković & Son, Serbia
keywords: Mould-blown; Enamelled decoration; Manufacture; Painted decoration; Serbia

en.name: House of the Robev family
short_description: The house of the Robev family is one of the highlights of traditional urban architecture in Macedonia. It represents the best of the distinctive style of Ohrid architecture, as well as exquisite layout and interior decor. The house was listed as protected architectural heritage after the First World War. It is a three-storied house having been divided vertically into two parts (left and right), thus belonging to the type of brothers' house traditionally built in Macedonia in the 19th and 20th centuries. The distinctive features of this structure are protruding decks expanding the usable surface on the second and third stories. The most outstanding elements decorating the interior of the house are niches in the walls, as well as wood-carved ornaments applied in the rooms and on the ceilings.
history: The construction of the first house of the Robev family was finished on the 15 April 1827 as witnessed by the inscription in Greek on the marbled flagstone. It was rebuilt in 1863–1864. Construction foreman Todor Petkov built the house from scratch. Konstantin Robev lived in the left part of the house and his brother Atanas Robev in the right one. The two families lived in the newly built house until 1900 when they moved to Bitola and used the house as a summer residence. At present this building houses the exhibition galleries of the Institute for Protection of Culture Monuments and Museum of Ohrid.
keywords: woodcarving; yetties

en.name: ‘Attarin Suq
description:
As well as *funduq*s, Fez possessed markets, *suq*s, whose reputation extended far beyond the town walls. The *qaysariya*, a term signifying a commercial neighbourhood, which was situated at the heart of the Qarawiyin Quarter, with its numerous *suq*s and shops, is one of the oldest of its kind, offering goods imported from Europe and the East ever since the Middle Ages.  
Destroyed at first by a great fire in 724/1324, and then by floods in 725/1325, the *qaysariya*, with its thousands of terraced houses, was then rebuilt. The ‘Attarin Suq, one of the most reputable in the *qaysariya*, occupies the length of a long street which links up to the Merinid *madrasa* of the same name, at *Bab al-Faraj*. Complemented by trade on adjacent streets and places, this market extends over more than 600 m. and was equipped with a large gate at each end, whose “*guardians*”, wrote Leon the African, “*do their rounds at night, with dogs, with weapons, holding up lanterns in their hands. They were paid by the traders themselves*”.  
The *suq*, according to Leon the African, consisted of 150 stalls, which grew in number to 170 a few years later according to the Portuguese historian Mármol de Carvajal (16th century). Originally specialising in the sale of medicinal products and groceries, medicinal stalls stood shoulder to shoulder with hardware stalls which were distinct for the opulence of their ornamentation. Doctors themselves made up the medicinal preparations, and then sent them to specialised stalls where staff would dispense them under medical supervision.  
In the 10th/16th century, the *suq*, through the importance it had gained in terms of the geographical area it fulfilled, through the number of important shops it represented and through the abundance of specialised products it sold, was unrivalled. Even if the *suq* of today has lost a little of its identity through the growth of product variety, one can still find some traditional hardware sellers who are living examples of this market, typical of its kind.

en.name: Portrait Album – Ottoman State Officers
short_description: With the political developments of the 19th century, interest in the East increased steadily in the western world. Everything belonging to the East was the centre of interest for western observers. As a result, close to 160 artists visited Istanbul in the 19th century. Born in Costantinople in 1851, Nicolas Andriomenos was an Ottoman Greek who learned photography in the 1870s from Cosmi Abdullah. At that time, Cosmi operated a studio of his own in Beyazıt, but turned the business over to Andriomenos in late 1879, after which its new proprietor soon made it into one of the city's most prestigious portrait studios.
holder: Istanbul University, Nadir Eserler Kütüphanesi (Rare Books Library)
dates: Late 19th century – beginning of the 20th century

en.name: *Théâtre de l'Opéra. "Aida". Avenue of the sphinxes at the gates of Thebes (act 2 scene 2)*
short_description: Commissioned by Isma'il Pasha for the inauguration of the Suez Canal, Verdi's opera *Aida* was performed for the first time in Cairo in 1871, with great success. It recreated life at the time of the pharaohs, with the details and the plot developed by the archaeologist Mariette. *Aida* was performed in Paris from 1876, with a grand and successful performance at the Opéra Garnier in 1880.

keywords: Opera; Orientalism

fr.name: *Théâtre de l'Opéra. 'Aïda.' L'avenue des Sphinx aux portes de Thèbes (2e tableau du 2e acte)*

Il mettait en scène la vie du temps des pharaons, et l'intrigue et les détails en avaient été conçus par l'archéologue Mariette. *Aïda* fut représenté à Paris dès 1876, et produit à l'Opéra Garnier en 1880 dans une mise en scène fastueuse qui lui assura un très grand succès.

en.name: Salim Kills Rhinoceros and a Lion
description: This painting was once part of a *Shikarnama*, an album of images of the hunt presumably compiled for the Mughal emperor Jahangir while he was still a prince (and thus still known by his birth name, Salim). The prince is shown having just killed a lioness, with a pile of dead rhinoceros nearby. In the background are several dead antelope and around them a group of *shikari*s (hunt attendants), some with antelope slung over their shoulders, one holding the prince’s sword (wrapped in a cloth casing), and one holding a quiver full of arrows, but almost every one of them is looking or gesturing towards the cheetah on the other side of the stream that has just brought down yet another antelope.

description: إن ما كان سابقا مجلدين منفصلين هو الآن مجلد واحد يشكل هذه المخطوطة الصغيرة. حيث أن أول نصف من المخطوطة يتألف من السورة السادسة من القرآن منسوخة بخط النقش بينما النصف الثاني يتألف من السورة 73 منسوخة بخط الثلث وذلك بأسطر متناوبة بالحبر الأسود والذهبي وهي موقعة من قبل الخطاط يوسف ابن عبد الله. والجلد الرائع المستخدم في تجليد المخطوطة محمي بوضعه في حقيبة مخمل أحمر مزينة بنماذج ونقوش كتابية مطرزة بخيوط معدنية.

en.name: Two *Sura*s of the Qur'an
description: What were originally two separate volumes are now bound together to form this small manuscript. The first half of the manuscript consists of *sura* (chapter) VI of the Qur’an, copied in a black *naskhi* script, while the second half consists of sura LXXIII, copied in a large *thuluth* script, alternately in lines of black and gold ink, and signed by the calligrapher Yusuf ibn ‘Abdallah. The fine leather binding of the manuscript is protected by being placed in a red velvet satchel adorned with patterns and inscriptions embroidered in metal threads.

ar.name: قطعة من قفطان.
description:
قطعة من البروكار الحريري (كمها) كانت الجزء الخلفي لقفطان طفل بدون قبة وبأكمام قصيرة، مفصل بخصر مستقيم وتنورة/ جونلة جرسية الشكل. تمت حياكة القماش بتصميم مؤلف من صفوف أفقية من السنتاماني الكثيف، وهو تشكيل من ثلاث دوائر ورقش جلد النمر، وهنا تظهر الدوائر والرقش باللون الأحمر في حين أن الأرضية خضراء فضية.  
عُرف السنتاماني على أقمشة الكمها منذ حوالي النصف الأول من القرن العاشر/ السادس عشر، وما يزال معناه وأصله مجهولان حتى الآن، ولكن من المفترض أن الشكل الثلاثي الدوائر قد يكون ذا تأثير مانع للشر عن طريق قلبه على الساحر في حين أن الرقش على شكل جلد النمر يذكر بجلد النمر الذي كان يرتديه البطل الإيراني رستم.  
يفيد أرشيف المتحف الأصلي أن القطعة تمثل جزءاً من ثوب تشريفات لطفل من القسطنطينية أو بورسة، وقد تكون قد وصلت إلى تركيا عبر سوريا، وقد تم استعمال تقنية الحياكة المعقدة هذه، المعروفة باسم الحرير الصيني، من قبل العثمانيين في أواخر القرن التاسع- أوائل العاشر/ أواخر الخامس عشر- أوائل السادس عشر. وقد كانت أهم مصانع الحرير العثمانية موجودة في بورسة، ولكن، وخلال القرن العاشر/ السادس عشر، ظهرت ورشات البلاط أيضاُ في العاصمة العثمانية اسطنبول. تم تصميم ثياب الكمها للتأكيد على المكانة الإمبراطورية للسلطان وعائلته حتى بعد الوفاة حيث كان يتم وضع هذا النوع من الألبسة فوق التوابيت أو الصناديق الإمبراطورية.  
تشكل هذه القطعة جزءاً من مجموعة من الثياب تم إحضارها إلى أوروبا من قبل تاجر قطع فنية، وقصها وتقسيمها بين متحفي فيكتوريا وألبرت في لندن، والمتحف الملكي في أدنبرة.

ظهرت رسمة التشنتماني لمِزْقة القفطان هذه، ببقعها وخطوطها الفهدية الثلاثية، على المنسوجات العثمانية منذ القرن العاشر الهجري/ السادس عشر الميلادي. في الأساس، ربما كانت لرسمة البقع الثلاثية أهمية طلسمية، أو سحرية، في حين كانت الخطوط الفهدية تُذكِّر بإهاب النمر، الذي كان البطل الإيراني الخارق رستم يرتديه.
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
dates: أواخر القرن العاشر- أوائل الحادي عشر/ أواخر السادس عشر- أوائل السابع عشر.
keywords: كمها؛ سنتاماني.

en.name: Kaftan fragment.
description:
A silk brocade (*kemha*) fragment that originally formed the back of a child's collarless, short-sleeved kaftan, cut with a straight waist and bell-shaped skirt. The textile is woven with an overall pattern of horizontal rows of dense *chintamani*, a design comprising three circles and ‘tiger-stripes’; here the circles are green and the stripes red, while the entire pattern is set against a silvery green ground.  
The *chintamani* motif is common on *kemha* textiles from about the first half of the AH 10th / AD 16th century. Its origin and meaning are still unclear, but it has been suggested that the triple-circle motif may have had apotropaic associations among Turkic peoples, warding off evil by reflecting it back at the perpetrator, while the tiger-stripes seem to recall the tiger-skin worn by the Iranian superhero Rustam.  
The original museum record states that this piece represents a portion of a child's robe-of-honour from Constantinople or Bursa. Possibly arriving in Turkey via Syria, the complex weaving technique adopted on this textile, known as lampas weave, was used by Ottoman weavers in the late AH 9th–early 10th /AD late 15th–early 16th century. The most important Ottoman silk manufactory was at Bursa but in the AH 10th / AD 16th century, court workshops were also set up in Istanbul, the Ottoman capital. *Kemha* garments were designed to emphasise the imperial status of the sultan and his family even in death, when such garments were often draped over imperial cenotaphs or *sanduka*s.

The *chintamani* motif on this kaftan fragment, with its triple-dot and tiger-stripe motifs, appeared on Ottoman textiles since the AH 10th / AD 16th century. Originally, the triple-dot motif may have had talismanic significance, while the tiger-stripes recall the tiger skin worn by the Iranian superhero Rustam.
dates: Hegira, late 10th–early 11th century / AD late 16th– early 17th century.
keywords: Kemha; chintamani; cintamani; costume; Ottoman costume; textile

es.name: Fragmento de caftán
description:
Fragmento de brocado de seda *(kemha)*, originalmente la parte posterior de un caftán infantil sin cuello y de manga corta, talle recto y falda acampanada. La prenda está bordada en su totalidad con franjas horizontales de *chintamani* (rayas de tigre y tres bolas o puntos). Las rayas están bordadas en rojo y los círculos en verde, todo sobre un fondo verde plateado.  
  
El *chintamani* fue un motivo habitual en los tejidos(*kemha)* a partir de la primera mitad del siglo X / XVI. No se conocen con exactitud el origen y el significado del *chintamani*, se cree que los tres puntos centrales tienen un carácter apotropaico entre los pueblos turcos, al reflejar el mal contra quien lo proyecta, mientras que las rayas parecen referir a la piel de tigre que vestía el héroe iraní Rustam.  
Según la documentación del museo, se trata de un fragmento de vestido infantil de gala procedente de Constantinopla o Bursa. Posiblemente llegada a Turquía a través de Siria, la complicada técnica de este caftán, conocida como lampás, fue utilizada por los tejedores otomanos a finales del siglo IX y principios del X (XV-XVI d. C.). Bursa concentraba la manufatura otomana de la seda, pero en el siglo X / XV se abrieron también talleres de la corte en la capital, Estambul. Los tejidos *kemha* se diseñaban para enfatizar el estatus imperial del sultán y su familia, incluso al morir; así, los cenotafios o *sandukas* imperiales eran cubiertos a menudo con ellos.

El motivo conocido como *chintamani* (rayas atigradas y tres bolas o puntos) apareció en los tejidos otomanos en el siglo X / XVI. Puede que los tres puntos tuvieran una función de talismán, mientras que las rayas recuerdan la piel de tigre que vestía el héroe iraní Rustam.
dates: Finales del siglo X-principios del XI de la Hégira / finales del XVI-principios del XVII d. C.
keywords: kemha
materials: Seda, algodón y brocados en plata *(kemha)*.
tags: Seda, algodón y brocados en plata (kemha).

fr.name: Fragment de caftan.
description:
Fragment de brocart de soie (*kemha*) qui formait à l'origine le dos d'un caftan d'enfant sans col, à manches courtes, taille droite et jupe en cloche. Le tissu présente un motif couvrant de rangées horizontales de *cintamani*, motif ici à trois boules vertes et “rayures de tigre” rouges sur fond gris argenté.  
Le motif de *cintamani* est courant sur les textiles *kemha* vers la première moitié du Xe siècle (XVIe siècle J.-C.). Son origine et sa signification sont mal connues, mais on a suggéré que pour les peuples turcmènes les trois boules exerçaient une fonction apotropaïque. Elles protégeaient ceux qui les portaient du mauvais œil, tandis que les rayures de tigre semblent rappeler la peau de cet animal dont était revêtu le héros mythique iranien Rustam.  
Les archives du musée précisent que cette pièce est une partie de robe d'honneur d'enfant de Constantinople ou de Bursa. Venues probablement de Syrie, les techniques complexes de ce type de tissage appelé armure de *lampa* qu'illustre ce fragment furent utilisées par les tisseurs ottomans à la fin du Xe-début XIe siècle H (fin XVIe-début XVIIe siècle J.-C.). La plus importante manufacture de soierie ottomane se trouvait à Bursa, mais, au Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.), des ateliers furent également créés pour la cour ottomane à Istanbul. Les vêtements en *kemha* soulignaient le statut impérial du sultan et de sa famille même dans la mort, puisque ils étaient souvent drapés sur les cénotaphes impériaux.  
Ce fragment fait partie d'un groupe de caftans rapportés en Europe par un marchand et découpés, ce qui explique que le devant et le dos se trouvent l'un au Victoria & Albert Museum de Londres et l'autre au Royal Museum d'Édimbourg.

Le motif *cintamani* sur ce fragment de caftan, avec ses ornements à trois boules et ses rayures de tigre, est apparu sur les textiles ottomans dès le Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.). À l’origine, le motif à trois boules a pu avoir une portée apotropaïque, alors que les rayures de tigre rappellent la peau de cet animal dont était revêtu le héros mythique iranien Rustam.
dates: Fin Xe-début XIe siècle de l’Hégire (fin XVIe-début XVIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: kemha ; cintamani; chintamani
materials: Brocart de soie et de coton (*kemha*).
tags: Brocart de soie et de coton (kemha).

en.name: São João Baptista (Parish Church)
names: São João Baptista (Vila do Conde Parish Church)
description:
"The Parish Church is one of the most interesting of those built by the masters from Biscay and it has the advantage of being very much as it was, whilst information is also available as to who worked there and when. The church to be seen today was designed by João Rianho who began to construct the building, although the work was handed over to his compatriot, Sancho Garcia, in 1500. He was succeeded by the Basques: Rui Garcia de Penagós, who worked there until 1511, when it was handed over definitively to João de Castilho, the man who was to complete the Mosteiro dos Jerónimos and the Convento de Cristo in Tomar. Paid by the municipality, Castilho and 20 masons, almost all of them from Biscay, completed the aisles in either February or March 1514, together with their respective arches and the axial door. Among the masons were João Garcia, André de la Cota and João de Quintanilha.  
The door in this church is the same as that of the Church of Azuaga, in Spain, which means that one was copied from the other. So, it seems most likely that João de Castilho also made, or at least designed, the Spanish portal.  
The three aisles of the church are separated by a simple series of arches and a wooden ceiling with evolved Manueline ribbed vaulting similar to that of Braga Cathedral in the triple apse, chancel and side chapels. The crossing chapels, which form a false transept, date from the same period and are in the same style, with curved ribs and finely decorated foliate and heraldic keystones."

en.name: *Portrait of a Greek Wearing a Fustanela*
short_description: It may depict a notable of Aighion, Andreas Londos (1786–1846) who entertained Lord Byron on his first visit to Greece. The picture is similar in style, setting and pose to that entitled ‘Un Grec de Janina’ in Dupré’s *Voyage à Athènes et Constantinople*, 1825. Louis Dupré (1798–1837) was one of the most talented painters who travelled to Greece. He arrived in 1819. The French artist who was an ardent philhellene published in 1825 a set of coloured lithographs of views and studies of costumes from Greece, entitled *Voyage a Athènes et Constantinople*.
keywords: travels; Greece; Dupre

en.name: The Mother of God Smolenskaya
description: This Mother of God icon is known as a *Hodegetria* icon (Greek for “one who shows the way”). It is recognizable by the solemn expression of the Mother of God and the frontal position of the Christ Child delivering a blessing. The Christ Child sits on his mother’s left knee and holds a tightly rolled scroll. A copy of the original *Hodegetria* icon was brought to the Assumption Cathedral in Smolensk from Byzantium in the 12th century. In the 15th century, it was transferred to Moscow before being returned to Smolensk. The icon has a silver *repoussé basma* (hammered metal ornamentation) nailed to its surface, as well as a Kremlin School *cloisonné* raised halo dating back to the 17th century.
keywords: Virgin Mary and Child; Religious iconography
materials: Egg tempera on wood with silver basma, enamel

cs.name: Světlonoš
description: Významná role v barokní ikonografii připadá světlu, symbolu Ducha sv. který je synonymem svatosti. Andělé, zprostředkovatelé božské vůle, jsou na spodní balustrádě schodiště zobrazeni jako dekorativní putti – poslové a strážci Světla.

en.name: Light-bearer
description: Light played a major role in Baroque iconography as a symbol of the Holy Spirit and was synonymous with holiness. Angels, the mediators of God's Will, are represented on the bottom balustrade of the staircase as decorative *putti*, messengers and guardians of the light.
artist: Ondřej Zahner (1709 Ettershausen – 1752 Olomouc) and workshop

en.name: Church of San José
description:
It was here in the lower part of the Albaicín where the first administrators of the recently conquered city established themselves, giving the streets names such as *los Oidores*, the Judges, where the officials of the Chancellery lived. Continuing from here, heading up the calle San Juan de los Reyes and then turning along the Cuesta de San Gregorio, we find the Church of San José, built in around 1525 by the architect Rodrigo Hernández on top of the former Mosque *al-murabitin*, or Mosque of the Almoravids.  
Of the Islamic building, still surviving are the *aljibe* or water tank, which must have supplied water to the fountain for ablutions, and the *laminar*, which was repurposed as the bell tower. Inside, the church is organised with four pointed arches that support the pitched roof decorated with geometric motifs. The sanctuary roof comprises magnificent strapwork *armadura* made by the carpenter Domingo de Frechilla, and financed by doña Leonor Manrique, the widow of don Pedro Carrillo de Sotomayor, as a burial place for the family. The Memorial Chapel of the Nuñez de Salazar family also has a notable *armadura*, richly decorated with strapwork.

es.name: Iglesia de San José
description:
En esta zona baja del Albaicín se establecieron los primeros administradores de la ciudad recién conquistada, dando nombre a calles como la de los Oidores, en la que se hallaba la vivienda de los funcionarios de la chancillería. Recorriendo a partir de aquí la calle San Juan de los Reyes, para después ascender por la cuesta de San Gregorio, nos encontramos con la iglesia de San José, que construyó hacia 1525 el arquitecto Rodrigo Hernández sobre la antigua mezquita de los *al-murabitin* (almorávides).  
De la obra islámica aun queda el aljibe, que debió de servir para dar agua a la fuente de abluciones, y el *alminar*, convertido en torre de campanas. Internamente, la iglesia se articula mediante cuatro arcos apuntados que sostienen una cubierta con faldones decorados de elementos geométricos. La capilla mayor, cubierta con una magnífica *armadura* de lazo realizada por el carpintero Domingo de Frechilla, fue financiada por doña Leonor Manrique, viuda de don Pedro Carrillo de Sotomayor, como lugar de enterramiento familiar. La capilla funeraria de los Núñez de Salazar también posee una notable *armadura* ricamente adornada con lacería.

en.name: Divino Salvador (Parish Church)
description: This is one of the few Manueline buildings in the Algarve to remain almost intact. The main portal is the loveliest and most complex in the region. A pruned tree trunk forms the external *colonnettes* and the main *archivolt* surrounds the frame made up of another *colonnette* and plain *archivolt*, that separate a simple inter-columnation with scenes sculpted in six registers superimposed on either side. The interior has three aisles, with four bays, separated by semicircular arches set on cylindrical columns, with large bases and crowned capitals, decorated with foliage, each one different from the others. All that remains of the Manueline apse is the *triumphal arch* of the chancel.

en.name: Mosquée Sidi Bouali
description: The Almohad building was constructed in 544 / 1150, when the new city was founded by Abdelmoumen. Sidi Bouali Mosque, though simple and classical in appearance, is more finely decorated than the Great Mosque. The Almohads were esteemed for having a more imaginative architectural style than their Almoravid predecessors, ascetic Saharans known for their austerity. In addition to the typical exterior courtyard and prayer room, the mosque also houses the mausoleum of Sidi Bouali, saint of the city.

fr.name: Mosquée Sidi Bouali
description: Édifice almohade construit en 544/1150, date de création de la ville nouvelle par Abdelmoumen, la mosquée Sidi Bouali, bien que d’aspect simple et classique, est plus finement décorée que la Grande Mosquée, les Almohades s’étant distingués par une plus grande fantaisie architecturale que leurs prédécesseurs almoravides, ascètes sahariens dont l’austérité était connue. En plus de ses deux parties habituelles, cour extérieure et salle de prière, la mosquée renferme le mausolée de Sidi Bouali, le saint de la ville.

en.name: *A Room in the Egyptian Museum*
short_description: The drawing shows the arrangement of Drovetti's collection inside the right wing of the building of the Academy of Sciences in 1852. The wall decoration mimics a wall of green stone tiles. The organisation of this room remained roughly unchanged until 2006. The institution of the Egyptian Museum in Turin marked an essential stage in the rediscovery of Egypt and followed the interpretation of hieroglyphics by Champollion. In 1824 King Carlo Felice of Savoy bought the collection of Egyptian antiquities gathered together by Bernardino Drovetti, general consul of France in Egypt from 1803 to 1830, in order to give to the Piedmontese capital an archaeological museum able to compete with all the other museums around Europe. The Drovetti’s collection was donated to the University Museum together with other Egyptian monuments already part of Savoy's collection. This collection already included more than five thousand pieces including statues (one of them is the famous statue of Rameses II), steles, offering tables, wood and bronze objects, mummies, furniture, jewellery, other materials and a significant number of papyri. A catalogue of the collection was made by Champollion around the 1820s.
holder: Soprintendenza Archeologia del Piemonte: Authority for the Archaeological Heritage of Piedmont
keywords: Egyptomania; Thebes; Karnak; Memphis; papyrology; epigraphy; Alexandria; Cairo; Ferdinand de Lesseps; Napoleon Bonaparte; Vienna; Berlin; collector; Egyptology; Nubia; languages; diplomacy; Muhammad Ali; Charles X; Louvre; Cailliaud; Henry Salt; botany
partner: MIBACT | Authority for the Archaeological Heritage of Piedmont

de.name: Gnadenstuhl
description: Vor dem oberen Choraltar, der einst anstelle des Glorienfensters ein Relief des Kirchenpatrons aufwies, formieren in bewusster Nachahmung des Baldachins in der römischen Peterskirche vier gewundene Säulen einen Bildraum, in welchem sich die Trinität in Begleitung von Engeln herabzusenken scheint. Indem Gottvater seinen gekreuzigten Sohn präsentiert, folgt die Skulpturengruppe dem Typus des Gnadenstuhls. Die von ihm zudem getragene Papstkrone propagiert zusammen mit den Säulen den Führungsanspruch der katholischen Konfession.

en.name: The Mercy Seat
description: Four winding columns, deliberately imitating the ciborium of St. Peter’s Basilica in Rome, form a pictorial space in front of the upper high altar. There, instead of the modern glory window, a relief of the church’s patron once hung. It is into this space that the Holy Trinity seems to descend in the company of angels. This array of sculptures follows the iconography of the Mercy Seat: God the Father is shown presenting His crucified Son. Moreover, the papal crown that He is wearing, together with the winding columns, symbolizes the Catholic Church’s claim to religious leadership.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

ar.name: زبدية عليها طائر بطراز خاص
description: هذه الزبدية المسطحة ذات القاعدة الحلقية تظهر طائرا ذو طراز خاص وعلى رأسه تاج من ريش. وهي مرسومة على طلاء فخاري أبيض والحدود الخارجية للطائر مرسومة بالأسود وجسمه وجناحاه وذيله مملوءة بلون أخضر زيتوني وأسود وأحمر. وحول الطائر الزبدية مزينة بشكل مزهر وبنبات الكرمة والإطار مزين بنقاط سوداء. وربما أنتجت إما في نيسابور أو أمول.

en.name: Bowl with stylised bird
description: This flat bowl with a ring base shows a bird with stylised plumage on its head. Painted on white engobe (slip), the outline of the bird is painted in black, its body, wings and tail filled with olive green, black, and red. Around the bird, the bowl is decorated with a floral and vine motif and the rim is decorated with black dots. It was presumably produced in either Nishapur or Amol.
keywords: Ceramics

ar.name: مصباح مسجد
description: القطعة عبارة عن مصباح مسجد ذو نقش جاري يقول : "" هذا صنع لمولانا السلطان المالك كوجوك حفظه الله بحفصله ونوّر قبره"". هذا المصباح صنع لقبر السلطان المملوكي الأشرف الدين كوجوك ابن الناصر ابن قلوون الذي حكم كطفل لستة أشهر في عام 746 هجري (1341-42) ميلادي وفي شهر سبتمبر عام 1345 فقد اغتيل من قبل أخيه الأصغر شعبان وقد بني ضريحه في القاهرة في 1346 -1347

el.name: Καντήλα τεμένους
description: Καντήλα τζαμιού με επιγραφή σε ρέουσα γραφή : «Αυτό κατασκευάστηκε για τον άρχοντα μας τον σουλτάνο αλ-Μαλίκ αλ-Κουτζούκ, είθε ο θεός να τον προστατεύει με την χάρη του και να φωτίζει το μαυσωλείο του». Η καντήλα κατασκευάστηκε για τον Μαμελούκο σουλτάνο αλ-Ασράφ Αλά αλ-Ντιν Κουτζούκ ιμπν αλ- Νάσιρ ιμπν Καλαούν, που βασίλευσε ως παιδί για έξη μήνες το έτος Εγίρας 746 (1341-42). Το Σεπτέμβριο του 1345 δολοφονήθηκε από τον νεώτερο αδελφό του Σααμπάν και το 1346-47 αναγέρθηκε το μαυσωλείο του στο Κάιρο.
materials: Γυαλί με επίχρυσο και σμάλτινο διάκοσμο

en.name: Mosque lamp
description: Mosque lamp with a cursive inscription reading: “This was made for our Lord the Sultan al-Malik al-Kujuk, may God protect him with his Grace and illuminate his mausoleum”. This lamp was made for the tomb of the Mamluk sultan al-Ashraf Ala` ad-Din Kujuk, ibn al-Nasir, ibn Qalawun, who reigned as a child for six months in AH 746 (AD 1341-42). In September 1345 he was murdered by his younger brother Sha`ban and his mausoleum was erected in Cairo in 1346-1347.
keywords: Lamp; Tomb; Al-Ashraf Ala` ad-Din Kujuk; Glass; funerary object
materials: Glass with gilded and enamel decoration
tags: Glass with gilded and enamel decoration

de.name: Stuck
description: Der kräftige Laubwerkstuck mit langen, teils durchaus feinen und filigranen Akanthusranken ist ein Werk des Paolo d’Allio, der ein Verwandter von Diego Francesco Carlone war. Er arbeitete im Gefolge der Carlone in Süddeutschland und Österreich.

en.name: Stucco
description: The bold foliage stucco with long acanthus vines, often highly delicate and filigree is a work of Paolo d’Allo, who was a relative of Diego Francesco Carlone. He worked as part of Carlone’s retinue in southern Germany and Austria.

en.name: *The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia*, Volume 3, title page: *Temple of El Khasne*
short_description: This image represents the vignette on the title page of Volume 3 to 'The Holy Land, Syria, Idumea, Arabia, Egypt and Nubia' from drawings made on the spot by David Roberts, lithographed by Louis Haghe and published in six volumes by F.G. Moon in London between 1842-1845. It is entitled 'Temple of El Khasne, Petra' and shows the spectacular treasury of Petra as seen by travellers approaching the ancient city through the famous, steep and narrow ravine. Petra had remained forgotten until rediscovered by the Swiss explorer Johann Ludwig Burckhardt in 1812. Subsequently, it became one of the romantic fascinations of European Orientalist artists and writers.Roberts visited Petra in early March 1839, and he wrote that it was 'probably one of the greatest challenges on earth to a painter'.
holder: Sharjah Art Museum / Sharjah Museums Authority

en.name: Lamborghini LM002
description:
This white-on-red SUV marks a surprising endeavour for Lamborghini – a brand known for sports cars. Challenging all expectations, the LM002 represents the third among Lamborghini’s off-road vehicles, following the Cheetah and the LM001.  
  
With only 328 models produced worldwide, the rare civilian model offers all customary luxuries outfitted in the military truck. The massive exterior of the so-called Rambo-Lambo camouflages numerous curiosities within the snug interior including a battery power switch, storage in rear seats and a stereo mounted on the ceiling.  
  
Whilst Lamborghini commissioned special Pirelli Scorpion tyres to soar through the desert, its most daring feature remains the impressive V12-engine, borrowed from the Lamborghini Countach. The desert-yacht ranges between 455-600 horsepower and prevails as an all-time favourite of bizarre car creations.
holder: Sheikh Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
keywords: SUV; Four-Door; Lamborghini; Military; 4x4; Sports Car
materials: Steel, aluminium, glass, leather, rubber, paint, plastic; assembling, moulding, welding, painting
tags: Steel, aluminium, glass, leather, rubber, paint, plastic

ar.name: لوحة معكوسة على الزجاج : قالب وشم ذو أشكال مسيحية
description: في القاهرة فإن الأولياء الأكثر شهرة لديهم يوم زيارة أسبوعي.    وبالنسبة للإمام الشافعي هو يوم الجمعة. و ضريح هذا العالم الشرعي الذي توفي في عام 820 هو أحد المواقع الأكثر شعبية للزوار المسلمين في المدينة. و في منتصف عقد 1970 كان هناك فنان أوشمة جوال الذي كان يرسم لوحاته معكوسة على الزجاج كل أسبوع في السوق أمام ضريح الشافعي وكان ينتظر الزبائن: المسلمون وكذلك الأقباط. وإحدى اللوحات الزجاجية المعكوسة التي تم الحصول عليها منه تظهر صورتين لمريم العذراء التي كانت تعرف بـ (أم الرب) ومرة ثانية (سيدة الأحزان) والصورة الأخيرة كانت تستخدم كنموذج لـ ( ماتر دولوروسا) من فلورنتين في القرن السابع عشر للمعلم كارلو دولشي حيث وصلت لمكانة دينية من الإسكندرية إلى أسوان بين المسيحيين. و يقال بأنه في كنيسة على الضفة الغربية للنيل فإن الطبعة الملونة لدولشي ( سيدة الأحزان لدينا) بكت دموعا من الدم من شعاع الضوء من أجل الأقباط الذين تم إضطهادهم.

en.name: Reverse painting on glass: Tattoo template with Christian motifs
description: In Cairo, the most famous saints have their weekly visiting day. For Imam Shafi’i it is Friday. The mausoleum of the legal scholar, who died in 820, is one of the most popular sites for Muslim pilgrimages in the city. In the mid-1970s a wandering tattoo artist set up his reverse glass paintings every week on the market place in front of the Shafi’i Mausoleum and waited for customers: Muslims as well as Copts. One of the reverse glass paintings acquired from him shows two images of the Virgin Mary, once as the *Mother of God*, and again as *Our Lady of Sorrows*. The latter image served as a model for the *Mater Dolorosa* of the Florentine 17th century master Carlo Dolci, as it attained cult status from Alexandria to Aswan among Christians. It is said that, in a church on the west bank of the Nile, a coloured print of Dolci's *Our Lady of Sorrows* "cried tears of blood" from her right eye for the persecuted Copts.

en.name: Panel with a large bouquet
short_description: This polychromatic panel is decorated with an image of a bowl filled with pears, apples and other fruits, topped by a small vase with flowers such as carnations, tulips, sunflowers and daisies coming out of it, which are interlaced with a rinceau pattern of palmettes, half-palmettes and vine leaves. The main colours are blue, green and brown. The decorative style, colour palette and manufacture all indicate a typical Tunisian ceramic, containing a mix of Andalusian and Ottoman influences.
keywords: Ceramic; Andalusian influences; Ottoman influences
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Panneau au grand bouquet
short_description: Il s’agit d’un panneau polychrome décoré d’une coupe remplie de fruits, de pommes et de poires, surmontée d’un petit vase d’où émerge une gerbe fleurie, une composition florale où œillets, tulipes, tournesols et marguerites se mêlent aux rinceaux de palmettes, demi-palmettes et feuilles de vigne. Les couleurs dominantes sont le bleu, le vert et le brun. Le décor, les couleurs et la technique de fabrication de ce panneau caractérisent la céramique tunisienne où les traditions andalouses se mêlent aux influences ottomanes.
keywords: Céramique; Influences andalouses; Influences ottomanes
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Awl
description: This weaving tool, made of wood and iron is used for piercing and fibre manipulation. The holes created by an awl may be used as a guide for threads.
holder: Jordan River Foundation Bani Hamida Weaving Project

de.name: Kreuzaltar (Hochaltar)
description: Der elegante Hochaltar Augsburger Provenienz birgt anstelle eines Altarblattes eine vollplastische Darstellung der Kreuzigung Christi mit Maria und Johannes. Da das üblicherweise im Altarbild dargestellte Martyrium der Kirchenpatrone Gordian und Epimachus schon in den Deckenfresken abgehandelt wird, kann es hier dem 'Urmärtyrer' Christus Platz machen, in dessen Nachfolge die beiden seitlich in Form von Statuen präsenten Heiligen mit ihrem Wirken und Sterben stehen.

en.name: Altar of the Cross (High Altar)
description: The elegant high altar of Augsburg origin contains a three-dimensional representation of the crucifixion of Christ with the Virgin Mary and John instead of an altarpiece. Since it is usually portrayed in the altarpiece, the martyrdom of the church patrons Gordian and Epimachus already depicted in the ceiling frescoes gives way for the “original” martyr Christ, in whose succession the two saints, present at the side in the form of statues, stand with their work and death.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Dish serving for dried fruits or nuts
short_description: Sultan Abdülhamid II founded in 1891 the *Yıldız Çini Fabrika-i Hümâyûnu* (Yıldız Royal Tile Factory) in the garden of Yıldız Palace in order to revive Turkish tile art and give it a new direction and momentum. Vases, hanging wall plates and many sorts of daily-use wares were produced in the factory, including writing and dinner table utensils, card plates, lidded bowls, pans, *aşure* (a kind of dessert) trays, sugar bowls, tea and coffee cups. Many native and foreign artists have worked in the tile factory of Yıldız. One of them, Halid Naci received training in tile painting in Sevres, France after his education at the *Sanayi-i Nefise Mektebi* (School of Fine Arts) and he was assigned to be head painter of the tile factories after his return.
keywords: yıldız ceramic; Turkish decorative arts

ar.name: صحن
description: من بين القطع الأكثر جدارة بالملاحظة في مجموعة المتحف لفخار إزنيق هو هذا الصحن ذو التشكيل الشجري في المنطقة الوسطى والشريط الذي يحيط متعرجا بالحافة وهذا الصحن يعود لبداية القرن السابع عشر ويعطي مثالا دقيقا  للطلاء فيما يعرف بطراز (الساز) وهو يستند إلى ورقة مشرشرة/مسننة  كبيرة ذات شكل خاص. ويتميز الصحن بحرفية الرسم على سطح أبيض مثالي المنفذ بوضع بطانة عالية الجودة على الجسم وقد استخدم الفنان الطلاء السائل الذي يحتوي أكاسيد معدنية متعددة التي أعطته ألوانا مختلفة في الشي. ولمنع تلطيخ الأصبغة فإن الصور أطرت بخط أسود رفيع بتقنية (الحبل الجاف) وإن إضافة تزجيج رصاصي شفاف على سطح الصحن يعطي طبقة طلاء ملساء كثيقة بدون شقوق.وبالإضافة لمزاياه التزيينية فإن الصحن يجذب الانتباه بسبب الدقة الفنية الخاصة التي تصور ساق زهرة مقطوعة التي توازن بشكل ذكي التصميم غير المتناظر.

en.name: Dish
description: Among the most noteworthy pieces of the museum collection of Iznik pottery is a dish with a “bush” composition in the central field and a ribbon that meanders on the edge. This plate dates to the AD early 17th century and gives a refined example of painting in the so-called “*saz*” style based on a key motif of a large serrated leaf of a specific shape. The dish is distinguished by a masterly drawing on a perfectly white surface, achieved by applying on the body a high quality white engobe. The artist used liquid paints that contained various metal oxides that gave different colours in the firing. To prevent blurring of pigments, the motifs were outlined with a thin black line in “*cuerda seca*” technique. Application of a transparent lead glaze created on the surface of the dish a dense smoothly glittering layer without cracks. In addition to its decorative merits, the dish attracts attention by a peculiar artistic decision of featuring a broken flower stem that subtly balances the asymmetrical design.
keywords: Ceramics; stonepaste; Turkey; Iznik; Ottoman
materials: Stonepaste; polychrome painted under transparent glaze
partner: The Bohdan and Varvara Khanenko National Museum of Arts

de.name: Hauptfassade
description: Der gegen die Maria-Theresien-Straße ausgerichtete Flügel bildet die monumentale Hauptschauseite des Baus. Dem Schema das Palazzo Chigi Odescalchi in Rom folgend, ist allein der Mittelrisalit durch Kolossalpilaster ausgezeichnet; zusammen mit dem großen Frontispiz ergibt sich eine mächtigte, vom rustizierten Erdgeschoss gleichsam emporgehobene Tempelfront. Die an den Flanken dreigeschossige, durch kräftige Gesimse betonte Horizontalgliederung wird hier um ein Mezzaningeschoss erweitert. Das borromineske Mittelfenster bereichert im Zentrum der Fassadenkomposition die Strenge und Wucht der Gliederung mit geschwungenen Formen. Wehrhaftigkeit und hoheitliche Würde werden an dieser Fassadengestaltung unmittelbar ablesbar.

en.name: Main façade
description: The façade facing Maria-Theresien-Straße forms the buildings’ main, monumental visible side. Modelled on the scheme of the Palazzo Chigi Odescalchi in Rome, only the central projection is distinguished by colossal pilasters, a massive temple-like front elevated above the rusticated ground floor. The central projection is extended by a mezzanine storey and flanked by three-storey sections whose horizontal plane is augmented by powerful mouldings. The central Borrominian window enriches the austere, massive design with flowing forms. The design of the façade clearly expresses combativeness and sovereign dignity.

en.name: Ausbootung in Haifa. (Disembarking in Haifa)
description: The photograph shows Haifa’s waterfront railway facilities. A passenger train stands directly beside the stone quay, while a large crowd gathers between the railway carriages and the water and on a boat. Thousands of pilgrims and travellers travelled through Haifa, arriving at the port and continuing by rail through Daraa toward the Hijaz; some remained in the city for several days, contributing to local commercial and service activities. Haifa also developed as a gateway for international tourism and some offices organised railway trips from Haifa through Samakh and the Sea of Galilee toward Damascus.
keywords: Palestine; Boat; Travel; Pilgrimage; Commerce

en.name: *Guisot* (sic): *Sir, do we have to agree to the reforms? Philippe: No! No! No my friend, not even the slightest reform* \[etc.\]
short_description: Pictured in this cartoon are the King Louis-Philippe and the Head of Government François Guizot. The latter, who in 1848 did not foresee the importance of reform, advised the King to maintain a conservative approach. Since 1847, the opposition to the regime had been getting around the ban on political gatherings by organising banquets. The suppression of one of these banquets triggered the 1848 revolution.
keywords: Monarchy; revolution; cartoon; caricature

fr.name: *(Guisot)* \[Sic\]. *Sire, devons-nous accorder des réformes ? (Philippe) Non ! Non !.., mon ami, pas la moindre réforme* \[etc.\]
short_description: Cette caricature montre le roi Louis-Philippe  et le chef du gouvernement François Guizot. Ce dernier, ne pressentant pas en 1848 l'urgence des réformes, conseille au roi de maintenir une politique conservatrice. Depuis 1847, les opposants au régime contournent l'interdiction des réunions politiques en organisant des banquets. L'interdiction d'un de ces banquets est le point de départ de la Révolution de 1848.
keywords: Monarchie; révolution

en.name: Vine scroll carpet
description: In addition to North India, the Deccan Plateau, the region of the Indian subcontinent lying south of the Indo-Gangetic Plain, was an important centre of Indian carpet production. Many carpets of this group were produced for export; numerous exemplars have survived in Japanese collections. This example is regarded as one of the finest; it strongly borrows stylistic elements from 17th-century Iranian carpets due to its vine scrolls. Not only the enlargement of the tendrils, but even more the emphasis of the lance or *saz* leaves also evokes Ottoman models of the 16th century.
holder: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art
keywords: Mughal; textile; carpet; wool; cotton; floral design
materials: Cotton warp and weft; wool; knotted; asymmetrical and Jufti knot
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

ar.name: غطاء
description: تحوي مجموعة بوميلر مجموعة من أغطية الأباريق ذات أشكال مقولبة حيوانية أو بشرية على أحد وجهيها. والقطعة مثل هذه المعروضة هنا هي مكسورة ولكن المشهد والجزء الباقي للثقب الدائري لسحب الغطاء إلى مقبض الإبريق مرئي بوضوح. والطرف العلوي يبدي صياد يحمل صقرا في يمناه خلف ظهره. والصياد مع الصقر الذي يمتطي صهوة جواد هو شكل قياسي وشائع في كل مجموعات المواد ويمكن أن يوجد في كل أنواع المشغولات المعدنية ، الخزف ، العاج ، الأقمشة ، القوارير الزجاجية والدوارق اعتبارا من القرن التاسع الميلادي فصاعدا. وكان يقصد به أصلا كشعار للسلطة الملكية أو النبالة وربما يكون مجرد تمثيل لغرض التذكير في هذه القطعة المستخدامة يوميا.

en.name: Lid
description: The Bumiller Collection holds a row of jug lids with moulded zoomorphic or figurative motifs on one side. A part of this one is broken off, but the scene and the remaining part of the circular hole for attaching the lid to the handle of a jug is clearly visible. The upper side shows a mounted falconer, holding a falcon on his right hand behind his back. The falconer on horseback is a standardized and popular motif in all groups of materials and can be found on all kinds of metalwork, ceramics, ivory, textiles, glass flasks and beakers, from the 9th century CE on. Originally meant as an emblem of royal power or nobility, it may just fulfil a reminiscent purpose on this rather modest artefact of daily use.
holder: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection
place: Afghanistan Northern Iran or Central Asia
keywords: Lid; Earthenware; Falconer; Falcon; stamp
partner: University Museum of Islamic Art | The Bumiller Collection

ar.name: صندوق مجوهرات.
description: صندوق مجوهرات من العاج ذو غطاء على شكل جذع مخروط، يتألف من 12 قطعة محفورة من العاج (أربع للصندوق، وثماني للغطاء)، وقد فقدت بعض القطع، وربما أزيلت عندما تمت عملية التطعيم بالفضة الأوروبية في القرن السابع عشر أو الثامن عشر. وقد حمل الجزء السفلي للغطاء بالأساس نقشاً إلا أنه أزيل في مرحلة ما واستبدل بشرائط فارغة. لقد تم حفر قطع الصندوق بطريقة جميلة بما مجموعه 15 رصيعة ضمن إطار متشابك، يظهر بعضها أشخاصاً يشربون أو يعزفون على آلات موسيقية، وتظهر اثنتان منها صياداً ومدرباً لطيور الباز، وتظهر أخرى شخصاً يجلس في هودج محمول على ما يبدو أنه جمل. وتظهر باقي الرصائع طيوراً وحيوانات بما فيها السباع والأرانب البرية والفيلة والأيائل، بالإضافة إلى مجموعة من الحيوانات الوهمية كالتنانين والأسود المجنحة، وتظهر أغلبها في أزواج متقابلة. لقد تم ملء المساحات بين الرصائع وحولها بالمزيد من الطيور والحيوانات مما يجعل هذا الصندوق عبارة عن مجمع صغير للحيوانات من القرن الحادي عشر، وقد يكون استعمل كصندوق تخزين للمجوهرات من قبل أحد أفراد العائلة المالكة.

علبة مجوهرات صُنعت من 12 لوحاً من العاج (القطع الفضية تمَّت إضافتها لاحقاً، على يد مالكها الجديد، الأوروبي الأصل). زُخرفت القطع العاجية بزخارف مُعقَّدة، مع مشاهد لأشخاص يستمتعون في جلسات خارجية. على الأغلب، فإن هذه العلبة استُعملت، في الأصل، لحفظ المجوهرات من قبل أحد أفراد العائلة الحاكمة الأموية، في الأندلس.
keywords: زخرفة تصويرية؛ حيوان وهمية.
materials: عاج محفور (الفضة المنقوشة تمت إضافتها لاحقاً).
tags: عاج محفور (الفضة المنقوشة تمت إضافتها لاحقاً).

en.name: Casket.
description: An ivory casket with a truncated pyramidal lid, consisting of 12 carved ivory panels (four for the box, eight for the lid). Some pieces are missing, probably removed when the European silver mounts were added to the object in the 17th or 18th century. There was also originally an inscription below the lid, but at some point it was removed and replaced with blank strips. The casket’s panels are beautifully carved with a total of 15 large medallions in an interlacing framework. Some of these depict seated figures drinking or playing musical instruments; two others show a hunter and a falconer, and another one shows a figure riding in a howdah on what seems to be a camel. The rest of the medallions feature birds and animals, including lions, hares, elephants, deer, and imaginary animals like griffins and winged lions. Many of these are shown in confronted pairs. The areas around and between the medallions are filled with yet more birds and animals, making this casket a lively little 11th-century bestiary. This casket may have been used as a storage-box for jewelry by a member of the royal court.

A casket made up of 12 ivory panels (the silver mounts were added by a later, European owner). The panels are intricately carved with depictions of people enjoying themselves in an outdoor setting. The casket may have been used by a member of the Spanish Umayyad court to store jewellery.
keywords: figurative decoration; imaginary animal; zoomorphic imagery; human representation; hunting; music; musician; jewelley
materials: Carved ivory (engraved silver mounts added later).
tags: Carved ivory (engraved silver mounts added later).

es.name: Arqueta.
description: Arqueta de marfil con tapa en forma de pirámide truncada y formada por doce placas de marfil tallado (cuatro para la caja y ocho para la tapa). En el siglo XI / XVII o el XII / XVIII se quitaron algunas piezas para añadir las monturas de plata, ya en Europa, y también se eliminó una inscripción situada bajo la tapa para sustituirla con franjas en blanco. Las placas están bellamente labradas con quince medallones rodeados de un entrelazado. Algunos representan figuras bebiendo o tocando instrumentos musicales; dos de ellos muestran a un cazador y un halcón; otro, a una figura montada en un animal que parece un camello, sobre una silla con dosel. En el resto de medallones se ven, casi siempre afrontados, animales reales como aves, leones, liebres, elefantes y ciervos, e imaginarios como grifos y leones alados. Los espacios entre los medallones se han rellenado también con motivos de animales, lo que convierte esta arqueta en una especie de bestiario del siglo V / XI. Pudo ser el joyero de algún miembro de la corte real.

Arqueta de doce placas (posteriormente, un dueño europeo añadió los herrajes de plata). Está profusamente tallada con figuras de personas divirtiéndose al aire libre. Algún miembro de la corte omeya andalusí la utilizaría para guardar joyas.
keywords: decoración figurativa; animal imaginario
materials: Marfil tallado (los herrajes en plata grabada se añadieron posteriormente).
tags: Marfil tallado (los herrajes en plata grabada se añadieron posteriormente).

fr.name: Coffret.
description: Coffret en ivoire à couvercle pyramidal tronqué, composé de douze panneaux en ivoire sculpté (quatre pour la boîte, huit pour le couvercle). Certaines pièces manquent, probablement supprimées lorsque furent ajoutées des montures européennes en argent au XVIIe ou XVIIIe siècle. Une inscription qui figurait à l'origine à la base du couvercle a été supprimée à une date inconnue pour être remplacée par des bandeaux vides. Les panneaux du coffret sont superbement sculptés de quinze grands médaillons inclus dans une structure d'entrelacs. Certains décrivent des personnages assis buvant ou jouant d'instruments musicaux. Deux autres montrent un chasseur et un fauconnier, un troisième un personnage voyageant dans un howdah sur ce qui semble être un chameau. Les autres médaillons mettent en scène des oiseaux et des animaux, dont des lions, des lièvres, des éléphants, un daim, ainsi que des bêtes fabuleuses comme des griffons et des lions ailés. Beaucoup sont représentés en paires affrontées. Les zones autour et entre les médaillons sont également décorées d'oiseaux et d'animaux, qui font de ce coffret un véritable petit bestiaire du XIe siècle. Il a pu être utilisé comme coffret à bijoux par un membre de la cour royale.

Coffret fait de 12 panneaux en ivoire (les montures en argent ont été ajoutées ultérieurement par un propriétaire européen). Les panneaux sont magnifiquement sculptés d'une structure d'entrelacs intégrant des personnages profitant des plaisirs de la campagne. Le coffret a pu servir à un membre de la cour omeyyade d'al-Andalus pour ranger ses bijoux.
keywords: Décoration figurative ; animal imaginaire
materials: Ivoire sculpté (montures en argent ciselé ajoutées ultérieurement).
tags: Ivoire sculpté (montures en argent ciselé ajoutées ultérieurement).

en.name: *Al-Maryamiyya (St. Mary’s Church), Damascus*
names: Main church aisle towards the iconostasis
short_description: This church was a late 4th century foundation, which was, after its destruction in 1860, rebuilt in red brick with the financial support from Russia. Today the Maryamiyya Church, one of the oldest Greek-Orthodox churches in Damascus, is still very  popular and regularly used by the Christian community there.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

en.name: Qasr al-`Ayni Hospital Employees
short_description: The first employees at the first Egyptian national hospital, Qasr al-`Ayni.
keywords: Medicine; Doctors; Qasr al-`Ayni Hospital; Egyptian Hospitals; Hospital Employees

en.name: Detail of the alcove, putto
description:
It was probably realised after 1704, surely before 1739, when it is mentioned in a biography dedicated to its author, the sculptor Giuseppe Mazza, here working together with the painter Ercole Graziani senior.  
Coming back from Venice, the artist was probably engaged by the Zaniboni family, owner of the palace, to create this superb nuptial bedroom lavishly decorated with stuccoes and sculptures (among them *Venus* and *Apollo,* allusive to abundance and fertility); every element contributes here to a very dynamic composition inspired by typically baroque concepts.
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Particolare dell'alcova, putto
description:
Probabilmente realizzata dopo il 1704, sicuramente prima del 1739, quando è menzionata in una biografia dedicata al suo autore, lo scultore Giuseppe Mazza, che qui lavora insieme al pittore Ercole Graziani senior.  
Al ritorno da Venezia lo scultore fu probabilmente ingaggiato dalla famiglia Zaniboni, proprietaria del palazzo, per creare questa superba camera nuziale riccamente decorata con stucchi e sculture (tra cui *Venere* e *Apollo*, allusive all'abbondanza e alla fertilità). Ogni elemento dà il suo contributo ad una composizione molto dinamica, ispirata a concetti tipicamente barocchi.

ar.name: صحن أزرق
description: هذا الصحن الكبير بشكل غير عادي يعكس التأثير الصيني الذي وجد في أكثرية الخزف الفارسي الأزرق والأبيض بعد عام 1400 تقريبا. ولكن هناك فروقات حيث عود الصليب العصبي والذي بتلاته تقريبا تبدو مثل زخارف الغيوم الصينية أصله من الشرق الأقصى بينما على العكس الزخرفة على الإطار بالورقة المشطورة هي إسلامية بحتة.
type: آنية خزفية ، ذات تزيين مقصوص عبر لصاقة زرقاء تحت زجاج شفاف
dates: القرن الحادي عشر الهجري / القرن السابع عشر الميلادي

en.name: Blue dish
description: This unusually large dish reflects the Chinese influence that was found in by far the majority of Persian blue and white ceramics after c. 1400. But there are differences. The nervous peony, whose petals almost look like Chinese cloud ornaments, is of Far Eastern origin, while the rim’s split-leaf ornamentation, in contrast, is purely Islamic.
keywords: Blue dish; China; Fritware
materials: Fritware, with decoration cut through a blue slip under a transparent glaze
tags: Fritware, with decoration cut through a blue slip under a transparent glaze

en.name: Marjeh Square
description: The first public square in Damascus proclaimed the city's transformation into a modern metropolis with all the benefits of Europeanised administrative systems and industrialisation. A model of Istanbul is perched at the top of the central column erected in 1907 to commemorate the activation of the Istanbul-Mecca telegraph line.

en.name: Astrolabe-quadrant
description: One side of the instrument carries a Prophatius astrolabe-quadrant for latitude 41°, with an unequal hour diagram (horary quadrant) above. The other side is a sine-cosine quadrant with arcs of sine and versed sine. There are brief instructions in Turkish and Arabic on the sides and edges. The maker’s name and the date appear on each side, with slight variations in some details of the signature. The *nisbah* of the maker, al-Uﬁ, indicates that he was from Of, a small town on the Black Sea.
holder: Nasser D. Khalili Collection of Islamic Art
artist: maker al-Hafiz al-Hasan al-‘Ufi (Hafiz Hasan al-Hilmi, known as Gebirzade
materials: solid walnut, inscribed in red and black ink under a yellowish varnish; brass socket for the plumb-line; the lead weight for the plumb-line is housed in the instrument
