en.name: High altar
description: Occupying the whole width and height of the concluding wall of the sanctuary, the altar fits very successfully into the highly articulated setting of the Gothic sanctuary with Ranger’s Baroque painting. Through the choice of an altar design with marked architectural features – with fluted columns repeated in the forms of the tabernacle – a monumental unit was created revealing obvious Classicist tendencies. There is a depiction of the Virgin of Częstocowa, the patron saint of the Paulists, in the central intercolumniation and four figures of the Fathers of the Church in more than life size in the lower part of the altar. In the gable, there is a figure of God the Father in a gloriole interwoven with clouds and angels.

de.name: Äußeres
description: Das Äußere der kleinen Kirche ist durchaus mit Anspruch und Formenreichtum gegliedert. Die Eingangsseite zeichnet eine Einturmfassade aus, deren Hauptgeschoss von Doppelpilastern großer Ordnung eingefasst wird, dazwischen ein Portal und darüber ein Fenster, beide in geschweifter Form. Diese Gliederung mit Fenstern und Pilastern setzt sich am gesamten Außenbau fort. Im Zusammenspiel von laternenbekrönter Kuppel und Zwiebelturm ergibt sich gerade in der Fernsicht ein höchst reizvolles Ensemble.

en.name: Exterior
description: The design of the exterior is ambitious and rich in forms. The entrance side is distinguished by a single-tower façade whose main storey is framed by massive double pilasters, between which there is a portal surmounted by a window, both in curved forms. This arrangement of windows and pilasters is repeated throughout the entire building exterior. The combination of cupola with skylight turret and the onion tower form a charming ensemble, even when viewed from afar.

ar.name: صفحة العنوان لنسخة من القرآن الكريم.
description:
الورقة الأولى مزينة بتزويق ذو لمعان فريد، وتتألف من حقل مستطيل الشكل مذهب ومنقط باللونين الأسود والأحمر، يأطره شريطان مضفوران. وتزخرف السطح المحوري دائرة مركزية متساوية البعد عن نصفي دائرتين. وقد تم فصل المجموع بأنصاف معينات تملأ كل واحدة منها زخرفة لورقة كرمة مبسطة، لها خمسة فصوص تحيط بها دائرة يظهر منها نصفا ورقتين، فيما تبرز نحو الهامش زخرفة سعيفة نخل ذات زخرفة نباتية كثيفة.  
وتندرج هذه العناصر الزخرفية ضمن الرصيد الزخرفي الإفريقي (التونسي) إبان العصر الوسيط الأعلى : القرن 3 – القرن 5 الهجري (القرن 9 – القرن 11 الميلادي).  
وتحتوي الورقة الثانية على نص قرآني مأخوذ من سورة يونس (السورة رقم 10، الآيتان 70 و 71). أحيطت الكتابة الكوفية المذهبة واللامعة باللون الكستنائي، كما تم وضع نقاط الإعجام باللون الأحمر على الأحرف الصوتية، ونقطتين فوق بعضهما البعض لحركة التنوين؛ وأشير كذلك بنقطتين، واحدة خضراء وأخرى حمراء اللون، على التوالي لحركتي الهمزة والشدة، وفقاً للمنهج الذي طوره العلامة أبي الأسود. كما استعملت خطوط مائلة قصيرة لنقاط الأحرف الصوتية. من ناحية أخرى، تمت الإشارة للتقسيم بين الآيات بزخرفة على شكل وردة صغيرة مذهبة محاطة بدائرة زرقاء اللون، وأشير إلى الآية الخامسة بحلية زخرفية مدورة مذهبة مركزها أزرق اللون ومحيطها أحمر. وأبرزت الآية العاشرة على الهامش بحلية زخرفية مدورة مغطاة بتويجات مذهبة، وتضم دائرة داخلية مزينة بنقش كتابي مذهب على أرضية حمراء اللون.
أثثت الورقة الأولى بتزويق ذي لمعان نادر؛ وتتكون الورقة الثانية من نص قرءاني مأخوذ من سورة "يونس". كتبت الخطوط الكوفية بلون مذهب، وأحيطت باللون الكستنائي.
dates: النصف الثاني من القرن 4 الهجري /القرن 10 الميلادي.
keywords: فن الخط ؛ زخرفة زهرية ؛ الحبوس/الأحباس/الوقف.

en.name: Frontispiece of a Qur’an.
description:
The first page is decorated with a particularly brilliant illumination. It consists of a rectangular field gilded and stippled with red and black dots and framed by two plaited strips. In the axial plane is a central circle equidistant from two semi-circles. The whole is separated by four half-lozenges. Each one of these contains a stylised, five-lobed, vine-leaf motif inscribed in a circle from which two half-leaves emerge. A palm-leaf motif with abundant floral decoration projects towards the edge of the page.  
These different motifs come from the Ifriqiyan decorative repertoire of the classical period: AH 3rd–5th centuries / AD 9th–11th.  
The second page contains a Qur'anic text taken from the tenth *sura*, Yunis (Jonas, verses 70-1). The lively gilded *kufic* script is framed in brown. The vowels are indicated by red dot diacritics, with two vertically arranged dots for the *tanwin* and green and blue dots respectively for the *hamza* and the *shadda*, after the method established by Abi al-Aswad. Short diagonal lines are also used for the vowel points.  
The divisions between the verses are marked by gilt rosettes inside blue circles. The fifth verse is marked by a gilded roundel with a blue centre and a red circumference. The tenth verse is marked in the margin by a roundel covered with gilded petals. An ornate inner circle contains a gilded inscription on a red background.
The first page bears an uncommonly bright illumination. The second page contains a Qur'anic text taken from the *sura* Yunis. The *kufic* script is gold and outlined in brown.
keywords: Calligraphy; floral decoration; habus;  religious manuscript

es.name: Frontispicio de Corán.
description:
La primera página, decorada con una ilustración de excepcional luminosidad, se compone de una superficie rectangular dorada, punteada en rojo y negro, y enmarcada por dos franjas trenzadas. El plano axial está adornado con un círculo central equidistante a dos semicírculos. El conjunto se encuentra separado por cuatro medios rombos, cada uno de ellos con una estilizada hoja de vid de cinco lóbulos, inserta en un círculo del cual dimanan dos medias hojas. Una palmeta con profusos diseños florales se proyecta hacia el margen. Estos motivos pertenecen al repertorio decorativo ifriqí del primer periodo: siglos III-V / IX-XI.  
La segunda página está compuesta por un texto coránico tomado de la sura X, “Jonás” (*Yunis*), aleyas 70-71. La escritura cúfica, dorada e intensa, está envuelta en color marrón. Las vocales se señalan con puntos diacríticos rojos; dos puntos superpuestos marcan el *tanwin* y los puntos verdes y azules sirven para indicar la *hamza* y la shadda respectivamente, según el método desarrollado por Abi al-Aswad. Unos cortos trazos diagonales indican las vocales.  
Una roseta dorada, rodeada por un círculo azul, marca la división entre aleyas. Un aro dorado de núcleo azul y contorno rojo señala la quinta aleya, mientras que la décima está remarcada, en el margen, con un aro cubierto de pétalos dorados y cuyo círculo interior está adornado con una inscripción dorada sobre fondo rojo.

En este folio de Corán puede apreciarse, en una de las caras, una ilustración de excepcional luminosidad. En la segunda se lee un texto coránico perteneciente a la sura “Jonás” (*Yunis*). La escritura cúfica dorada está envuelta en marrón.
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo IV de la Hégira / X d. C.
keywords: Caligrafía; decoración floral; habús

fr.name: Frontispice d’un coran.
description: Le premier feuillet est meublé par une enluminure d'une rare luminosité. Il est composé d'un champ rectangulaire doré pointillé en noir et en rouge qu'encadrent deux bandes tressées. Le plan axial est meublé par un cercle central équidistant de deux demi-cercles ; l'ensemble est séparé par quatre demi-losanges. Chacun d'entre eux est occupé par une feuille de vigne stylisée à cinq lobes inscrite dans un cercle d'où émanent deux demi-feuilles. Une palmette à décor floral fourni se projette vers la marge. Ces différents motifs s'inscrivent dans le répertoire décoratif ifriqiyen de la haute époque : IIIe-Ve siècle H (IXe-XIe siècle J.-C.). Le deuxième feuillet est constitué d'un texte coranique extrait de la sourate X, Younis (Jonas, versets 70-71). L'écriture coufique dorée et vive est entourée de marron. Les voyelles sont indiquées par des points diacritiques rouges, avec deux points superposés pour le tanwin et des points respectivement verts et bleus pour la hamza et la chaddah, conformément à la méthode développée par Abi al-Aswad. De courtes lignes diagonales sont aussi utilisées pour les points-voyelles. La division en versets est marquée par une rosette dorée entourée d'un cercle bleu. Le cinquième verset est indiqué par une rondelle dorée dont le centre est bleu et les pourtours rouges. Le dixième verset est marqué à la marge par une rondelle recouverte de pétales dorés. Un cercle intérieur orné contient une inscription dorée sur un fond rouge.

Le premier feuillet est meublé par une enluminure d'une rare luminosité. Le deuxième feuillet est composé d'un texte coranique extrait de la sourate “Younis”. L'écriture coufique est dorée et cernée de marron.
dates: Seconde moitié du IVe siècle de l’Hégire (Xe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Calligraphie; décoration florale; habous
partner: Musée des arts islamiques de Kairouan

ar.name: إبريق وصحن
description: تشير أوعية فينيتو السرسينية لمجموعة كبيرة من القرن الخامس عشر والسادس عشر من الأواني المعدنية والتي هي بشكل أساسي مجموعات أوربية. ومثل هذه الأوعية ذات طبيعة محلية وتتضمن أوعية ، مباخر كروية وشمعدانات . وهي مصنوعة من البرونز أو النحاس الأصفر وهي مطعّمة عادة برسوم هندسية أو أرابيسك من الفضة مع بعض الذهب أحيانا و إضافات متكررة للمركب الأسود.

en.name: Ewer and dish
description: Veneto Saracenic refers to a large group of 15th and 16th century metal ware, primarily in European collections. It is attributed to Muslims artists working in Venice. Such ware is domestic in nature and includes bowls, spherical incense burner and candlesticks. They are made of bronze or brass and are usually inlaid with geometric or arabesque motifs in silver, with occasional traces of gold and frequent additions of a black compound.

en.name: Ráday Mansion
description:
Today the mansion is a two-storey U-shaped building, the side-wings of which surround a small courtyard. During alterations carried out under the auspices of Gedeon Ráday, parts of the old building were re-used. The central risalit of the main façade stands out emphasised by two alettes, an embossed gable and the cupola. The gate is framed by four pillars, above which the beautiful wrought-iron balcony is shouldered by corbels decorated with volutes. The side risalits only stand proud of the wall to a slight degree, completed with triangular tympana, which probably in the past bore coats of arms.  
There are significant sequences of wall paintings in two rooms on the ground floor. The main library is divided by four red marble columns into nine bays, on which painted allegorical figures of the Sciences appear. Pallas Athene and the Triumph of Science can be seen in the middle, surrounded by History, Philosophy, Mathematics, Theology, Law, Medicine, Grammar, Poetics and Rhetoric. On the vault of the small library the Dionysiac Poet, Arion, appears riding a dolphin and playing the lute. This composition reflects an engraving from Bernard Pickart's *Le Temple des Muses* (Amsterdam, 1733). The side-wall pictures also portray the power of Music and Poetry represented by scenes from the Life of Orpheus.  
Besides the main library, the 12,000–15,000-volume book collection (that consisted of 6,500 literary works) of Gedeon Ráday, filled more than five rooms in the mansion. The collection, and the policy by which Count Ráday selected books for it, was unique in the era: encyclopaedic in its remit, it aimed to own works from all branches of the natural sciences, humanities and literature. It included works in Hungarian, French literature of the Enlightenment and Protestant theology. With the systematisation of the collection based on the expertise of Count Ráday, the collection emerged as one of the most important and unique in Hungary; in all of Europe among private libraries.        
The wall paintings in the ceremonial hall on the upper floor (1766) follow a unique iconographic programme mentioned both by Kazinczy and Gedeon Ráday in the journal entitled *Orpheus* of 1790. The pictures were modelled on Pickart's aforementioned work and Ovid's *Metamorphoses* (Amsterdam, 1732) illustrated by Pickart and Philipp v. Gunst.  
The ceiling fresco in the ceremonial hall, which was ruined in 1825, illustrated the Fall of Phaeton; thematically linked are two of the *grisaille* paintings on the side walls depicting two scenes from the Life and Death of Phaeton. These pictures, along with the other *grisaille*s depicting scenes from Ovid's *Metamorphoses* completed with Gedeon Ráday's own Hungarian hexametric commentaries, transmit a homogeneous pictorial message of the idea of Gedeon Ráday.  
In the “picture room facing the courtyard” immediately next to the ceremonial hall, images of Habsburg monarchs copied from coins reveal their patron's taste. **The Hercules Room in the west wing is also worthy of mention, where wall paintings illustrating the Labours of Hercules can be seen, again based on Pickart's engravings.**

Ráday Mansion in Pécel is a fine example of Hungarian 18th-century gentry-class architecture. Its significance lays not so much in the architectural form of the building – which mirrors the owner's social status – but in the unique intellectual character of the Protestant Ráday family that is revealed in the interior decoration. The extensive library of Gedeon Ráday I, the son of Pál Gedeon I, was extraordinary for its time, yet he coupled his learnedness with artistic sensitivity; for instance he applied his own poems to certain murals in the mansion. The mansion of the “holy old man”, as Hungarian language-reformer Ferenc Kazinczy called him, was the apogee of the cultural taste of the day.
artist: Pál Ráday I (1677–1733); Gedeon Ráday I (1713–1792)

Architecture attributed to: András Mayerhoffer (1690–1771), János Mayerhoffer (1721–1780); painters: Johann Nepomuk Schöpf, Mátyás Schervitz, an unknown painter from Pozsony (Bratislava),  Ádám Mányoki (1673–1757), János Jakab Stunder (1759–1811), Franz Paul Zallinger (1724–1800); stonemasons: Mátyás Kayr, János Pauk, Lipót András Conti; carpenter: János Lipót Weingartner, József Hacker; locksmith: János Hempfner; stove makers: “Conrad”, Ferenc Weiss, Franz Hoffmann, József Grossig, Johann Scheihenstüll; joiner: Henrik Rakovitz, András Cancsini
history:
The first multi-winged mansion in Pécel was built by Pál Ráday I between 1722 and 1730. The alterations that led to the mansion's present form (1755–66; 1766–1774) are associated with his son, Gedeon Ráday I, and were inspired by the “*Grassalkovich* style” of Gödöllő Palace.  Apart from stylistic similarities, these two buildings are also connected through their architects: András Mayerhoffer designed Gödöllő Palace, while his son, János Mayerhoffer, is thought to have designed Pécel Mansion possibly with his father's help. The murals in the two libraries were painted by Mátyás Schervitz between 1763 and 1766; Schervitz was still working there in 1770, probably in one of the larger rooms. However, the decayed ceiling mural, as well as the *grisaille* pictures (of which there were originally 16), are the works of an unknown artist from Pozsony (Bratislava). The Czech painter, Johann Nepomuk Schöpf, was also known to have worked in Pécel. Several stoves, made by local and foreign craftsmen, were set on the premises.  
The bookshelves were a unique part of the interior decoration, as was the Ráday Gallery with its well-known collection of Hungarian portraits, which was destroyed by fire in 1825. The Ráday family's collection of paintings, built up in the 18th century, was sold by the family to Count Antal Brunswick and was auctioned in Wien, together with other precious works of art belonging to the Brunsvik family, in 1902.  
After many attempts to sell the contents of the library following the death of Count Gedeon Ráday the library's founder, the family successfully sold the contents of the library and some paintings to the Danubian District of the Hungarian Reformed Church in 1861. The Ráday Collections of the Danubian District of The Hungarian Reformed Church contains three departments: the Library, Archive and Museum, which today, with their continuously growing collection from 1861, is open for research and public visits.  
Today Ráday Mansion is managed by the National Trust of Monuments for Hungary.
keywords: Mansion, Protestant, library, Sciences, András Mayerhoffer, János Mayerhoffer, Johann Nepomuk Schöpf, Mátyás Schervitz, Ferenc Weiss, Henrik Rakovitz, Lipót András Conti, Pál Ráday I, Gedeon Ráday I, Bernard Pickart, Philipp v. Gunst, Pécel
partner: Eszterháza Centre for Culture, Research and Festivals

en.name: Mughal Cabinet
description:
During the first half of the 16th century, the Indian sub-continent was confronted by two new foreign presences: the Portuguese, who had dominion over the coastal regions and, in the north, the forces that would later become the vast empire of the Mughals. Among the Mughal Emperors, Akbar (r. 1556–1605) stands out. He consolidated his rule and, having gained stability and subsequently reorganised the imperial finances, he demanded from his workshops creations of extraordinary quality. Akbar understood the complex reality of India with its roots in both Hindu and Islamic traditions. The imperial workshops, therefore, produced hybrid objects to reflect this reality, but also revealed the strong artistic influences of the Portuguese missionaries (namely the Jesuits), and of the Chinese and European merchants. Such were Akbar's curiosity and interest in the Christian religion of the Portuguese and their art, that he requested the civil and ecclesiastical authorities in Goa to send a Jesuit mission to his court. A refined artistic style resulted from this fusion, seen not only in paintings but also in textiles, metalwork, clothing and furniture.  
This magnificent piece of furniture takes as its prototype Portuguese cabinets which had inspired those made in Goa. The decoration and the materials used are, however, from Mughal sources. The front of the cabinet is inlaid and symmetrical in 12 sections; each section a drawer decorated with human figures among vegetation in either courtly scenes or with animals. The doors are decorated with the Tree of Life, among which branches are mythical birds and elephants. Significantly, beneath, are Portuguese figures – indicated by their clothing – hunting on horseback with long lances.  
This cabinet clearly shows the crossover between cultures and illustrates the luxurious items available among the European courts.

The term Mughal defines the dynasty founded in 1526 by Babur in Northern India and also signifies objects produced by the imperial workshops where several influences from different areas of the empire and from Portuguese missionaries combined. Based on Portuguese cabinets made in Goa, the material and the decoration are typically Mughal. Significantly, on the bottom of the doors, Portuguese figures – indicated by their clothing – are hunting on horseback with long lances.
dates: End of the 16th century or the early 17th century

pt.name: *Contador mogol*
description:
Na 1ª metade do século XVI, a península indiana foi confrontada com o impacto de duas realidades estrangeiras: o domínio português, na região litoral, e, a partir do norte, aquilo que viria a constituir o vasto domínio mogol.  
Entre os imperadores mogóis, destacou-se Akbar (1556-1605), que conseguiu reforçar a sua posição no norte da Índia, após uma luta sem tréguas. Garantida a estabilidade e com as finanças e a economia reorganizadas, Akbar logrou elevar as criações artísticas provenientes dos seus ateliers imperiais ao mais alto nível.  
Dotado de curiosidade e de perspicácia ímpares, soube compreender a rica e complexa realidade indiana, assente em tradições hindus e islâmicas, e congregou à sua volta a elite dos artistas das várias províncias do Império que dominava.  
Nas oficinas imperiais, dirigidas geralmente por mestres persas, produziram-se obras híbridas, nas quais ressaltam as influências levadas por missionários (sobretudo os jesuítas) e por mercadores europeus e chineses.  
Movido pela curiosidade pelos portugueses e pela religião cristã, o imperador pediu às autoridades civis e eclesiásticas de Goa que enviassem uma missão de jesuítas à sua corte.  
Da fusão das várias contribuições, resultou uma expressão artística requintada e minuciosa, patente na pintura, nos têxteis, nos metais, no traje e no mobiliário, como é o caso deste contador.  
Este magnífico móvel inspira-se nos protótipos portugueses levados para Goa e aí copiados, embora a decoração e a técnica se filiem numa produção mogol.  
A frente do móvel apresenta decoração embutida, com o corpo superior formado por doze gavetas iguais, onde cenas de corte, caça e animais são representadas simetricamente, sobre um fundo vegetalista.  
No corpo inferior, as portas são decoradas com a Árvore da Vida, junto à qual se destaca o pássaro mítico com elefantes nas garras. Na linha inferior, recortam-se cavaleiros portugueses (identificáveis pelo traje) caçando com grandes lanças. Este contador ilustra eloquentemente o cruzamento de culturas e integra-se nos objectos de luxo apreciados pelas cortes europeias.

O termo mogol define a dinastia fundada em 1526, por Babur, no norte da Índia. Aplica-se, também, aos objectos produzidos naquela época, que combinavam a diversidade cultural do império com as influências trazidas por missionários e mercadores. O cruzamento de culturas é evidenciado nas portas deste móvel, onde se destacam, pelo seu traje, cavaleiros portugueses caçando com lanças.
dates: Final do século XVI, início do século XVII.
keywords: Mogol; contador; português; missões.
materials: Teca, sissó e outras madeiras exóticas; marfim natural e tinto; laca e ferragens em latão; pés entalhados.
tags: Teca, sissó e outras madeiras exóticas

description: هذه القطعة هي شبك نافذة مدبب (جالي ) مصنوع من الحجر الرملي. والجالي حرفيا يعني الشبكة الدقيقة وإن نوافذ الحجر ذات الفتحات كانت مميزة لواجهات القصور الملكية في الهند المغولية.وهذه النوافذ لها العديد من الوظائف المهمة فهي تساعد في الحماية من الظروف البيئة وتعطي الظل وتستخدم وسائل تقليدية لتنظيم درجات الحرارة الداخلية. والنماذج للضوء والظل المشكلة على الجدران والأرضيات والتفسير الفني لهذا التصوير الضوئي(جالي ) يعطي ناحية دينية. إضافة لذلك بسبب تصميمها ثنائي الأطراف فقد كانت تستخدم في العمارة الداخلية والخارجية.هذه الجالي لها تصميم متكرر من أشكال سداسية التي كانت شائعة جدا خلال عصر الإمبراطورية المغولية. ووفقا للقرآن فإن الله خلق العالم في 6 أيام ومثله بأشكال سداسية ذات ست أوجه.

en.name: Window grill (*Jaali*)
description:
This object is a pointed window grill, or *jaali*, made of red sandstone. *Jaali* literally means a net or fine web. Windows of perforated stone were typical features of royal palaces façades in Mughal India. These windows had several important functions, helping to protect against environmental conditions, providing shade, and using traditional means to regulate indoor temperatures. The patterns of light and shade created on walls and floors and the artistic interpretation of this light imagery gave *jaali*s a religious aspect. Additionally, due to their double-sided design, they were used both in interior and exterior architecture.  
This *jaali* has a repeating design of hexagon shapes, which was very popular during the Mughal empire. According to the Qur’an God created the world in 6 days, represented by the hexagonal, six-sided shapes.
keywords: Moghul; Jali

A light four-seater car and a two-seater car with internal drive were presented at the Turin Exhibition that year. These models were unique for their low weight (800 kg) and good range (80 km).This car is fitted with a centrally positioned electric motor with a cardan shaft transmission and battery power supply, housed in the false bonnet. It powers the car with 10 horsepower to reach a speed of 30km/h.

de.name: Kath. Pfarrkirche St. Georg
description: Der Grundriss des dreijochigen Baus ist ein einfaches Rechteck mit querhausartiger Verbreiterung in der Mitte. Jede Raumeinheit ist von einer Flachkuppel überwölbt und weist doppelstöckige Fensterachsen auf (je drei im Osten und Westen, zwei in der Mitte). Durchlaufende Gesimse trennen die Wandzonen. Darüber setzen die teils korbbogig geschnittenen Gurte an, die auf wenig hervortretenden Wandpfeilern ansetzen. Die Ausstattung zeigt die unterschiedlichen Stiltendenzen dieser Zeit. Vor allem an den drei zur selben Zeit entstandenen Deckenbildern, die den Eindruck maßgeblich mitprägen, lässt sich das ganze Spektrum dieser Zeit ablesen, das sich zwischen Spätbarock, Rokoko und ersten Tendenzen zum Frühklassizismus bewegt. Der wuchtige kulissenartige Hochaltar bedient sich noch ganz der Stilmittel und Effekte des Barock, während die Feinheit des ausgehenden Rokoko in Stuck und Kanzel zum Ausdruck kommt. Diese unterschiedlichen Stil- und Formtendenzen finden im Gesamtbild jedoch zusammen und ergeben insgesamt ein spätbarockes Raumbild.

Die zweitgrößte Dorfkirche in Tirol, in der hintersten Gemeinde des Stubaitals errichtet, ist wohl das beeindruckendste Beispiel für die sogenannten „Bauerndome“. So nennt man diejenigen Pfarrkirchen, deren Größe und Pracht bei weitem über das übliche Maß hinausgehen. Die baukünstlerisch eigentlich nicht besonders anspruchsvolle Kirche wirkt vor allem durch lichte Weite und das Zusammenspiel der qualitätvollen Ausstattung.
history: In dem zur Pfarrei von Telfes gehörenden Neustift wurde eine erste Georgskirche bereits 1516 geweiht. 1686 wurde ein Kurat eingerichtet. Als der Neubau 1768 vor allem auf Betreiben des Baumeisters Penz begonnen wurde, bestand die alte Kirche noch, doch fiel sie 1772 einem großen Brand zum Opfer. Die Weihe des Neubaus erfolgte 1780. Zur eigenständigen Pfarrei wurde Neustift indessen erst 1891 erhoben.

en.name: Catholic Parish Church of St. George
description: The ground plan of the three-bayed building is a simple rectangle with a broader, transept-like section in the centre. Each spatial unit has shallow dome vaulting and displays double-storey window axes. Continuous mouldings separate the wall zones. The interior design displays all the stylistic tendencies of the period. The spectrum of styles is most clearly evidenced by three ceiling pictures which move between Late Baroque, Rococo and the first intimations of Early Classicism. The coulisse-like high altar still employs the stylistic devices and effects of the Baroque, while the delicacy of the Late Rococo style is expressed in the stucco and pulpit. Overall, these contrasts are united to form a Late Baroque spatial impression.

The second largest village church in the Tyrol, built in the remotest parish of the Stubaital, is the most impressive example of the so-called “farmer’s cathedral”. This is the name given to those parish churches whose size and grandeur greatly exceed the norm. The church, which lacks any great architectural sophistication, stands out primarily due to the width of the interior and the interplay of its high quality fittings and furnishings.
artist: Architecture: Franz de Paula Penz (1702–1772); sculpture: Johann Perger (1729–1774); ceiling frescos: Josef Anton Zoller (1730–1791), Joseph Keller (1740–1823), Franz Joseph Haller (1737–1773); altarpieces: Johann Josef Karl Henrici (1737–1823)
history: The first church of St. George was consecrated in Neustift, part of the parish of Telfes, in 1516. In 1686 a curacy was established. As work on the construction of the new building was begun in 1768, largely at the instigation of the master builder Penz, the old church was still standing. However, in 1772, it was the victim of a major fire. The consecration of the new building took place in 1780. Neustift was elevated to the status of an independent parish in 1891.

de.name: Kath. Pfarrkirche St. Peter und Paul, Marinus und Anianus, ehem. Benediktinerabteikirche
description: Eine Pilasterädikula als triumphales Tormotiv dominiert die in die Klostergebäude eingebundene Kirchenfassade. Das Innere ist als symmetrische Abfolge dreier Zentralräume angelegt, wobei Raumvolumen und -form der Funktion entsprechend und szenografisch kalkuliert gesteigert und gemindert werden: ein rechteckiges Vorjoch weitet sich zum oktogonalen Versammlungsraum der Gemeinde, den acht abwechselnd breite Pfeilerarkaden konstituieren, und verengt sich zum wiederum rechteckigen Presbyterium, das in einer als Rahmung des Hochaltars vorgesehenen Pilasterarkade endet. Dahinter befindet sich der Mönchschor; seitliche Anräume dienen als Seitenkapellen und Herrschaftsemporen. Für den Gesamteindruck mitbestimmend ist der akzentuierend eingesetzte farblich getönte Rocaille-Stuck Wessobrunner Provenienz, dessen Grund die weiß getünchten Architekturglieder bilden.

Mit der Benediktinerabteikirche in Rott am Inn hat der berühmte bayerische Kirchenbaumeister Johann Michael Fischer ein spätes Werk von klassischer Reife geschaffen. Der für ihn typische oktogonale Zentralbau kann zudem mit einer beredten figurenreichen Ausstattung aufwarten, die von erstklassigen Meistern aus den süddeutschen Kunstzentren stammt: virtuose Altäre vom brillanten Münchner Rokoko-Bildhauer Ignaz Günther und beeindruckende Deckenmalereien vom Augsburger Akademiedirektor Matthäus Günther.
history: Schon 1718, nach dem Spanischen Erbfolgekrieg hatte man in der 1018 gegründeten Benediktinerabtei begonnen, die alte Klosteranlage zu erneuern, aber erst der 1757 gewählte kunstsinnige Abt Benedikt II. Lutz wagte den vollständigen Neubau der Klosterkirche, lediglich die Grundmauern und die Chorflankentürme des romanischen Vorgängerbaus konnten beibehalten werden. Die Pläne lieferte der seinerzeit bereits bekannte Münchner Architekt Johann Michael Fischer. Am 4. Juni 1759 wurde der Grundstein gelegt, und schon am 23. Oktober 1763 konnte die Kirche geweiht werden.
keywords: Klosterkirche; Altäre; Rocaille; Deckenmalerei; Rokoko-Skulptur

en.name: Parish Church of St. Peter and Paul, St. Marin and Anian, former Benedictine abbey church
description: A pilaster aedicule as a triumphant gate  motif dominates the church façade integrated into the monastery building. The interior is laid out as a symmetrical array of three central rooms, in which volume and shape of the feature are calculated to be appropriately and scenographically increased and decreased. A rectangular ante-bay widens to the octagonal assembly hall of the religious community. It  is composed of eight alternating pier arcades, and narrows again to the rectangular presbytery, ending in a pilaster arcade framing the high altar. Behind this is the monk’s choir; adjacent rooms serve as side chapels and galleries for noble persons. The whitewashed architectural elements serve as background for the Rococo stucco of Wessobrunn origin. Modestly coloured and used as an accent, the stucco contributes to the overall impression of the interior.

With the Benedictine abbey church in Rott am Inn, the famous Bavarian church architect Johann Michael Fischer created a late work of classical maturity. His typical octagonal central-plan building also provides eloquent features rich with figures , which originate from first class artists  of southern German art centres: masterful altars from the brilliant Munich Rococo sculptor Ignaz Günther and impressive ceiling paintings from Augsburg Academy director Matthäus Günther.
history: In 1718, after the War of the Spanish Succession, the Benedictine abbey, which was founded in 1018, began renovations of its old monastery buildings. However, it was not until 1757 when the elected and artistically inclined Abbot Benedikt II Lutz dared the complete rebuilding of the monastery church. Only the foundation walls and the chancel-flanked towers of the previous Romanesque building could be retained. The Munich architect Johann Michael Fischer, who was already well known at the time, provided the plans. On 4 June 1759 the foundation stone was laid, and the church was able to be consecrated as early as 23 October 1763.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Cisterns of Sidi Bou Othmane
description:
The cisterns of Sidi Bou Othmane, in the Haouz region near Marrakech, are an outstanding example of medieval Moroccan hydraulic engineering. Built in the AH 6th / AD 12th century under the Almohad dynasty, they show how crucial water management was in a semi-arid environment. Designed to collect, store, and distribute water, they supplied local populations, commercial caravans, and military garrisons in a water-scarce region. The complex comprises several basins and tanks linked by a system based on the impluvium principle, where channels run off into settling basins for filtration before reaching the main cisterns. At its core are nine large cisterns, each about 4 metres wide, 5 metres high, and 25 metres long, holding over 3,250 cubic metres of water. Thick walls of roughly 1.5 metres provided stability, and roof openings allowed ventilation and maintenance. Water flowed through a network of canals, with a nearby dam regulating the supply.  
  
Built from local stone and mortar, the cisterns were waterproofed with fine finishes. Fragments of decorated ceramics, now preserved at El Badi Palace, reflect the attention paid to durability and aesthetics.  
  
These cisterns had multiple roles: they irrigated surrounding lands, supporting cereals, fruits, and other crops. Strategically, they supplied garrisons and caravans moving between Marrakech, southern Morocco, and Saharan trade routes. Socially, many cisterns were managed through *waqf* endowments, a type of Islamic charitable donation where property or income is dedicated to public or religious use, funding mosques, madrasas, and aid for the poor. Though their use declined with modernisation, they remain a vital heritage site showcasing historical water management and human adaptation to environmental challenges in Morocco.
history: During the Almohad period (c. AH 524–667 / AD 1121–1269), Marrakech, then the empire’s capital, saw major developments in urban planning, agriculture, and water infrastructure. The dynasty inherited knowledge from the Almoravids and introduced new structures adapted to the local climate and terrain. In Haouz, capturing rain and floodwaters was essential. The Sidi Bou Othmane cisterns collected runoff from the surrounding mountains, ensuring a year-round supply.
keywords: Almohad, cistern, water storage, irrigation, Haouz, hydraulic system, waqf
tags: Almohad, cistern, water storage, irrigation, Haouz, hydraulic system, waqf
partner: Mohammed VI Museum for the Civilisation of Water in Morocco

ar.name: سقف خشبي ملون لكاتدرائية مدينة تشفالو.
description:
هذا السقف في كاتدرائية مدينة تشفالو، مؤلف من ألواح خشبية ملونة، تظهر عليها رسوم وزخارف غير دينية، تمثل مواضيع (حياة حاشية الملك والطبيعة والخيال) وقد نفذت الرسوم بذوق ومهارة عالية. كما أن ألوانها قد درست وُمزجت بحذق، واستخدمت ريشتها لتعطي انطباعاً واضحاً لتقاطيع الوجه وخطوطاً تبرز حركات الجسد. وكانت الالوان ثمينةً ( اللازورد وورق الذهب)، ولم يبق منها سوى أثر قليل جداً، الأمر الذي يجعل هذا العمل يندرج ضمن الأعمال المنفذة لصالح سلطات ملكية.  
إن هذه الرسوم والزخارف والألوان التي بلغت غاية الجمال تشبه إلى حد كبير رسوم سقف كنيسة البالاتينا. إلا أن هذه الأخيرة، فيها رسوم عيون ذات تعبير قوي وفرسان وعازفين وشاربين. وهناك رسم لأسد كان شعار أسرة صاحب البناء روجييرو الثاني، ورسوم حيوانات أخرى مثل طائر المنجل والطاووس والصقر والنسر والوعل والظبي والغزال والفيل والجمل. وهناك رسوم تمثل صراعاً بين حيوانات، ومناظر صيد ومخلوقات خيالية مثل الحوريات، نصف إنسان ونصف سمكة؛ وهي رسوم تقليدية مصرية، أثبتها بالمقارنة معهد أوريجيما (2004) من جزء من قطعة خشبية كانت في قصر كان الخليفة الفاطمي الثاني (364/975-386/996) قد أمر ببنائه لابنته في القاهرة، حيث ضُمّ فيما بعد الى قصر السلطان المملوك قلاوون (678-687/ 1279- 1290).  
أما في تشفالو فإن الرسوم تضم أشكالاً أكثر تنوعاً وحرية: نفذها حرفيون ذوو مستوىً ثقافي يضاهي مستوى حرفيي كنيسة البالاتينا، وذوو ثقافة بيزنطية، ومن الجائز أنهم حرفيون جاؤوا من مصر ومن مناطق حوض البحر المتوسط لمهام مختلفة. وتبادل الناس القطع المصنوعة من العاج والمعادن والسيراميك ( بأشكالها العديدة والقديمة) بين المملكة النورمندية والفاطمية. وقد نتج عن ذلك تصورات جديدة للفن وزخارف الأسقف في صقلية.  
لم تكن هذه الرسوم والزخارف في كنيسة البالاتينا ذات طابع ديني أو جو ومكان دينيين، لذا من الواجب أن تدرس بشكل محايد بعيداً عن التفكير الديني، وتفسرعلى أنها صور لاحتفالات ومواقف، تعبر عن الملذات والمتع أثناء فترة حكم روجييرو الثاني.  
أسست كاتدرائية تشفالو في عام (525/1131) بأمر روجييرو الثاني لتكون مدفناً ملكياً لأعضاء الأسرة الحاكمة آلتا فيلا. ولهذا أمربوضع تابوتين من الحجر الأصم عام (539/ 1145 ) في باحة الكنيسة. ثم أمر فيديريكو الثاني زفيفا عام (611/ 1215) بنقلهما إلى كاتدرائية باليرمو.

يمكن إرجاعُ هذه المجموعة من الرسوم المدهونة إلى حرفيين ينتمون إلى نفس الوسط الثقافي للكنيسة البلاطية؛ ومن المحتمل أنها كانت تضم فنانين قادمين من مصر، ولكن مع إسهامات تنحدر من كل البحر الأبيض المتوسط، وخاصة من الثقافة البصرية البيزنطية.  
ويمكن تفسير هذه اللوحات الصباغية كتخليد للملذات والأفراح الدنيوية تحت حكم روجي الثاني (روجار).
keywords: زخرفة رمزية.
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

en.name: Painted wooden ceiling at Cefalù Cathedral.
description:
The painted wooden boards of the ceiling in the cathedral at Cefalù show a series of lively, secular representations in courtly, naturalistic and imaginary settings, executed with great skill. Delicate pastel colours and masterly lighting have been used for the characters’ faces, and bolder black strokes to emphasise their outlines. The use of precious pigments, such as costly lapis lazuli, and of gold leaf (of which only microscopic fragments have survived) in the pictorial cycle is the obvious hallmark of a royal commission. The ceiling at Cefalù Cathedral includes iconographic themes and stylistic formulas extremely similar to the contemporaneous paintings on the ceiling of the Palatine Chapel but, unlike this latter, the paintings at Cefalù develop around a continuous band that is divided by medallions. The numerous images represented include animals, in particular the lion, the heraldic emblem of the patron’s family, the Altavilla. There are also ibis, peacocks, falcons, eagles, griffins, harts, antelopes, gazelles, elephants and camels. The eyes and marked expressions of the human figures in the cycle evoke knights, dreamers and drinkers. The paintings also include animal fights, hunting scenes and mythical creatures, such as the ‘merman’, half-man half-fish.  
The style of the paintings reveals an obvious Egyptian influence, as demonstrated by the comparison drawn by Aurigemma (2004) with a fragment of the wooden frieze from the palace built by the second Fatimid caliph (AH 364–86 / AD 975–96) for his daughter in Cairo, subsequently transferred to the rooms of the new palace of the Mamluk Sultan Qalawun (AH 678–89 / AD 1279–90). Nonetheless, the paintings at Cefalù have a greater variety of figurative models and greater compositional independence: the pictorial cycle can be entirely attributed to craftsmen from the same cultural milieu as the Palatine Chapel, probably including some artists from Egypt, who nonetheless introduced different influences from all over the Mediterranean basin and from Byzantine visual culture in particular. The trading of extremely varied, precious and, in some cases, very old ivory, metal and ceramic objects between the Norman court and the Fatimid kingdom would have provided the artists working on both Sicilian ceilings with additional figurative ideas.  
Like the paintings in the Palatine Chapel, these secular images in an ecclesiastical setting should be considered without resorting to symbolic–religious interpretations but rather as a celebration of the earthly pleasures enjoyed during the reign of Ruggero (Roger) II.

This pictorial cycle on the wooden boards of the ceiling can be attributed to craftsmen from the same cultural background as those who produced the Palatine Chapel. They probably included artists from Egypt, who brought a range of influences from throughout the Mediterranean basin, in particular Byzantine visual culture. The paintings can be understood to be a celebration of the earthly pleasures and joys enjoyed during the reign of Ruggero (Roger) II.
history: The cathedral at Cefalù was founded in 1131 by Ruggero II with the intention of making it a royal mausoleum for members of the Altavilla dynasty. To this end he had two porphyry sarcophaguses built and transferred to the cathedral before it was finished. They were placed in the chancel in 1145 before being moved to Palermo Cathedral by Frederick II of Swabia in 1215.
keywords: figurative decoration
partner: Regione Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

es.name: Techumbre de madera pintada de la Catedral de Cefalù.
description:
Los tableros de madera pintada de la techumbre de la Catedral de Cefalù muestran una serie de representaciones vívidas y de carácter profano de escenarios cortesanos, naturalistas e imaginarios, ejecutadas con gran maestría. Destacan delicados tonos pastel, una iluminación magistral para los rostros de los personajes y pinceladas negras más intensas para perfilar las figuras. El empleo de pigmentos valiosísimos en este ciclo pictórico, como el costoso lapislázuli o los panes de oro (de los que sólo se conservan fragmentos microscópicos), puede considerarse el sello distintivo de un encargo real. La techumbre incluye temas iconográficos y fórmulas estilísticas muy similares a las pinturas contemporáneas de la Capilla Palatina, aunque, a diferencia suya, las de Cefalù ocupan una franja continua estructurada en forma de medallones. Entre las numerosas representaciones hay animales, en particular el león, emblema heráldico de los Altavilla, la familia del patrocinador Ruggero II. También aparecen el ibis, el pavo real, el halcón, el águila, el grifo, el venado, el antílope, la gacela, el elefante y el camello. Entre las imágenes de seres humanos, de ojos y gestos de gran fuerza expresiva, aparecen caballeros, músicos y bebedores. Las pinturas también incluyen luchas entre animales, escenas de caza y criaturas míticas como el tritón, mitad hombre y mitad pez.  
El estilo de las pinturas denota una clara matriz egipcia, tal y como Aurigemma (2004) demuestra en la comparación que hizo con un fragmento del friso de madera que se halla en el palacio que el segundo califa fatimí (364-386 / 975-996) mandó construir para su hija en El Cairo, con el tiempo trasladado a las habitaciones del nuevo palacio del sultán mameluco Qalawun (678-689 / 1279-1290). No obstante, las pinturas de Cefalù presentan una mayor variedad de modelos figurativos y más originalidad en su composición. Así, el ciclo pictórico se puede atribuir perfectamente a artesanos que frecuentarían el mismo ambiente cultural que los de la Capilla Palatina. Entre ellos se contarían con toda probabilidad algunos artistas de Egipto, pero con distintas aportaciones procedentes de la cuenca mediterránea en general y de la cultura visual bizantina en particular. El intercambio de un amplísimo abanico de objetos preciosos de marfil, metal y cerámica, en ocasiones muy antiguos, entre la corte normanda y el reino fatimí habría suministrado a los artistas que trabajaron en ambos techos sicilianos nuevas ideas figurativas.  
Como en el caso de las pinturas de la Capilla Palatina, estas imágenes profanas en un escenario eclesiástico deberían analizarse prescindiendo de interpretaciones simbólico-religiosas y atendiendo más bien a la idea de celebración de los placeres terrenales de que se disfrutaba durante el reinado de Ruggero II.  
La catedral de Cefalù fue fundada en 1131 por Ruggero II con el propósito de convertirla en un mausoleo real para los miembros de la dinastía Altavilla. Con este fin mandó construir dos sarcófagos de pórfido e instalarlos en la catedral antes de que ésta estuviese terminada. Se colocaron en el coro de la iglesia en 1145 y, posteriormente, Federico II de Suevia ordenó su traslado a la catedral de Palermo en 1215.

El ciclo pictórico de esta techumbre puede atribuirse a artesanos que frecuentaban el mismo ambiente cultural que los de la Capilla Palatina, probablemente artistas procedentes de Egipto pero con diversas aportaciones de toda la cuenca mediterránea y de la tradición visual bizantina en particular.  
Hay que interpretar las pinturas como la exaltación de los placeres y los gozos terrenales bajo el dominio de Ruggero II.
keywords: decoración figurativa
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

fr.name: Plafond en bois peint de la cathédrale de Cefalù.
description:
Les panneaux de bois peint qui constituent le plafond de la cathédrale de Cefalù offrent une série de représentations à caractère profane concernant des thèmes courtois, naturalistes et fantastiques, réalisés avec un grand raffinement technique ; on a utilisé de délicates couleurs pastel, de savants rehauts pour dessiner les traits des personnages, des coups de pinceau noirs, plus énergiques, pour souligner le contour des silhouettes. L'utilisation de pigments précieux, tels le coûteux lapis-lazuli ou encore la feuille d'or, dont il ne subsiste que des traces microscopiques, permet d'attribuer sans hésitation ce cycle de peintures à une commande royale. Sur le plafond apparaissent des thèmes iconographiques et des éléments stylistiques présentant d'étroites analogies avec les peintures de plafond de la chapelle Palatine, de même époque. Mais les peintures se déploient ici sur une bande continue, constituée de médaillons ; parmi les nombreuses images représentées figurent des animaux, en particulier le lion, emblème héraldique des Hauteville, la famille du commanditaire. On trouve également l'ibis, le paon, le faucon, le griffon, le cerf, l'antilope, la gazelle, l'éléphant et le chameau. Parmi les images représentant des êtres humains, dont le regard et les attitudes sont très expressifs, figurent des chevaliers, des musiciens et des buveurs. On peut aussi admirer des combats opposant des animaux, des scènes de chasse et des monstres fantastiques comme la créature mi-homme, mi-poisson.  
  
Ces peintures révèlent une matrice stylistique clairement égyptienne : cela est démontré par la comparaison établie par Aurigemma (2004) entre le fragment de frise en bois, provenant du palais réalisé par le deuxième calife fatimide (364-386 H / 975-996 J.-C.) pour sa propre fille au Caire. Il fut inséré, par la suite, dans l'ensemble du nouveau palais du sultan mamelouk Qalawun (678-689 H / 1279-1290 J.-C.). On note cependant, à Cefalù, une plus grande variété dans le répertoire des modèles figuratifs, et davantage d'autonomie en matière de composition : ce cycle de peintures peut être pleinement attribué aux artisans appartenant au même milieu culturel que ceux de la chapelle Palatine, qui comprenait probablement des artistes provenant d'Égypte ainsi que d'autres apports, originaires de tout le bassin méditerranéen, et plus particulièrement de la culture visuelle byzantine. Les échanges d'objets précieux, en ivoire, en métal et en céramique (avec leur répertoire de modèles variés, et très anciens) entre la cour normande et le royaume fatimide fournirent probablement d'autres modèles figuratifs aux artistes qui travaillèrent à ces deux plafonds siciliens.  
  
Comme dans les peintures de la chapelle Palatine, ces représentations profanes, dans un cadre ecclésiastique, furent analysées avec le souci d'éviter les lectures à caractère symbolique et religieux ; on pourrait plutôt les interpréter comme la célébration des plaisirs et des joies terrestres, auxquels on pouvait goûter sous le règne de Roger II.  
  
La cathédrale de Cefalù fut fondée en 1131 par Roger II, dans le but d'en faire un mausolée royal pour les membres de la dynastie des Hauteville ; c'est dans cette intention qu'il fit exécuter, et transférer, dans l'ensemble en cours de construction, deux sarcophages en porphyre, placés en 1145 dans le chœur de l'église ; par la suite, ils furent déposés dans la cathédrale de Palerme par Frédéric II de Souabe, en 1215.

Ce cycle de peintures peut être attribué à des artisans appartenant au même milieu culturel que celui de la chapelle Palatine : il comprenait probablement des artistes provenant d'Égypte, mais avec des apports issus de tout le bassin méditerranéen, et de la culture visuelle byzantine en particulier.  
Les peintures peuvent être interprétées comme la célébration des plaisirs et des joies terrestres, sous le règne de Roger II.
keywords: décoration figurative
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

it.name: Soffitto ligneo dipinto della Cattedrale di Cefalù.
description: Le tavole lignee dipinte del soffitto della cattedrale di Cefalù presentano una serie di vivaci raffigurazioni di carattere profano, riguardanti temi cortesi, naturalistici e fantastici, realizzati con grande raffinatezza esecutiva: vi sono impiegati delicati colori pastello, sapienti lumeggiature per tratteggiare i volti dei personaggi, pennellate nere più energiche per sottolineare i contorni delle figure. L'uso di pigmenti preziosi, quali il costoso lapislazzuli, come pure della foglia d'oro, di cui restano solo microscopiche tracce, fa rientrare a pieno titolo questo ciclo pittorico nell'ambito di una committenza reale. Sul soffitto cefaludense compaiono temi iconografici e formule stilistiche che presentano stringenti analogie con le coeve pitture del soffitto della Cappella Palatina ma, a differenza di quest'ultimo, qui i dipinti si sviluppano in una struttura a fascia continua, articolata a medaglioni; tra le numerose immagini rappresentate figurano gli animali, ed in particolare il leone, emblema araldico degli Altavilla, la famiglia del committente Ruggero II. Vi sono inoltre l'ibis, il pavone, il falcone, l'aquila, il grifone, il cervo e l'antilope, la gazzella, l'elefante e il cammello. Tra le immagini di esseri umani, dagli occhi e dagli atteggiamenti di grande forza espressiva, compaiono cavalieri, suonatori e bevitori. Vi sono rappresentate, inoltre, lotte tra animali, scene di caccia e creature fantastiche, come il “sireno”, mezzo uomo e mezzo pesce. I dipinti rivelano una chiara matrice stilistica egiziana: lo dimostra il confronto istituito da Aurigemma (2004) con il frammento di fregio ligneo proveniente dal palazzo realizzato dal secondo califfo fatimide (364AH/975-386AH/996) per la propria figlia al Cairo, successivamente inserito negli ambienti del nuovo palazzo del sultano mamelucco Qalâwûn (678AH/1279-689AH/1290). Tuttavia a Cefalù si rileva una più ampia varietà nel repertorio dei modelli figurativi e anche una maggiore autonomia compositiva: il ciclo pittorico è pienamente ascrivibile a maestranze appartenenti allo stesso milieu culturale della Cappella Palatina, probabilmente comprendente anche artisti provenienti dall'Egitto, ma con diversi apporti, derivanti da tutto il bacino del Mediterraneo e dalla cultura visiva bizantina in particolare. Gli scambi di preziosi oggetti d'avorio, metallo e ceramica (con il loro variegatissimo repertorio di modelli, anche molto antichi) tra la corte normanna e il regno fatimide dovettero fornire probabilmente ulteriori spunti figurativi agli artisti attivi in entrambi i soffitti siciliani. Analogamente alle pitture della Cappella Palatina, queste rappresentazioni profane in ambito ecclesiastico andrebbero prese in esame evitando letture di carattere simbolico-religioso: sarebbero piuttosto interpretabili come la celebrazione dei piaceri e delle gioie terrene godute sotto il dominio di Ruggero II. La cattedrale di Cefalù venne fondata nel 1131 da Ruggero II con l'intenzione di farne un mausoleo reale per i membri della dinastia degli Altavilla: a tal fine fece eseguire, e trasferire nel complesso in costruzione, due sarcofaghi di porfido, collocati nel 1145 nel coro della chiesa ma poi traslati nella Cattedrale di Palermo da Federico II di Svevia nel 1215.

Il ciclo pittorico è ascrivibile a maestranze appartenenti allo stesso *milieu* culturale della Cappella Palatina, probabilmente comprendente artisti provenienti dall'Egitto, ma con diversi apporti da tutto il bacino del Mediterraneo e dalla cultura visiva bizantina in particolare.  
  
Le pitture sono interpretabili come la celebrazione dei piaceri e delle gioie terrene godute sotto il dominio di Ruggero II.
keywords: decorazione figurativa
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

description: Diese kleinen Handpauken wurden paarweise am Sattel des Pferdes befestigt und zu Beginn der Schlacht mit bloßen Händen oder kleinen Trommelschlägeln geschlagen. Der halbkugelige Korpus aus Bronze wurde mit einem dünnen Trommelfell aus Leder überzogen.

en.name: Drum
description: Small kettle drums like this one were used in pairs; attached to the saddle they were beaten by hand or with small drumsticks at the onset of the battle. Their semi-circular bronze corpus was covered with a leather drumhead.

en.name: Dar al-Batha (Batha Museum)
names: Pavillion of the Royal Palace in Fez
short_description: Dar al-Batha is the site of a large palace with two wings (east and west) and separate dwellings located at either side of a rectangular Andalusian-type garden (*riyadh*), which also surrounds the entire main palace. Within the palace are some large rectangular rooms that lead on to porches, at the corners of which are doors opening to outbuildings and annexes (*Douira*, sheds or *khzine*, etc.), and leading to the basement (now the Palace Museum) from which one can access the nearby Batha Square. Two side galleries (north and south) connect the two wings with the main house.
history: Although the foundations for the Palace of Dar el-Batha were laid during the reign of Mulay al-Hasan I, it was completed during the reign of Mulay ‘Abd al-‘Aziz in 1897. The palace was used for private meetings, receptions and sometimes as a summer residence. The Museum of Arts and Traditions of Fez and its region took over the palace in 1915 and, although the building was altered at this time, the outline of its plan has remained intact.
keywords: Palace; royal palace; public space; private space; garden; Islamic garden; gardens and architecture; Islamic city; Moroccan city; traditional city; urban space; urban planning; plan; house; traditional house; North African house; Moroccan architects; Islamic art; Islamic architecture; Islamic influence
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate for Cultural Heritage

en.name: Bowl
description: Abbasid ceramic production in Iraq indicates the significant impact of Chinese porcelain, found in numerous fragments throughout Mesopotamia. The plain elegance of this production is embodied in this small bowl, whose surface, entirely coated in white opaque glaze, is decorated simply by the phrase "work of Khalid" traced in elegant *kufic* characters with cobalt blue, painted directly over the glazing.
keywords: Ceramic; Abbasid; pottery; cobalt blue
materials: Earthenware, opaque white glaze, blue decoration
tags: Earthenware, opaque white glaze, blue decoration

it.name: Coppa
description: La ceramica abbaside dell'Iraq evidenzia il forte impatto della porcellana cinese, rinvenuta in numerosi frammenti in Mesopotamia. L'eleganza semplice di questa produzione è rappresentata da questa piccola coppa, la cui superficie, interamente ricoperta dalla vetrina bianca opaca, è decorata unicamente dalla frase "opera di Khalid" tracciata in bei caratteri cufici di colore blu cobalto dipinti direttamente sull'invetriatura.
keywords: Ceramica; abbaside

en.name: Yıldız Palace Small State Kiosk
short_description: Small State Kiosk was built in 1901 as the studying and resting kiosks upon the order of Sultan Abdulhamid II. The Sultan was holding official meetings here and it was used for the same purpose by the subsequent sultans. The two storied building has also a garret known as Winter Garden. The kiosk is famous for its ceiling decorations, the handrails decorated with flower branches in the form of elegant Art Nouveau and leaded windows bearing Bonet s signature. Sultan Abdulhamid II was informed about his dethronement in this kiosk. After his residence in Dolmabance Palace, Sultan Vahidettin settled in Yildiz Palace and made his interviews in this kiosk in the armistice period. Mustafa Kemal Ataturk also met Sultan Vahidettin for the last time on May 15th, 1919, in one of the room of this kiosk , before heading to Samsun with the title of 3rd Army Inspector.
history:
Yildiz Palace, which is the last architectural example of Turkish Ottoman palace, is located on the Yildiz hill in the district of Besiktas. Sultan Ahmed I was the first to build a pavilion, over this land registered at the time to the Private treasury of the Ottoman Sultan as a hunting place sultans beginning during the reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (1520-1566).  
The main construction in the palace started in the period of Sultan Abdulhamid II (1876-1909) and it was called Saray-i Humayun (Central palace). During this period the palace comprised of buildings for private use of the sultan as well as buildings, allocated for the officials, repair shops and carpentry like repairing shop, carpenter’s shop and the buildings of culture and art such as theatre, museum and library. The Palace begun to serve as a museum under the name of “Directorate of the Museum of Yildiz Palace since 1993.
keywords: Photography; Istanbul; History of architecture
partner: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (General Directorate for Cultural Heritage and Museums)

en.name: The Salting Carpet
description:
Dating from late sixteenth-century Iran, this is an extremely fine and beautiful carpet, with an intricate floral design filled with wild creatures, and verses of Persian poetry all around the borders, highlighted in metal brocade. The lines quote the great Iranian poet Hafez (d.1389), and they describe a blissful world of gardens, nightingales, roses and wine. This poetry was certainly chosen to suit the design and intended purpose of the carpet itself, to be a beautiful place to sit together with friends, in a private garden, reciting romantic verses: “Call for wine and scatter roses: what do you seek from Time?/ Thus spoke the rose at dawn. O nightingale, what say you?” The verses are emphasised by the scale of the fine calligraphy, by the use of silver brocade lettering against a dark red background, and by the distinctive formatting: each half-verse is placed in a cartouche, laid against a green border. The central medallion repeats the red and pink background, with a leafy design also overlaid with gleaming metal brocade.  
  
The central field of the carpet is filled with a rich floral landscape, organised in spiralling plant stems, with wonderfully large lotus flowers and leaves, all against a dark blue background. These are depicted to a more minute scale than the Persian poetry borders, and seem almost cramped. Among the foliage, there are perching green parrots and brown birds – these are presumably the nightingales from the poem. On closer inspection, the garden also contains Chinese-style dragons and lions (located in the four corners), and curling clouds which again echo Chinese design. One further detail rewards the careful observer: within many of the great blossoms and stems, the designer has hidden single animal heads.  
  
The carpet is attributed to the late sixteenth century, and the Safavid court of Iran (which was then based in Qazvin). At this time, carpet weaving had reached an extraordinarily high standard of design and technique, and the Safavid shahs commissioned the finest carpets as pious shrine donations, personal furnishings and suitably impressive diplomatic gifts to other states. This carpet has been linked with a very large group of royal gifts, sent by Shah Tahmasp to congratulate the newly-enthroned Ottoman Sultan Selim, in 1567. If confirmed, this account could explain an Istanbul provenance for this carpet, and many others like it.  
  
[V&A online catalogue link](http://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O54294/the-salting-carpet-carpet-unknown/)
type: Carpet; medallion carpet with Persian inscriptions in metal brocade
keywords: Iran; Safavid; gift; poetry; Hafez; parrots; birds; calligraphy; Persian
materials:
Wool; silk; silver; knotted pile; brocading.  
Wool pile on silk foundation, depressed warps, asymmetrical knots open to the left.

en.name: Carpet
description:
Carpets were one of the most important expressions of Persian art, especially during the reign of Shah ‘Abbas (1587‒1629), when they achieved the height of technical perfection and creative design. Made in leading workshops located in Tabriz, Kashan, Kerman and Isfahan, their floral and arabesque patterns with central medallions and figural scenes featuring animals contrasted with the geometric-designs that had characterised previous Persian carpets, as well as the Spanish and Turkish examples, which up until the mid-16th century had prevailed in Europe.  
These carpets were very expensive and usually had bigger dimensions when compared to their counterparts. This is the case for the large carpet fragment seen here, once part of a wide and impressive example measuring nearly six metres in length. Even though the two ends are now missing (they were cut off), the carpet still stands out for its extraordinary technical and artistic quality. One of its ends is currently in the Textile Museum in Washington, DC (Inv. No. R.33.4.6), after it was gifted by George Hewitt Meyers (1875‒1957); he, in turn, had purchased it from its previous, famous owner, the Armenian dealer of Islamic art, Dikran Kelekian (1868‒1951).  
The design of this “tree and animal” carpet combines the concept of the Persian pleasure garden with that of the royal hunting park. In addition, its wide-ranging palette, comprising 17 colours in total, shows the influence of Persian miniature painting. With a composition organised symmetrically, along its two centre lines, the field is made up of a small central medallion, with tall trees and flowering bushes inhabited by exotic birds and animals such as light brown lions and deer, blue *quilins* and multicoloured parrots. This is set against an elaborate network of scrolling vines, palmettes, blossoms, buds and leaves, on a red ground, which contrasts with the carpet’s emerald-green border.
keywords: Carpet; Iran; 16th century; Portugal
materials: Cotton, wool and silk; white silk warp; off-white cotton weft; wool knots 2Z; asymmetric knots, open to the left
tags: asymmetric knots, open to the left
partner: National Museum of Ancient Art ‒ MNAA

cs.name: Vstupní portál
description: V. Render a jeho dílna je autorem všech kamenických prací v interiéru i exteriéru. Do pětiosého zvlněného průčelí, prolamovaného nikami se sochami světců (D. Zürn, 1720) a okny, vnáší nakoso na bosovaných soklech postaveným sloupovím další prvek pohybu a napětí, v barokní architektuře na Moravě spíše ojedinělý. Toto řešení vzniklo jako součást celkového ikonografického programu univerzitního chrámu. Tordované sloupy evokují chrám Šalamounův, jehož zničení znamenalo ztrátu duchovního centra. Znovuvybudování chrámu bude znamením příchodu Spasitele, jehož symboly IHS nese kartuš nad vstupními dveřmi. Základním prvkem tohoto konceptu, jenž je synonymem moudrosti, je sepjetí světské a duchovní moci a její obnova po náboženských rozkolech.

en.name: Entrance portal
description: V. Render and his workshop executed all the stonemasonry for both the exterior and interior. Columns on pedestals bring an element of movement and suspense – rather rare in Moravian Baroque architecture – to the five-axis, undulating frontage, broken by windows and niches within which are statues of the saints (D. Zürn, 1720). The approach was part of a comprehensive iconographic programme for the university church. Columns in the frontage evoke the Temple of Solomon. Set in a cartouche is the Jesuit trigram: *IHS*, indicating also the coming of the Saviour. The principal element of the concept, synonymous with wisdom, is the union of the secular and spiritual, and its restoration after religious schisms.

ar.name: مقلمة
description:
تم تزيين علبة الأقلام بزخرفة مميزة تتكون من أنماط غير محددة المعالم تشبه أوراق الشجر ومتشابكة معًا. تذكرنا في مجملها بالأشكال الحلزونية ( الولبية). ثلاث خراطيش نحاسية اللون مرتفعة قليلاً "تطفو" فوق هذه الأرضية ذات اللون الأصفر المخضر. وهي مليئة بزخارف متموجة تشبه شكل الضفيرة المعروفة لدى صاغة الذهب الأوروبيين.  
وعلى حد علمنا ، فقد طور رجب علي هذه الزخرفة في النصف الأول من القرن التاسع عشر، ثم اتخذ أبو طالب هذا الأسلوب فيما بعد وجعله مشهوراً. ربما تكون علبة الأقلام هذه صنعت من قبل ناسخ.  
وبحسب النقش الموجود في الأعلى، فإن هذا العمل قد صنع بطلب رجل يدعى حسن.

tags: ورق معجن ، ألوان مائية غير شفافة ، ورنيش

en.name: Pencase
description:
The pencase is adorned with a characteristic decoration consisting of amorphous, leaf-like structures that are entwined together. In their entirety, they are reminiscent of spiral tendrils. Three slightly raised, copper-coloured cartouches “float” on top of this greenish-yellow ground. They are filled with a wave decoration that resembles the guilloche pattern of European goldsmiths.  
  
As far as we know today, this decoration was developed by Rajab ʿAli in the first half of the 19th century, with Abu Talib later taking up the style and making it famous. The pencase exhibited here was probably made by a copyist.  
  
According to an inscription on the top, the work was ordered by a man named Hasan.

en.name: Church of St. Jerome
description: The Pauline Church of St. Jerome was built in Štrigova near Čakovec in Croatia, a place thought to be the birthplace of St. Jerome, one of the Pauline order's most celebrated saints. The church relates stylistically to Styrian architecture, for example, the Church of Maria Trost in Graz, seen clearly in the trefoil presbytery, above which rises a dome divided by radial sections, and the façade with two Baroque bell towers. The exquisite frescos in the sanctuary are the work of Ivan Krstitelj Ranger (1744); the high altar the work of the Baroque sculptor, Joseph Weinacht, one of only a few sculptors who lived in Zagreb in the first half of the 18th century. The high altar is a most unusual work in Joseph Weinacht's opus, and is one of only a few carved-wood retables in the form of a large monstrance. The altar tabernacle – decorated with the figurative reliefs – appears compact, while the construction above *St. Jerome* takes the form of golden radials shining through a garland of stylised clouds. St. Jerome stands in the foreground surrounded by angels holding attributes and inscriptions in their hands.

The ground plan of the Pauline Church of St. Jerome consists of two different units: an almost square single nave and a trefoil presbytery surmounted by a dome. With two Baroque bell towers flanking the façade, the church is a powerful architectural statement. The Pauline lay-brother painter, Ivan Krstitelj Ranger, decorated the presbytery with ceiling paintings. The Baroque sculptor, Joseph Weinacht from Zagreb, constructed the high altar in 1747.
artist: Painter: Ivan Krstitelj (Johann Baptist) Ranger (1700–1753); sculptor: Joseph Weinacht (active: 1744–1750s)
history: In around 1738, the Pauline monks built a new church dedicated to St. Jerome. Built on the site of the former monastery of St. Helen in Strigova near Čakovec in Croatia, it became the centre of the Pauline order there, as it was thought to be the birthplace of the Pauline philosopher and hermit, St Jerome.
keywords: Baroque, Pauline church, trefoil presbytery, Ivan Krstitelj Ranger, Joseph Weinacht
tags: Baroque, Pauline church, trefoil presbytery, Ivan Krstitelj Ranger, Joseph Weinacht
