en.name: Emperor Akbar Receiving a Book
description:
The emperor is seated with pillow at his back upon an octagonal-shaped and portable throne, under a canopy and at the foot of a tree in an open field. A poet or *mullah* (Muslim priest) presents him with a book. The throne rests upon a floral- patterned Mughal carpet spread over a platform. The emperor is attended by two of his courtiers, two musicians, one with *sitar* (stringed instrument) and one with tambourine; by his falconer who holds a large falcon in his right hand; by an attendant to right of falconer and one to the left, the latter holding a staff; and near him is another mullah. The last four are only partially seen at the base of the platform. The emperor is fanned by a figure behind him. To the immediate left of the emperor stands a servant with a fly-whisk and another holding an unidentified object. All the personages on the carpet except the *mullah* and the two servants are seated. Just above the step to the platform is a dish with a bottle possibly for water with leaf sprays issuing from the mouth, a cup nearby, and at the left corner, a covered cup.  
In the landscape, which extends back to the horizon line, there are two trees and a flowering bush. In the larger tree behind the emperor are two birds. On the horizon line, which is hilly, there is an open wood in the midst of which is a castle.  
The painting is glued down on a thick matboard. The borders (frames) are on a separate piece of paper.
keywords: Emperor; Akbar; Book; Drawing; Watercolor; Ink; Gold; Paper; India; Indian; Asia; watercolour
materials: Ink, opaque watercolor, gold on paper
tags: Ink, opaque watercolor, gold on paper

en.name: Vat
description:
Globular vat with a conical base, a flaring neck, a flanged rim and winged handles. The paste is whitish and unglazed. Its decoration consists of a stamped, alternating series of lozenges and eulogetic epigraphy arranged in perimeter friezes.  
  
A common feature of Andalusian homes, these large earthenware vats were strategically placed in the courtyards or in interior rooms to preserve goods such as oil, cereals, or water, as well as to store domestic objects. In this case, the porous nature of the unglazed clay suggests that this example functioned specifically as a water vat, as it would have filtered and cooled the water, keeping it clean and fresh.  
  
Beyond their practical function, some vats had also an aesthetic value, as can be seen in the stamped decoration or glazing. Decorations included epigraphic motifs invoked to protect the vats' contents. The production and use of these vats continued after the Castilian conquest.
keywords: Water; Technology; Conservation; Household goods; Prophylactic practices

en.name: Fountain of the Rivers
description:
The idea of adorning the fountain with the depiction of four river gods was Borromini's. However, another possible model could have been offered to Bernini by the fountain in Villa Lante in Bagnaia (Viterbo). Images of river gods depicted as colossal, bearded figures lying down abounded in Rome (among the most famous the Tiber, the Nile and the Marforio in the Campidoglio and again the Tiber, the Arno and the Nile in the Cortile del Belvedere in the Vatican). Despite those ancient models, Bernini would eventually rely on classic iconography only in the statue depicting the Ganges: the other three, seated and captured in dramatic actions, are instead closer to Renaissance models such as the Ocean Fountain of the Boboli Gardens (Florence) by Giambologna, or the statues of chained slaves placed at the base of the Monument to Ferdinand I of Tuscany, in Livorno, by Pietro Tacca. Some drawings made by Bernini, as well as the models made in wood and terracotta (Museo Civico di Bologna, Galleria Giorgio Franchetti alla Ca’ d’Oro in Venice) illustrate the different design phases of the fountain. The execution of the statues (which took place between February 1650 and July 1651) was entrusted to the collaborators of the master: Antonio Raggi sculpted the Danube, Jacopo Antonio Fancelli the Nile (his face covered to symbolize the then unknown location of its source), Claude Poussin the Ganges and Francesco Baratta the Rio de la Plata. The final touches to the rock, palm, horse and lion were given by Bernini himself.  
The Pamphili dove, eloquently placed on the top of the obelisk of Domitian, in turn soaring over the rocks, symbolizes the dominion of the papacy over the natural elements and over the four known continents (Asia, Europe, Africa and America represented respectively by the Ganges, Danube, Nile and Rio de la Plata). In this way the fountain became the spectacular fulcrum of the square, eternalizing in the stone the 17th century tradition of setting up sumptuous and ephemeral apparatuses dedicated to various entertainments, such as horse carriage races and staged square floods. Those traditions referred to the games that were held in ancient times in the stadium of Domitian, on which Piazza Navona was built.

Thanks to the Fountain of the Four Rivers Bernini, gained the admiration and protection of Pope Innocent X. It recalls the temporary *apparati* created at the Baroque time for festivals, mostly set in piazza Navona.
artist: Gian Lorenzo Bernini (design); Francesco Baratta; Claude Poussin; Antonio Raggi; Jacopo Antonio Fancelli
history:
Pope Innocent X Pamphili had decided to give prestige to his family by having Francesco Borromini design the new facade of the building on Piazza Navona (1644–50) and having the small Church of Sant’Agnese rebuilt from scratch to transform it into the family mausoleum. Borromini had also been commissioned to design a third fountain to be placed in the centre of the square, with the water provided by the Aqua Virgo aqueducts like the two pre-existing fountains. For the occasion, the architect from Ticino provided the design of a fountain surmounted by an obelisk (from the Circus of Maxentius, on the Appian Way) and with four figures of river gods. However, in the meanwhile Prince Niccolò Ludovisi, nephew of the pope and a great admirer of Gian Lorenzo Bernini, proposed to the artist to create a model for the fountain to be submitted to the attention of the pope.  
Bernini made the silver model (now lost) which, thanks to the mediation of Donna Olimpia, the pope’s sister-in-law, was shown to Innocent X who was so fascinated that he immediately commissioned the prestigious work to Bernini.

it.name: Fontana dei Quattro Fiumi
description:
L'idea di realizzare la fontana adorna di quattro divinità fluviali era già stata di Borromini. Tuttavia un altro possibile modello poteva essere stato offerto a Bernini dalla fontana della villa Lante a Bagnaia. Immagini di divinità fluviali raffigurate come colossali figure barbute sdraiate abbondavano a Roma (tra le più celebri il *Tevere*, il *Nilo*, il *Marforio* in Campidoglio e ancora il *Tevere*, l'*Arno*, il *Nilo* nel Cortile del Belvedere in Vaticano). Tuttavia Bernini avrebbe ripreso quell'iconografia classica solo nella statua raffigurante il Gange: le altre tre, sedute e colte in azioni drammatiche, sono invece prossime a modelli rinascimentali come la *Fontana dell'Oceano* del Giardino di Boboli (Firenze) di Giambologna, o le statue di schiavi incatenati posti alla base del *Monumento a Ferdinando I di Toscana*, a Livorno, di Pietro Tacca.  
Alcuni disegni eseguiti da Bernini illustrano le diverse fase progettuali della fontana come pure i modelli realizzati in legno e terracotta (Museo Civico di Bologna, Museo della Cà d'Oro di Venezia).  
L'esecuzione delle statue (avvenuta tra il febbraio 1650 e il luglio 1651) venne affidata ai collaboratori del maestro: Antonio Raggi scolpì il *Danubio*, Jacopo Antonio Fancelli il *Nilo* (con il volto coperto a simboleggiare l'allora ignota ubicazione della sua sorgente), Claude Poussin il *Gange* e Francesco Baratta il *Rio de la Plata*. I ritocchi finali alla roccia, alla palma, al cavallo e al leone vennero dati dal Bernini stesso.  
In modo molto eloquente, la colomba dei Pamphili posta sulla sommità dell'obelisco di Domiziano, a sua volta collocato e reso svettante dalla montagna rocciosa traforata, simboleggia il dominio del papato sugli elementi naturali e sui quattro continenti allora conosciuti (l'Asia, l'Europa, l'Africa e l'America rappresentate rispettivamente da Gange, Danubio, Nilo e Rio de la Plata).  
La fontana diveniva in questo modo lo scenografico perno della piazza, eternando nella pietra la tradizione degli sfarzosi apparati effimeri allestiti nel Seicento in quel sito deputato a divertimenti vari, quali le corse di carrozze e gli allagamenti della piazza: un richiamo ai giochi che si tenevano nell'antichità nello stadio di Domiziano su cui era sorta piazza Navona.

La fontana raffigura i quattro fiumi simboleggianti i quattro continenti allora conosciuti su cui regna il papato di Innocenzo X Pamphili, rappresentato dall’obelisco egizio su cui svettano la croce e gli emblemi di famiglia. Si ispira agli spettacolari apparati effimeri in legno, gesso e cartapesta che Bernini stesso disegnò per svariate celebrazioni.
artist: Gian Lorenzo Bernini (ideazione); Francesco Baratta; Claude Poussin; Antonio Raggi; Jacopo Antonio Fancelli
history: Innocenzo X Pamphili aveva deciso di dar lustro alla propria famiglia facendo realizzare a Francesco Borromini la nuova facciata del palazzo su piazza Navona (1644-50) e facendo ricostruire ex novo la piccola chiesa di Sant’Agnese per trasformarla nel mausoleo di famiglia. Borromini era anche stato incaricato di provvedere alla creazione di una terza fontana da porsi al centro della piazza, alimentata dall’Acquedotto Vergine al pari delle due preesistenti. Per l’occasione, l’architetto ticinese fornì il disegno di una fontana sormontata da un obelisco (proveniente dal Circo di Massenzio, sulla via Appia) con quattro figure di divinità fluviali. Frattanto il principe Niccolò Ludovisi, nipote del papa e grande ammiratore di Bernini, proponeva all’artista di realizzare un modello per la fontana da sottoporre all’attenzione del pontefice. Bernini realizzò il modelletto in argento (ora perduto) che, grazie alla mediazione di Donna Olimpia, cognata del papa, fu mostrato a Innocenzo X che ne rimase a tal punto conquistato da commissionargli immediatamente la prestigiosa impresa.
keywords: Acqua; fontana; feste; esotismo; Antico

en.name: Brocade Rug
description:
The decorations on 17th-century Cuenca rugs were inspired by patterns from 16th-century silk textiles and rugs. The Spanish rug in the Museum of Applied Arts’ collection belongs to the Brocade series. The field contains large, stylised palmettes in an axially symmetrical arrangement/composition on a blue ground. A vertical series of palmettes, each surmounted by a crown, runs along the central axis of the long, narrow rug and is enclosed by inclined palmettes. These are decorated with ivory, orange, light blue and green floral elements on a pale-yellow ground. The blue ground of the field is filled with a row of tiny, four-petalled rosettes. The border contains a chain created by horizontal "S" motifs connected by rings on a pale-yellow ground.  
  
At one time, lawyer Alfréd Perlmutter (1867–1929) also owned similarly decorated Spanish rug in Budapest. The whereabouts of the 520cm x 220cm rug are unknown; an photo of a detail of the rug can be found in the archives of the Museum of Applied Arts.  
  
A more richly patterned and larger version of this rug type can be found in the National Museum of Decorative Arts in Madrid (see Related Objects).
keywords: European rug; Hemp; Spanish rug; Wool
materials: Warp and pile: Wool; Weft: Hemp; Spanish knot

ar.name: بطاقات بريدية رسمية للخط الحديدي الحجازي
description: في عام 1900 بدأ السلطان العثماني عبد الحميد الثاني (حكم خلال 1876 – 1909 ) في إنشاء خط سكة حديدية يربط دمشق بالمدن المقدسة في الحجاز كالمدينة ومكة. وقد أنشأ هذا الخط بمشاركة من الجهات العامة ودعوة للعالم الإسلامي للدعم المالي وقد وصل خط السكة الحديدية للمدينة عام 1908 ولكنه لم يصل لمكة. وتمويل خط سكة الحديد الحجازي كان يراد به مبدئيا أن يأتي كليا من التبرعات الخيرية وفي مايو عام 1900 بدأ السلطان عبد الحميد العملية بتبرع سخي من أمواله الخاصة. بالرغم من السخاء الوطني والأجنبي تجاه حملة التبرعات فقد أصبح سريعا من الواضح أن هذا لوحده غير كاف لتأمين التمويل اللازم للإنشاء. وبالتالي سعت الحكومة لتأمين التمويل بعدة طرق أخرى التي تتضمن إصدار بطاقات بريدية من ضمن المنتجات الأخرى ألمانية الصنع من أجل تحقيق عائد أكبر. وتحت عنوان (منظر لسكة الحديد الحميدية  الحجازي ) وبعبارات مكتوبة بالفرنسية والتركية فقد صورت البطاقات البريدية إنشاء الخط الحديدي وأيضا المناظر العامة واحتفالات التدشين  /الافتتاح. وهذه كانت متوفرة للشراء في مكاتب البريد المحلية.

en.name: Official Hijaz Railway postcards
description: In 1900 the Ottoman Sultan Abdülhamid II (r.1876–1909) began the construction of a railway line connecting Damascus to the holy cities of Medina and Mecca. Built by public subscription and with an appeal to Muslims of the world for financial support, the railway line began from Damascus and reached Medina in 1908, never reaching Mecca. The financing for the Hijaz Railway was initially meant to come entirely from charitable donations and in May 1900 Sultan Abdülhamid II began the process with a sizeable donation from his personal funds. Despite national and foreign generosity towards the donations campaign, it soon became clear that this alone was insufficient to raise the funds needed for the construction. Therefore, the government sought to raise funds in many other ways, including the commission of postcards amongst other German-made products, in order to generate further yield. With the title ‘*Vue du chemin-de-fer Hamidié de Hedjaz*’ and with labels in French and Turkish, the postcards depict the construction of the Railway as well as general views and inauguration celebrations. These were available for purchase at local post offices.
holder: Khalili Family Trust – Hajj and the Arts of Pilgrimage Collection
keywords: Engineering; Hajj; Hijaz; Hijaz railway; Holy place; Ka'ba; Medina; Mosque; paper; Pilgrimage; Pilgrimage route; Prayer; Prophet Muhammad; Religion; Travel; Mecca

en.name: Çakırağa Mansion
short_description: This private mansion is one of the most authentic surviving examples of an Anatolian Turkish house with its layout and painted and woodwork decoration. This monumental mansion is three-storeyed and has a courtyard-garden. The ground floor, which is paved with stone plaques, is given over to service rooms. The living quarters on the upper two floors have an outer *sofa*. Among the wall paintings on the exterior and interior walls of the structure are noteworthy panoramas of Istanbul and Izmir. The wooden ceilings and cupboards have remarkable decoration. The structure has been open to public as a museum since 1995.
keywords: Birgi; Ödemiş; house; mansion; sofa (hayat); decoration; wall painting; woodwork; ceiling decoration; vegetal decoration; geometric decoration; landscape; architectural compositions; still life; trompe l’oeil

short_description: Frieze of ram heads from South Arabia found by Eduard Glaser during one of his four expeditions in Yemen from 1882 to 1894.

ar.name: حوض
description: إن الأواني اليومية المستخدمة في العصر الفاطمي كانت تصنع من خليطة النحاس مثل هذا الحوض. والشكل المخروطي الذي يذكر بالأوعية المتأخرة الغابرة ذات الشكل المشابه التي  كانت مصنوعة من المعادن النفيسة استمر استخدامها في الخزف الإسلامي والمشغولات المعدنية بعد القرن الثاني عشر. ويتالف التزيين من صف مزدوج من النقوش الكوفية المتبادلة التي تعبر عن أمنيات طيبة لمالك القطعة وهي مزخرفة بلفات وأشكال قلوب.

el.name: Λεκάνη
description:
Τα αντικείμενα καθημερινής χρήσης της φατιμιδικής περιόδου κατασκευάζονταν από κράμα χαλκού. Το κωνικό σχήμα της λεκάνης που θυμίζει αντίστοιχα σκεύη της ύστερης αρχαιότητας από πολύτιμο υλικό, συνεχίζει να χρησιμοποιείται στην ισλαμική κεραμική και μεταλλοτεχνία μετά τον 12ο αιώνα.  
Ο διάκοσμος σχηματίζεται από διπλή σειρά κουφικών επιγραφών –που τοποθετούνται πλάτη με πλάτη σαν να καθρεφτίζονται η μία στην άλλη- με ευχές για τον ιδιοκτήτη καθώς και καρδιόσχημα κοσμήματα και βλαστούς.

en.name: Basin
description: Everyday utensils used in the Fatimid period were made of cast copper alloy as this basin. The conical shape, which recalls late-antique vessels of similar shape made of precious metals, continued to be used in Islamic ceramics and metalwork after the 12th century. The decoration consists of a double row of reciprocating *kufic* inscriptions that express good wishes to the owner and is further adorned with scrolls and heart shapes.
keywords: Basin; Kufic; Metalwork

ar.name: إبريق وضوء.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن إبريق أسطواني الشكل مصنوع من البرونز، ليس له مقبض، وله عنق طويل. الإبريق مقسم إلى جزءين غير متساويين بواسطة شريط مزخرف. البدن أسطواني الشكل غير مزخرف، بينما الكتف مقسم إلى أشرطة ضيقة مملوءة بخطوط عمودية قصيرة.  
  
ربما كان الإبريق يستخدم وعاءً للوضوء للصلاة، إذ أن كثيراً من الأواني المعدنية والفخارية كانت ذات صلة بهذا النوع من الطقوس. هذا الإبريق بالتحديد عُثر عليه خلال التنقيبات الأثرية في حمام القصر الأموي في أم الوليد.
جرة برونزية مُرصَّصة، بلا يد، ومصنوعة من أربع قطع ملحومة. عُثر عليها في أثناء التنقيب في حمامات القصر الأموي في أم الوليد، ربما كانت تستخدم للوضوء قبل الصلاة.
keywords: آنية معدنية؛ وضوء؛ وعاء معدني.

en.name: Ablution jug.
description:
A cylindrical jug of leaded bronze without a handle and with a tall neck divided into two unequal parts by a decorative 'rope' band. The cylindrical body is plain, although the shoulder is divided into narrow bands that are filled with short vertical strokes.  
  
This vessel may once have been used as an ablution jug for ritual washing before prayer; many other such metal and ceramic jugs have been found associated with this ritual. This particular jug was found during archaeological excavations in the hammam that was part of the qasr (palace) at Umm al-Walid.

A jug of leaded bronze, without a handle and made from four parts welded together. Found during excavations at the baths of the Umayyad qasr at Umm al-Walid, it may have been used as an ablution jug for ritual washing before prayer.
holder: Now on display at Jordan Museum
keywords: Ablution; metalwork
materials: Leaded bronze; four parts joined together.

es.name: Vasija para abluciones
description:
Vasija cilíndrica de bronce y plomo, sin asas y con un cuello largo dividido en dos partes desiguales por una banda decorativa que imita una cuerda. La parte cilíndrica del cuerpo carece de ornamentación, pero la zona superior que la une con el cuello está dividida en bandas estrechas adornadas con trazos verticales.  
Este recipiente debió de utilizarse para el agua de las abluciones rituales previas a la oración. Se han encontrado numerosas vasijas metálicas y de cerámica destinadas a este uso. Esta en concreto fue hallada en el transcurso de unas excavaciones realizadas en el *hammam* que formaba parte del *qasr* (alcázar) de Umm al-Walid.

Vasija sin asas, de bronce y plomo, formada por cuatro partes soldadas entre sí. Se encontró durante unas excavaciones en los baños del *qasr* omeya de Umm al-Walid y debió de emplearse para abluciones o baños rituales previos a la oración.
dates: Siglo II de la Hégira / VIII d. C.
keywords: Ablución; metalistería; lavado ritual.
materials: Bronce y plomo; cuatro piezas unidas.

fr.name: Jarre à ablutions.
description:
Jarre cylindrique en bronze (cuivre et plomb) sans poignée et col court divisée en deux parties inégales par un “cordon” décoratif. La panse cylindrique est sans ornement, mais l'épaule est ornée d'étroits bandeaux meublés de petits traits verticaux.  
Ce récipient a pu être utilisé jadis comme jarre à ablutions pour la toilette rituelle qui précède la prière. De nombreuses autres jarres en métal ou céramique d'usage similaire ont été trouvées. Ce modèle particulier a été découvert lors de fouilles archéologiques dans le *hammam* du *qasr* (palais) d'Oum al-Walid.

Jarre en fonte de bronze, sans poignée et constituée de quatre parties assemblées entre elles. Découverte pendant les fouilles archéologiques dans le *hammam* du *qasr*omeyyade d’Oum-al-Walid, cette jarre a pu être utilisée comme jarre à ablutions pour la toilette rituelle qui précède la prière.
dates: IIe siècle de l’Hégire (VIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: ablutions ; travail du métal ; toilette rituelle
materials: Bronze (cuivre et plomb) ; montage en quatre parties.

ar.name: الحي العربي.
description:
الحي العربي في سامبوكا نشأ حول القلعة في القسم المرتفع من التل، ومازال محافظاً على صفات مخططه الأصلي؛ وهو مجموعات من المنازل المتلاصقة التي تختلف عن بقية أحياء المدينة. لكل منزل حديقة، يختلف شكلها عن الحدائق الأخرى (مرفق، ممر، حربة....) ويفصل بين المجموعات أزقة ملتوية ومتشعبة، كما غطي القسم الأكبر منها بأقواس، وصُنع لبعضها أبواب. يحيط بالحي سور له ثلاثة أبراج مراقبة، بقي منها برج أقيم فيه جرس الكنيسة الأم.  
أمر الأمير منكود ببناء هذا الحي في سامبوكا، وتقول المعلومات التي ذكرها الإدريسي والباحثون الصقليون إن هناك قلعة أخرى، أنشئت على طرف تلة سامبوكا في سنة (441هـ / 1050 تقريباً) لحماية المنطقة، وقد تم هدمها كلها.

ينتظم الحي داخل محيط  مثلثي؛ ويتخذ شكل مجموعة من البنايات السكنية المتماسكة جدا والمختلفة تماما عن باقي المركز الحضري. يتميز هذا الحي بصحون مختلفة النماذج (ملتوية، وعلى شكل مذراة وحربة وكُلاب)، ونسيج طرقي غير منتظم يتكون من أزقة مغطاة في أغلب الأحيان، أو مؤطرة بعقود مرور فقط. ويُدين مسكن سامبوكا بأصله للأمير ابن منقذ حسب رواية مؤكدة من قبل الإدريسي، ولاحقا من قبل مؤرخين صقليين.
keywords: تمدن.
partner: Regiona Siciliana, Assessorato ai Beni Culturali

en.name: Arab Quarter.
description: The Arab Quarter in Sambuca, built around the castle at the top of the hill, still retains its original layout, with its road network and densely packed houses still intact. The quarter fits within a triangular area and is an extremely compact collection of buildings. It is easily distinguishable from the rest of the urban area with its variety of courtyards (elbow-, fork-, bayonet- and hook-shaped) and its irregular road system consisting of lanes, most of which are covered or simply framed with entrance arches. The Arab Quarter was surrounded by a wall with three towers. The only surviving tower now forms part of the bell tower of the mother church.

The triangular Arab quarter is a compact group of buildings easily distinguished from the rest of the town centre by its variety of courtyard shapes (such as elbow, fork, bayonet and hook) and its irregular road system, in which most streets are covered or at least accessed through an archway. Sambuca owes its existence to the Amir Ibn Mankud, according to a tradition confirmed by al-Idrisi and later Sicilian historians.
history: According to tradition, Sambuca owes its existence to the Amir ibn Mankud, and this is confirmed by al-Idrisi and later Sicilian sources. Around AH 441 / AD 1050 a castle was built on top of the hill to defend the town. It has since been demolished.
keywords: town planning

es.name: Barrio árabe.
description:
El barrio árabe de Sambuca, edificado alrededor del castillo en la parte alta del cerro, aún mantiene su trazado original, conservando intacto el tejido viario y el sistema de aglutinamiento de las viviendas individuales. El barrio se inscribe en un perímetro triangular y se presenta como un compacto conglomerado de viviendas. Se diferencia fácilmente del resto del centro urbano por su variedad de patios (en recodo, en horca, en bayoneta, en garfio, etc.) y por su tejido viario irregular constituido por callejuelas, muchas de ellas cubiertas o sencillamente enmarcadas por arcos de entrada. El barrio árabe estaba circundado por un muro con tres torres. La única torre que se conserva forma parte de la torre del campanario de la iglesia matriz.  
El pueblo de Sambuca debe su origen al emir Ibn Mankud, según una tradición confirmada por al Idrisi y por historiadores sicilianos posteriores. Hacia 441 / 1050, para defender el centro, se edificó en la cima de la colina un castillo posteriormente demolido.

El barrio se inscribe en un perímetro triangular y se presenta como un conglomerado de viviendas muy compacto y diferenciado del resto del centro urbano. Se caracteriza por sus variados patios (en recodo, en horca, en bayoneta, en garfio, etc.) y por un tejido viario irregular, constituido por callejuelas en gran parte cubiertas o más sencillamente encuadradas por arcos de entrada. El pueblo de Sambuca debe su origen al emir Ibn Mankud, según una tradición confirmada por al-Idrisi y por historiadores sicilianos posteriores.

fr.name: Quartier arabe.
description:
Le quartier arabe de Sambuca, qui s'est développé autour du château, sur la partie haute de la colline, présente, encore aujourd'hui, les caractères de l'implantation d'origine, conservant intact le tracé des rues et le système d'agrégation des unités d'habitation. Le quartier s'inscrit à l'intérieur d'un périmètre triangulaire et se présente comme une agrégation urbaine très compacte, bien distincte du centre urbain : elle se caractérise par des cours de typologie variable (en forme de coude, de fourche, de baïonnette, de crochet, etc.) et un tissu viaire irrégulier, constitué de ruelles souvent couvertes, ou plus simplement encadrées d'arches d'accès. Le quartier était entouré d'un rempart muni de trois tours, dont la seule subsistante a été englobée dans le campanile de la Chiesa Madre.  
  
L'habitat de Sambuca doit son origine à l'émir Ibn Mankud, selon une tradition confirmée par al-Idrisi, et par des historiens siciliens postérieurs à ce dernier. Afin de défendre le centre, on édifia au sommet de la colline, vers 441 H / 1050 J.-C., un château qui fut démoli par la suite.

Le quartier s'inscrit dans un périmètre triangulaire et se présente comme un agrégat d'habitations, très compact et bien distinct du reste du centre urbain : il se distingue par des cours de diverses typologies (coudées, en forme de fourche, de baïonnette, de crochet) et un tissu viaire irrégulier, constitué de ruelles souvent couvertes ou simplement encadrées par des arcs d'accès. L'habitat de Sambuca doit son origine à l'émir Ibn Mankud, selon une tradition confirmée par al-Idrisi et, plus tard, par des historiens siciliens.

it.name: Quartiere arabo.
description: Il quartiere arabo di Sambuca, sviluppatosi attorno al castello, nella parte alta della collina, presenta ancor oggi i caratteri dell'impianto originario, conservando intatto il proprio tessuto viario e il sistema aggregativo delle singole cellule abitative. Il quartiere è circoscrivibile in un perimetro triangolare e si presenta come una aggregazione edilizia molto compatta e ben riconoscibile dal resto del centro urbano: lo distinguono i cortili di varia tipologia (a gomito, a forca, a baionetta, a uncino, etc) e un tessuto viario irregolare, costituito da vicoli in gran parte coperti o più semplicemente inquadrati da archi di accesso. Circondava il quartiere un perimetro murato, provvisto di tre torri, delle quali l'unica superstite è stata inglobata nel campanile della chiesa madre. L'abitato di Sambuca deve la sua origine all'emiro Ibn Mankud, secondo una tradizione confermata da Al-Idrîsî e dai più tardi storici siciliani. A difesa del centro, sulla sommità della collina fu edificato verso il 441 AH/1050 un castello, successivamente demolito.

en.name: Water mills
description:
Water mills, locally known as *maṭḥana*, date back to the AH 5th-16th / AD 11th–12th centuries during the Almoravid and Almohad dynasties. They played a vital role in Morocco’s rural and agricultural history, supporting traditional economies where farming was the main livelihood. These dynasties promoted the development of hydraulic infrastructure and the rational use of water in both cities and countryside.  
The concept of the water mill was not new, but it was refined in Morocco through the blending of Berber, Andalusian, and Eastern influences, enriching local know-how in construction, hydraulics, and community organisation.  
Built in rural regions near rivers and irrigation canals, these mills harnessed the power of flowing water to grind cereals such as wheat, barley, and corn: staples of Moroccan agriculture. Water was diverted through a small canal or pipe to a horizontal wheel, typically wooden or metal, which rotated and turned the upper stone. This efficient system turned grains into flour—an important step in preparing bread, the cornerstone of the Moroccan diet.  
In Morocco’s semi-arid climate, water management was always crucial to the survival of communities. Water mills were often integrated into larger hydraulic systems, linked to khettaras (traditional underground canals), norias (water wheels), dams, and retention basins. Beyond their agricultural function, water mills had a social and religious dimension. They might be incorporated into waqfs or habous (religious endowments), whose revenues were used to fund mosques, Quranic schools (madrasas), or hostels for travellers. The miller, often a respected figure in the village, played the role of mediator and overseer in ensuring fair access to milling services. More than functional structures, these mills served as social hubs and symbols of cooperation, sustainability, and spiritual value.  
With the advent of modern industry and the introduction of electric mills in the AH 16th / AD 20th century, the use of traditional water mills gradually declined. Some survive in mountainous areas, such as the Middle Atlas, or in remote regions of the Rif and Souss, preserved as part of Morocco’s cultural heritage. These mills stand as evidence of Moroccan hydraulic genius, of the ability of rural societies to adapt to their environment, and of the harmonious integration of nature, technology, and spirituality.
holder: Mohammed VI Museum of Water Civilisation
Various local communities or preserved as heritage by Ministry of Culture and Islamic Affairs

ar.name: مصحف برسباي.
description:
القطعة عبارة عن نسخة من النصف الثاني من القرآن الكريم، كانت موقوفة على المسجد الأقصى في القدس من قِبل السلطان الأشرف برسباي. وقد أهدي هذا المصحف له في مدينة دمشق أثناء توقفه فيها خلال سفره إلى أمد عام 836 / 1432، فأرسله للمسجد الأقصى، وجعل النظر عليه لشيخ المدرسة الصلاحية، وعين الشيخ شمس الدين محمد بن قطلوبغا الرملي الذي كان قارئاً مشهوراً في القدس للقراءة في المصحف.  
  
تعرض المصحف لإعادة تجليد وترميم استبعدت خلالها بعض أوراقه الممزقة واستبدلت بأخرى، وأدت هذه العملية إلى فقدان صدر المصحف ونهايته التي عادة ما تحمل اسم الخطاط والمذهِّب وتاريخ نسخ المصحف. وقد قصَّت أوراق المصحف من الجوانب الثلاثة عند ترميمه، إذ كانت أبعاد المصحف الأصلية تقريباً 120 × 95 سم. كتب في آخر المصحف نص يفيد أنه رمِّم، وهو يقرأ "صلحه الفقير إبراهيم أحمد السلفيتي العباسي وذلك في أواخر شهر جمادى الآخر سنة 1292 \[1875\]."  
  
يبدأ نص المصحف بسورة الكهف (رقم 18)، وكتب النص بالحبر الأسود الغامق السميك بخط الثلث المتقن. وأخذت علامات الوقف شكل زهرات سداسية مذهَّبة الأوراق. وكتب اسم الجلالة "الله" واسم الرسول "محمد" أينما وردا في النص باللون الذهبي. وكتب اسم السورة وعدد آياتها ومكان نزولها باللون الأبيض، وأحيطت بزخارف نباتية داخل الإطار المستطيل الذي يعلو كل سورة. يلاحظ أن الخطاط ميز الحروف الزائدة في بعض الكلمات بكتابتها باللون الأحمر، كذلك مدّ حرفي النون والتاء والأحرف المشابهة لهما في الشكل عندما جاءت في نهاية السطر إلى نهاية الهامش.  
  
وقد تم اقتطاع بعض أجزاء من الإطارات الموجودة في أعلى السور من مكانها بشكل متعمد، وغطي مكانها بورق أبيض في فترة لاحقة كتب فيه اسم السورة. وبيّن هذا الأمر أن ورق المصحف سميك، وربما يتكون من أكثر من طبقة.

النصف الثاني من القرآن الكريم، أوقفه على المسجد الأقصى السلطان الملك الأشرف برسباي. هذا أكبر مصاحف في فلسطين (تبلغ أبعاده: 110 سم × 170 سم، حين يكون مفتوحاً). كُتب المصحف بخط الثلث المملوكي الجميل، بالحبر الأسود، على ورق سميك، ومتين. المصحف يضمُّ الكثير من الزخارف، وكُتب لفظ الجلالة، واسم الرسول، أينما ورد، باللون الذهبي.
place: من المرجّح أن يكون قد أنتج في دمشق، سوريا.
keywords: تذهيب؛ خط الثلث؛ قرآن كريم؛ مصحف.

en.name: *Mashaf* (Qur’anic manuscript) of Barsbay.
description:
A copy of the second half of the Holy Qur'an. It was an endowment (*waqf*) to al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem by Sultan al-Ashraf Barsbay. This *mashaf* was given to him by the city of Damascus during his stop-over there part-way on a journey to a final destination in AH 836 / AD 1432. He sent it to al-Aqsa Mosque and made the *sheikh* of the Madrasa Salihiyya its custodian. He appointed Sheikh Shams al-Din Muhammad bin Qatlubga al-Ramli who was a famous orator in Jerusalem, to read this *mashaf*.  
The *mashaf* has been rebound and restored. During this process, a number of torn pages have been removed and replaced by others. This process has led to the loss of the front of the *mashaf* and the end, which would typically have borne the name of the calligrapher, the illuminator and the date the *mashaf* was copied. The folios of the *mashaf* had been trimmed on three sides at the time of restoration, since the dimensions of the original were approximately 120 cm x 95 cm. At the bottom of the *mashaf* is a statement that it was restored: “This was repaired by the humble Ibrahim Ahmad al-Salfayni al-‘Abbasi in the latter half of the month of Jumada II in the year 1292 \[1875\]”.  
The text begins with *Surat “al-Kahf”* (“the Cave”), written in thick, dark-black ink in skilful *thuluth* script. The pauses are indicated by six-leafed and illuminated blossoms. The names of “Allah” and the “Prophet Muhammad” are illuminated everywhere they appear in the text. The beginning of each new chapter, the chapter heading, the verse number, and the area where they are placed, is written in white ink and surrounded by vegetal decoration within a rectangular frame. The scribe distinguishes the elongated letters in some of the words by writing them in red. Furthermore, he elongates the two letters “Nun” and “Ta”, as well as any letters resembling these in form when they reach the end of the line, to the end of the margin.  
Some of the chapter headings have been intentionally ripped out, and the gap they have left covered over with white paper with the name of the chapter written on it. The substitute white paper is distinctive from the thick paper of the *mashaf*, which perhaps was composed of more than one layer.

This is the second half of a Qur’anic manuscript endowed to al-Aqsa Mosque by Sultan al-Ashraf Barsbay. It is the biggest Qur’an in Palestine (110 cm x 170 cm when open). It is written in beautiful *thuluth* script in black ink on a thick, strong paper and has many decorations. The name *al-Jalala* (Majesty) and the name of the Prophet are illuminated wherever they appear.
holder: Islamic Museum, al-Aqsa Mosque / al-Haram al-Sharif.
keywords: Illumination; thuluth; Qur’an; mashaf
materials: Coloured ink on paper, decorated and illuminated; the binding of leather.
tags: Coloured ink on paper, decorated and illuminated

es.name: Manuscrito coránico *(mashaf)* de Barsbay.
description:
Copia de la segunda mitad del sagrado Corán que el sultán al-Ashraf Barsbay donó en concepto de *waqf* a la Mezquita al-Aqsa de Jerusalén. Este *mashaf* (manuscrito del Corán) es un regalo que la ciudad de Damasco hizo al sultán en 836 / 1432, cuando éste hizo escala allí en el transcurso de un viaje. El sultán lo envió a Jerusalén y encargó al *shaij* de la madrasa Salihiyya que lo custodiase. Designó para su lectura al *sheij* Shams al-Din Muhammad ibn Qatlubga al-Ramli, un famoso orador de Jerusalén.  
El manuscrito se restauró y se reencuadernó; durante este proceso, se retiraron páginas rasgadas y se reemplazaron por nuevas, lo que produjo la pérdida del principio del *mashaf* y del final, en el que normalmente aparecía el nombre del calígrafo, el del iluminador y la fecha de la copia. En esta restauración también se recortaron las hojas por tres lados, que originalmente medían 120 × 95 cm. En la parte inferior se puede leer el texto que explica su restauración: “El humilde Ibrahim Ahmad al-Salfayni al-Abbasi reparó este *mashaf* en la segunda mitad del mes de *yumada* II, en el año 1292 \[1875\]”.  
El texto, escrito en tinta negra con gruesas letras *zuluz* de gran calidad, comienza por el sura “La cueva”. Las pausas están señaladas con flores de seis pétalos iluminadas. Los nombres de Allah y el profeta Muhammad aparecen siempre iluminados. El principio de cada capítulo, el encabezamiento, el número de la aleya y el lugar en que se encuentran están escritos con tinta blanca y rodeados por decoración vegetal dentro de un marco rectangular. A veces, para destacar las letras alargadas en algunas palabras, el escriba utiliza el color rojo. Alarga especialmente las letras *nun* y *ta*, así como otras letras con forma parecida cuando aparecen a final de línea, en el extremo del margen.  
Algunos títulos de capítulos se arrancaron intencionadamente y el espacio que dejaron se cubrió con papel blanco, con el nombre del capítulo escrito de nuevo. El papel añadido se distingue perfectamente del original, que es más grueso y, tal vez, compuesto por varias capas.

Este manuscrito recoge la segunda parte del Corán. El sultán al-Ashraf Barsbay lo donó a la Mezquita al-Aqsa. Se trata del segundo Corán más grande de Palestina (110 cm x 170 cm abierto). Está escrito con tinta negra sobre papel grueso y fuerte, en letra *zuluz* de gran belleza, acompañada de muchos motivos decorativos. El nombre al-Yalala (‘majestad’) y el nombre del Profeta están iluminados.
keywords: Iluminación; escritura zuluz; Corán; mashaf.
materials: Tinta de color sobre papel, decorado e iluminado; encuadernación de cuero.
tags: Tinta de color sobre papel, decorado e iluminado
partner: Museo islámico en la mezquita de Al-Aqsa

fr.name: Machaf (manuscrit coranique) de Barsbay.
description:
Manuscrit de la seconde moitié du Coran donné en *waqf* à la mosquée al-Aqsa à Jérusalem par le sultan al-Achraf Barsbay. Il lui avait été offert par la ville de Damas au cours d'une visite effectuée en 836 H / 1432 J.-C. Il l'envoya à la mosquée pour en confier la garde au *cheikh* de la *madrasa* Salihiyya et la lecture au *cheikh* Chams al-Din Muhammad bin Qatlubga al-Ramli, célèbre orateur de Jérusalem.  
Le manuscrit a été relié et restauré. à cette occasion, un certain nombre de pages déchirées ont été supprimées et remplacées, ce qui a vraisemblablement entraîné la disparition du début et de la fin du manuscrit, qui devaient mentionner le nom du calligraphe, de l'enlumineur et la date de la copie. Les feuilles ont été recoupées sur trois côtés au moment de la restauration, puisque les dimensions de l'original étaient d'environ 120 x 95 cm. En fin d'ouvrage figure une mention de restauration : “Ceci a été réparé par l'humble Ibrahim Ahmad al-Salfayni al-Abbassi dans la seconde moitié du mois de *jumada* II en l'an 1292 \[1875\].”  
Le texte commence par la sourate “al-Khaf” (La caverne) écrite en style *thoulouth* à l'encre noire épaisse. Les pauses marquées par des fleurs à six pétales sont enluminées. Les noms d'Allah et du prophète Muhammad sont systématiquement enluminés tout au long du texte. Le début de chaque sourate, le titre de la sourate, le numéro de verset et le texte environnant sont écrits à l'encre blanche et entourés d'un décor de motifs végétaux dans un cartouche rectangulaire. Le scribe a différencié les lettres allongées de certains mots en utilisant une encre rouge. De plus, il allonge les deux lettres “nun” et “tat”, ainsi que les lettres qui leur ressemblent, en fin de ligne contre la marge.  
Certains titres de sourates ont été volontairement grattés et leur emplacement a été masqué par un papier blanc sur lequel le titre a été réécrit. Ce papier de substitution se distingue de celui, épais, du manuscrit – peut-être composé de plusieurs couches.

Manuscrit de la seconde moitié d’un coran donné en *waqf* à la mosquée al-Aqsa par le sultan al-Achraf Barsbay. C’est le plus grand coran de Palestine (110 x 170 cm ouvert). Il est écrit en un superbe style *thoulouth* à l’encre noire sur un épais et solide papier, et comporte de nombreuses décorations. Le nom *al-Djalala* (Majesté) et le nom du Prophète sont systématiquement enluminés tout au long du texte.
holder: Musée islamique, mosquée al-Aqsa / Haram al-Charif.
keywords: Enluminures ; écriture thoulouth ; Coran ; machaf
materials: Encre de couleur sur papier ; texte décoré et enluminé ; reliure en cuir

en.name: Courtyard house
description: The central courtyard would include a water fountain, occasionally a small square garden, and would be separated from the street by high surrounding walls. This particular courtyard is accessed by a relatively low arched door. The main building (*al dakhil dar*, meaning indoor building) is north facing, whereas the smaller outdoor buildings (*al-barrani*) such as the kitchen, pantry and toilet, are generally located on the east side. The living quarters included a central living room and two square side rooms. The central living room is an enclosed shared space, keeping the inhabitants dry on rainy days and cool on hot summer days.
history:
Older courtyard houses built with clay walls resting on wooden beams began to be replaced by concrete slabs with supporting walls made of *ramleh*, as we can see from this example. In other areas, such as Ashrafiyyeh, the old style was replaced with alternating sandstone and limestone-marl walls, a style known as *ablaq*.  
The *dar* is built on a principle of scalability: rooms were added as the number of inhabitants expanded and thus the building was able grow without any changes to its internal logic. This kind of house became popular in the 1850s, and generally belonged to the city's aristocracy. It was specifically designed to be able to host the same family in the same building across many generations.
keywords: House; Architecture; Typology; Court; Yard

en.name: Textile fragment from Archbishop Ximenez de Rada's burial garments
names: Fragmento del alba del arzopispo Ximénez de Rada
description: The textile fragment was part of the alb which was buried the Archbishop Rodrigo Ximénez de Rada in 1247 at the Monastery of Santa María de Huerta (Soria, Spain). The tomb was opened at the beginning of the decade of 1880 at the request of the Master of Sigüenza. The fragment was found in the coffin and the master give it to the Marquis of Cerralbo, who was present. After this event, because of the importance of the Archbishop garments and the marquis’ interest in the history of the Monastery, the marquis paid all the expenses of two new openings of the grave. The first one in 1886 for the Spanish Royal Academy of the History researches, and the second one in 1907 for his own studio, when he completed the description of the garments and took photographs to his publication in 1908.
dates: 13th century, before 1247; discovered at the beginning of the decade of 1880
keywords: Spanish Muslim art; islamic influence; orientalism; collectionism
materials: Silk, metallic threads; lampas and taqueté weave

en.name: Church of Santas Justa y Rufina
description: Very similar to the Church of Santa María, although it has a west front that emulates European Gothic, flanked on high by two towers, the work on this church was not completed until the year 1413, according to the inscription under the choir loft, at the foot of the nave. In the interior, there are two notable works in carved plaster: the pulpit, which is contemporary with the building of the church, and the archway at the entrance to the Rosary Chapel, which is from the early Renaissance period. The magnificent altarpiece over the high altar, dedicated to the saints who gave the church its name, and painted by Domingo Ram and Juan Rius between 1475 and 1477, is perhaps the most successful example in the whole of Aragon of the integration of Mudéjar space and Gothic painting.

es.name: Iglesia de las Santas Justa y Rufina
description:
Muy similar a la de Santa María, aunque con una fachada occidental émula del gótico europeo, flanqueada en alto por dos torres, las obras de esta iglesia no terminaron hasta el año 1413, según se lee en una inscripción bajo el coro alto, a los pies de la nave. En su interior, lo más sobresaliente son dos obras en yeso tallado: el púlpito, que es coetáneo de la fábrica de la iglesia, y el arco de entrada a la capilla del Rosario, ya de comienzos del período renacentista.  
El magnífico retablo mayor, dedicado a las santas titulares y realizado por los pintores Domingo Ram y Juan Rius entre 1475 y 1477, es tal vez el ejemplo más logrado en todo el territorio aragonés de integración entre espacio mudéjar y pintura gótica.

it.name: Chiesa delle Sante Giusta e Rufina

ar.name: واجهة قصر المْشَتّى.
description:
تشكل واجهة قصر مشتى الموجودة في برلين جزءاً من واجهة القصر الخارجية على جانبي المدخل في مبنى القصر، وقد كان هذا الجزء الجنوبي من السور، المربع والواقع بين برجين مستديرين، هو الجزء الوحيد المزود بنقوش زخرفية على شكل شريط متعرج ومستمر على مسافة 47م في الأصل. وكان هذا الشريط محاطاً بقاعدة وحواف. وقد نقشت أشكال وردية كبيرة في المثلثات التي يشكلها الشريط المتعرج. أما الأرض فمغطاة بأغصان كرمة تخرج من أحواض. وتحتوي المثلثات في نصف الواجهة اليساري على نقوش لحيوانات مختلفة وحيوانات أسطورية كالطيور والأسود والغِرفين وتنين طاووسي الشكل (سيمورغ) وكذلك أيضاً على رسم مشخص خرافي نصفه الأسفل على شكل فرس. وتجتمع كل هذه المخلوقات في جو فردوسي مسالم، وأغلبها تجلس منتعشة على ماء الأحواض الكبيرة. ويبدأ عند برج المدخل الأيمن تغيير في البرنامج حيث تتراجع المخلوقات الحية لصالح زخارف نباتية صغيرة، حيث تملأ القاعدة أغصان متعرجة تخرج من مزهريات أومن كؤوس الأوراق. ويبدو هذا التغيير مبرراً إذا أخذنا جامع القصر الواقع خلفها بعين الاعتبار. لأن الصور كانت ممنوعة في ذلك الوقت في المساجد. أما مثلثات الجانب الأيمن، التي لم تنقل إلى برلين في عام 1903، فقد بقيت في مكانها آنذاك وتعرضت للتلف منذ ذلك الوقت.  
من المحتمل أن يكون الخليفة الأموي الوليد الثاني (743-744م) قد أمر في فترة حكمه القصيرة، ببناء قصر في الصحراء الأردنية إلى الجنوب الشرقي من العاصمة الحالية عمان. وقد أحاط سور مربع الشكل بالقصر الذي كان يضم قاعة استقبال وجناحاً للسكنى بالإضافة إلى مسجد وبعض الأبنية الأخرى التي استخدمت أحياناً كمقرات للحكم. ولم يكن لهذا السور إلا طابع التحصين الظاهري. وعلى أية حال فقد بقي البناء غير مكتمل وهذا ظاهر للعيان بدليل أن القطع الزخرفية الأرضية كانت كلها مكتملة، في حين أن أرضية الزخارف المنحوتة بقيت في الكثير من الأماكن على شكلها التخطيطي الأولي. كما لم توجد كتابة تعّرف بالمبنى.  
لم تكتشف مْشَتّى إلا في القرن التاسع عشر وهناك قطع أساسية من الواجهة موجودة في متحف الفن الإسلامي في برلين منذ عام 1903 كهدية من السلطان العثماني إلى القيصر الألماني، بينما يمكن زيارة المبنى في مكانه في الأردن.

تأتي واجهة المشتى الجيرية من قصر صحراوي في الأردن، وقد قدَّمها السلطان العثماني هدية للإمبراطور الألماني. إنها جزء من السور الخارجي الذي كان يحمل رسوم حيوانية، بين نباتات. ولأن الخليفة الذي أمر ببناء القصر قُتل، فإنه بقي دون إنجاز.
dates: ربما في النصف الأول من القرن الثامن / حوالي 743-744م.
keywords: زخرفة معمارية ؛ زخرفة نقش بارز ؛ واجهة قصر.
materials: حجر كلسي، تزيينات بنقش بارز مشغولة على كتل كبيرة.
tags: حجر كلسي، تزيينات بنقش بارز مشغولة على كتل كبيرة.
partner: متحف الفن الإسلامي في متحف بيرغامون ، المتاحف الحكومية

de.name: Fassade des Palastes von Mschatta.
description: Die Fassade des Palastes von Mschatta in Berlin besteht aus einem Teil der äußeren Palastfassade beidseitig des Einganges in den Palastkomplex. Nur dieser südliche Teil der quadratischen Ummauerung war zwischen zwei Rundtürmen mit Reliefdekor aus einem fortlaufenden Zickzackband in einer Länge von ursprünglich 47 m versehen, das von einem profilierten Sockel und einem Gesims eingefasst wird. Große Rosetten sitzen in den von dem Zickzackband gebildeten Dreiecken. Den Grund überziehen aus Becken entspringende Weinranken. In den Dreiecken der linken Fassadenhälfte werden unterschiedliche Tiere und Fabeltiere wie Vögel, Löwen und Greifen, ein Pfauendrache (Senmurw) sowie ein Kentaur in paradiesisch friedlichem Nebeneinander, zumeist sich an dem Wasser der großen Becken labend, wiedergegeben. Mit dem rechten Torturm beginnt ein Programmwechsel, da auf lebende Wesen zugunsten eines kleinteiligen Pflanzendekors verzichtet wurde. Aus Vasen oder Blattkelchen aufsteigende, sich in vielfältigen Windungen hinziehende Ranken füllen den Grund Mit Rücksicht auf die dahinterliegende Palastmoschee mag dieser Wechsel begründet werden, da es damals bereits ein Bilderverbot für Moscheen galt. Die nicht nach Berlin gelangten Dreiecke der rechten Seite verblieben 1903 am Ort und sind seither zerstört worden. Es könnte der omaijadische Kalif al-Walid II. (743-744) gewesen sein, der während seiner kurzen Regierungszeit den Auftrag gab, einen Palast in der jordanischen Wüste südöstlich der heutigen Hauptstadt Amman zu bauen. Den Palast mit Audienzsaal und Wohnbereich, einer Moschee und weitere, für zeitweilige Regierungsgeschäfte erforderliche Bauten umgab eine quadratische Umfassungsmauer, die nur scheinbaren Festungscharakter hat. Der Bau blieb allerdings unvollendet, was bei einer Betrachtung ins Auge fällt, da alle am Boden vorgearbeiteten Versatzstücke fertig sind, während der vor Ort ausgemeißelte Reliefgrund stellenweise nur in Anrissen skizziert blieb. Eine Bauinschrift wurde nicht gefunden. Erst im 19. Jh. wurde Mschatta wiederentdeckt. Wesentliche Teile der Fassade befinden sich seit 1903 als Geschenk des osmanischen Sultans an den deutschen Kaiser im Museum für Islamische Kunst, während das Bauwerk sich weiterhin in situ in Jordanien besichtigt werden kann.

Die Kalksteinfassade von Mschatta stammt von einem Wüstenschloss in Jordanien und wurde dem Deutschen Kaiser vom Osmanischen Sultan als Geschenk überreicht. Es handelt sich um die Außenmauer, auf der Tiere inmitten von floralem Dekor zu sehen sind. Da der Kalif, der den Palast bauen ließ, ermordet wurde, konnte der Bau nicht vollendet werden.
dates: wahrscheinlich 1. Hälfte 2. Jh / 8. Jh., um 125-126 H. / 743-744
keywords: Palastfassade; Reliefdekor; Baudekor
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Façade of the Palace of Mushatta.
description:
The façade of the palace of Mushatta in Berlin is a section of the outer façade to either side of the entrance to the palace complex. Of the square surrounding wall, only this southern section was decorated between two circular towers. It was decorated with relief work consisting of a continuous band of zigzags that was originally 47 m long, bordered by a base with mouldings and a ledge. Large rosettes decorate the triangular corners formed by the zigzags. The background is covered in vine tendrils that spill out of basins. On the façade’s left side, a variety of animals and mythological creatures – such as birds, lions, griffins, a peacock dragon (Senmurw) and a centaur – can be found within the triangular spaces, living peacefully alongside one another as if in the Garden of Eden, mainly occupied in refreshing themselves with water from the large basins. The tower gateway on the right-hand side heralds a change in motif: instead of living creatures, there is now a small-scale plant-motif decoration. The background is filled with shoots and tendrils that rise up from vases or calyxes, spiralling in all directions. This change of motif can be understood by taking into account the fact that the Palace Mosque was situated behind this part of the façade: the depiction of pictorial images was at the time already prohibited in mosques. The triangular sections from the right-hand side of the façade that were not brought over to Berlin in 1903 remained there, where they were destroyed.  
It could have been the Umayyad Caliph al-Walid II (r. AH 125–6 / AD 743–4) who, during his short reign, commissioned the building of a palace in the Jordanian desert, southeast of the present capital Amman. The four-sided wall that was built around the palace complex – which included an auditorium, living quarters and a mosque and other buildings needed for temporary government activities there, although the wall looked more defensive and impregnable than it actually was. However, the construction was to remain incomplete, as is testified by the finished pieces pre-worked on the ground, and the sketched markings that are all that exist on the chiselled relief backdrop. A building inscription was never found.  
Mushatta was only rediscovered in the 19th century. The Ottoman Sultan donated considerable sections of the façade to the German Emperor. The rest of the ruin remained *in situ* in Jordan and can still be seen.

The limestone façade of Mushatta comes from a desert palace in Jordan and was given as a present by the Ottoman sultan to the German emperor. It is part of the outer wall, which had a decoration of animals among plants. Because the caliph who built the palace was murdered, it was never finished.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
dates: Probably Hegira first half of the 2nd century/ AD 8th century, *c.* AH 125–6 / AD 743–4.
keywords: Palace façade; Relief decoration; architectural decoration
materials: Limestone, decorated with relief work in block sections.
tags: Limestone, decorated with relief work in block sections.
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

es.name: Fachada del palacio de Mushatta.
description:
La fachada de Mushatta conservada en Berlín es la parte originalmente a ambos lados de la entrada en el muro exterior del complejo palatino. Del muro cuadrangular, sólo este tramo del lado sur, situado entre dos torres circulares, estaba decorado. La decoración consiste en una banda continua con una línea en zigzag; dicha banda, que en su origen tenía 47 m de longitud, está bordeada por una base con molduras y una cornisa. Los espacios triangulares que crea el zigzag están decorados con grandes rosetas sobre un fondo de zarcillos de parra que salen de pilas. En los triángulos del lado izquierdo se aprecian representaciones de animales y criaturas mitológicas –aves, leones, grifos, un pavo-dragón y un centauro–, juntos pacíficamente como si estuvieran en el jardín del Edén, ocupados principalmente en refrescarse con el agua de los estanques. La iconografía a la derecha de la puerta cambia los seres vivos por pequeños motivos vegetales sobre un fondo de cálices y jarrones de los que salen espirales de brotes y zarcillos en todas las direcciones. Para entender este cambio en el programa iconográfico, hay que tener en cuenta que la mezquita del palacio estaría ubicada detrás de este muro y que las imágenes estaban prohibidas en las mezquitas. Las secciones triangulares de la parte derecha que no fueron trasladadas a Berlín en 1903 acabaron destruidas.  
Pudo ser que el califa al-Walid II (r. 125–26/ 743–44) mandara construir este palacio en el desierto de Jordania, al suroeste de Ammán, actual capital de Jordania. El complejo, rodeado de un muro por sus cuatro lados, comprendía una sala de audiencias, zonas de viviendas, una mezquita y edificios para usos gubernamentales temporales. Este muro tendría un aspecto más defensivo e inexpugnable que en la actualidad. El complejo no llegó a terminarse, como atestiguan los elementos terminados trabajados previamente que se hallan en el suelo, así como las marcas de esbozos que se observan en el fondo de relieves cincelados. No se ha encontrado ninguna inscripción que informe de la construcción.  
El palacio de Mushatta fue descubierto en el siglo XIX y el sultán otomano donó al emperador alemán gran parte de la fachada, mientras que el resto de las ruinas permanecen en Jordania, donde aún pueden contemplarse.

Esta fachada de piedra caliza del palacio de Mushata procede del desierto jordano y fue regalada por el sultán otomano al emperador alemán. Formaba parte del muro exterior, decorado con animales entre plantas. El palacio nunca llegó a terminarse, pues el califa que mandó construirlo fue asesinado.
holder: Museo de Arte Islámico del Museo Pergamon
dates: Probablemente 125-26 de la Hégira/  743-44 d. C.
keywords: fachada de un palacio; decoración en relieve; decoración de un edificio
materials: Bloques de piedra caliza decorados en relieve.
tags: Bloques de piedra caliza decorados en relieve.
partner: Museo de Arte Islámico en el Museo de Pérgamo, Museos Estatales

fr.name: Façade du palais de Mchatta.
description:
Cet ensemble est une partie de la façade du palais de Mchatta et constitue les deux côtés de l'entrée principale. Il s'agit de la partie sud de l'enceinte carrée, la seule qui soit pourvue d'un relief en bande de chevrons, lequel avait à l'origine 47 m de longueur et court sur les deux tours rondes et le reste de la façade entre un socle profilé et une corniche. De grandes rosettes garnissent les triangles créés par les chevrons, sur fond de rinceaux de vigne s'élevant de vasques. Dans les triangles de la partie gauche est représentée toute une série d'animaux réels ou fabuleux vivant dans une harmonie paradisiaque, oiseaux, lions, griffons, dragon-paon, centaure, lapant souvent l'eau des vasques. À droite de la tour d'entrée, le programme iconographique change, renonçant aux figures d'êtres vivants au profit d'un décor végétal fouillé. Le fond est rempli des sinuosités de rinceaux volubiles surgissant de vases ou de calices. Il est possible que le choix du décor végétal ait été dicté par la proximité de la mosquée du palais, l'interdiction des images existant déjà à cette époque dans l'enceinte religieuse. Les triangles qui ne furent pas transportés à Berlin restèrent sur place où ils furent détruits.  
C'est probablement le calife omeyyade al-Walid II (743-744 J.-C.) qui, durant son court règne, donna l'ordre de bâtir un palais dans le désert jordanien au sud-est de la ville d'Amman. Le palais comportait une salle d'audience, des appartements privés, une mosquée et divers bâtiments nécessaires à l'exercice du pouvoir et était entouré d'une enceinte carrée qui n'a pas vraiment un caractère de forteresse. Le chantier resta inachevé, ce qui est patent sur le site puisque les moellons préparés sont toujours en attente sur le sol et que les reliefs qui étaient sculptés sur place sont souvent à l'état d'ébauche. On n'a pu trouver d'inscription d'architecte. Le site ne fut découvert qu'au XIXe siècle, de grandes parties de la façade furent données en présent par le sultan ottoman à l'empereur allemand et se trouvent depuis 1903 au Museum für Islamische Kunst. Le site se visite encore de nos jours en Jordanie.

La façade en calcaire du palais Mchatta provient d'un palais situé dans le désert jordanien et a été donnée en présent à l'empereur germanique par le sultan Ottoman. C'est un pan du mur extérieur, qui avait une décoration d'animaux environnés de plantes. Le calife qui construisait ce palais ayant été assassiné, l'édifice n'a jamais été terminé.
dates: Ier-IIe siècle de l’Hégire (VIIe-VIIIe siècle J.-C.), probablement première moitié du IIe siècle de l’Hégire (VIIIe siècle J.-C.) ; vers 743-744 J.-C.
keywords: façade de palais ; décor en relief ; décor architectural
materials: Pierre calcaire, décor en relief réalisé par blocs.
tags: Pierre calcaire, décor en relief réalisé par blocs.
partner: Musée d’art islamique du Pergamon Museum (Museum für Islamische Kunst)

en.name: Qal‘at Tadmur
description:
During the Ayyubid period, Palmyra belonged to the principality of Homs. Within the Roman city there are inscriptions that testify to the transformation of the Temple of Bel, located at the southern end of the colonnaded street, into a fortress by the Seljuq ruler Nasir al-Din Muhammad bin Shirkuh in 532/1137 who later, in 576/1180, added a mosque.  
The medieval citadel is similar to the many other Arab citadels visited during this exhibition. A deep ditch surrounds this towering medieval fortress, only accessible via a bridge that rests on three pillars. The rooms, arranged around five courtyards, rise in elevation towards the north-west tower on the most prominent part of the hill. So far, the citadel’s origins are largely unexplored, but ceramic evidence dates the site back to the Ayyubid period and suggests that it took over the function of the citadel that had once been the Temple of Bel.

en.name: "Device for Raising Water" from al-Jazari's "Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices"
description: In the AH 7th / AD 13th-century, a scholar and engineer named Isma‘il Ibn al-Razzaz al-Jazari wrote a famous treatise called *Kitab fi ma‛rifat al-hiyal al-handasiyya*, or The Book of Knowledge of Ingenious Mechanical Devices. The text offered detailed descriptions of a series of elaborate machines designed to delight and impress the elites at the court where he served, in eastern Anatolia. Al-Jazari’s text and its illustrations belong to a long tradition of studies about these kinds of devices, including Greek compendia on mechanics and mathematics. This page belongs to a copy of the text that was produced in Mamluk Egypt in AH 755 / AD 1354, and was copied by Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Izmiri for a Mamluk ruler.
keywords: Water; Folio; Technical Manuscript; Mamluks
materials: Opaque watercolour and ink on paper
tags: Opaque watercolour and ink on paper

en.name: *La Mhalla* (painting)
short_description: This oil on canvas by Bertrand de Moynier depicts the disembarkment of the *mhalla*, the field army, in the mid-19th century for the collection of taxes. The *mhalla*, a military term, was made up of soldiers, *mamluks*, civil servants, merchants and artisans, which were split into three categories: infantry, cavalry and artillery. This army was supported by informal troops and horsemen from local tribes. The beylical tent has been erected in the centre of the mhalla, next to the service tents for the bey's personnel and the tents for the administrative and fiscal representatives. The future 'Ali Bey III (1882–1902) can be seen in the centre of the painting, in front of the red and green flags.
holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
keywords: Oil on canvas; field army
partner: Higher Institute for the Study of Contemporary History of Tunisia, University of Manouba

fr.name: Tableau de peinture *La Mhalla*
short_description: C’est un tableau de peinture à l’huile sur toile réalisé par le peintre Bertrand de Moynier. Il représente une sortie de la *mhalla* ou l’armée de campagne au milieu du XIXe siècle pour la collecte des impôts. La *mhalla*, terme d’origine militaire, est composée de troupes de soldats, de mamelouks, de fonctionnaires, de commerçants et d’artisans. Les soldats appartiennent aux trois armes : infanterie, cavalerie et artillerie. Cette force était assistée par les troupes non régulières et des cavaliers issus de tribus. La tente beylicale est dressée au cœur de la *mhalla*, à côté des tentes du service du personnel du bey mais aussi de celles des représentants des fonctions administratives et fiscales. On distingue au centre, précédant les drapeaux rouges et verts, le futur Ali Bey III (1882-1902).
holder: Palais de la Rose – Musée de l’Armée
keywords: Peinture à l’huile sur toile; Armé de compagne
partner: Institut Supérieur d’histoire contemporaine de la Tunisie, Université de la Manouba

en.name: Ballroom with frescoes
description:
The most famous fresco of the palace is that of the ballroom located on the the first floor, it represents the *Apotheosis of Marescotti's family* and was painted  by Giuseppe and Antonio Rolli. It shows  Wisdom, with  Glory on her left,  holding up a pyramid. The circle on the pyramid symbolizes eternity. The main scene is surrounded by oval medaillons with allegorical figures of cities connected with the Marescottis (Bologna, Rome, Siena) and the personification of Scotland.  
The family portraits on the walls were painted in 1709 by Giovanni Battista Caccioli.
place: Salone Marescotti, first floor, Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti
artist: Giuseppe Rolli; Antonio Rolli; Giovanni Battista Caccioli
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Salone da ballo affrescato
description:
Nel salone da ballo del piano nobile si conserva l'affresco più famoso del palazzo: l'  *Apoteosi della famiglia Marescotti*, dipintoda Giuseppe e Antonio Rolli. Vi appaiono la Sapienza, con al Gloria alla sua sinistra, che sostiene una piramide. Il cerchio sulla piramide simboleggia l'eternità. La scena principale è circondata da medaglioni con le allegorie di città legate ai Marescotti, come Bologna, Roma, Siena e la personificazione della Scozia.  
Nel 1709 Giovanni Battista Caccioli dipinse i ritratti di famiglia sulle pareti.
place: Salone Marescotti, piano nobile, palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti
artist: Giuseppe Rolli; Antonio Rolli; Giovanni Battista Caccioli

ar.name: أجزاء من جصيات.
description: أجزاءٌ من جصيات منقوشة بتشبيكات محفورة حفراً بارزاً، وببنيات مختلفة، كانت في الأصل متعددة الألوان بالرغم من أنه لم يتبق منها اليوم إلا بقايا من الأحمر والأسود. تهيمن النجومُ ذات الثمانية فروع، وتتخذ مقاييس مختلفة تؤدي إلى أشكال من البنيات الهندسية وأشكال أخرى مبتكرة تؤثث الفراغات. جرى فصلُ كل نجمة عن جارتها بنوع من الأشكال التي تشكلُ الشرائط العمودية والأفقية. الجزء المسجل تحت رقم 50725 تمَّ الحصول عليه من إحدى اللوحات الجانبية للعقد الكبير للصالة الوسطى المستطيلة، التي كانت محاطة بصالتين مربعتين. الجزء (ج) الذي يحوي نجمتين ونصف النجمة قد يرجعُ إلى الإفريز الأفقي الموضوع فوق العقد؛ في حين ينتمي الآخر، الجزء (أ) ذو زخرفة التشبيكات الممزوجة مع زخارف توريقية منمنمة، بدون شك، إلى القاعدة. أما الجزء الثالث (ب) والمزخرف بنجمة وردية هندسية، فقد تم الحصول عليه من الركنيات.

كانت الأرستقراطية المسيحية تقف معجبة أمام الدقة الفنية الإسلامية؛ لذلك أدمجت في مساكنها موادا وأشكالا يرجعُ مصدرها إلى قصور أندلسية. فقد كانت الجدران في ورشة المغربي بطليطلة مزخرفة بجصيات مماثلة إلى هذه الكسر المزينة بتشبيكات هندسية رُسمت انطلاقا من نجوم تتألف من ثمانية فروع.
dynasty: فترة المدجنين، القرن الثاني عشر – الخامس عشر
keywords: جبس؛ طالير ديل مورو (ورشة المغربي)؛ طليطلة؛ مدجن؛ مشكَّل.

en.name: Plasterwork fragments.
description:
Fragments of plasterwork decorated with high-relief strap-work with a variety of structures and initially multicoloured, although now there are only traces of flat red and black. There is a predominance of eight-pointed stars of different sizes that generate geometrical structures (*azafates harpados*) and fanciful shapes that fill the spaces. Each star is separated from its neighbour by these types of figure, which form vertical and horizontal strips.  
The fragment with inventory number 50725 comes from one of the side panels of the great arch of the central rectangular hall, which was flanked by two square rooms. Fragment C, which has two and a half stars, may have come from the horizontal frieze placed above the arch. Fragment A, decorated with knotwork mixed with plant arabesques, undoubtedly came from the base. A third fragment, B, decorated with a geometrical rose, comes from the spandrels.

The Christian aristocracy, appreciative of Muslim artistic refinement, incorporated the materials and motifs of the Andalusian palaces in their mansions. The walls of the Moor’s Workshop in Toledo were decorated with plasterwork like this, with its geometric interlacing designs developing from an eight-pointed star.
place: Taller del Moro (Moor’s Workshop), Toledo, Spain.
keywords: Plasterwork; modelled; Moorish; Toledo

es.name: Fragmentos de yeserías.
description:
Fragmentos de yeserías decorados con lacería, muy resaltada y de diferente estructura, y originalmente polícromos, aunque ahora sólo se advierten restos de color rojo plano y negro. Predominan las estrellas de ocho puntas, de varios tamaños, que generan estructuras geométricas –azafates harpados– y otras formas caprichosas que llenan los espacios. Cada estrella está separada de la adyacente por este tipo de figuras, que forman bandas verticales y horizontales.  
  
El fragmento inventariado con el n.º 50725 procede de uno de los paneles laterales del gran arco del salón central, rectangular, que estaba flanqueado por dos salones cuadrados. El fragmento C, que abarca dos estrellas y media, proviene tal vez del friso horizontal dispuesto sobre el arco. Otro, el A, con decoración de lacería mezclada con ataurique, pertenecía sin duda al zócalo. Un tercer fragmento, el B, decorado con una roseta geométrica, procede de las enjutas.

La aristocracia cristiana, admiradora del refinamiento artístico musulmán, incorporó a sus mansiones materiales y motivos de los palacios andalusíes. En el Taller del Moro toledano, las paredes se decoraron con yeserías como estas, de lacería geométrica trazada a partir de estrellas de ocho puntas.
keywords: yesería; modelado; mudéjar; Toledo; Moro; Morisco

fr.name: Fragments de stucs.
description: Fragments de stuc décorés d'entrelacs en haut-relief et de différentes structures, initialement polychromes même si, aujourd'hui, ne subsistent que des restes de rouge et de noir. Les étoiles à huit branches prédominent, de différentes dimensions, et engendrent toutes sortes de structures géométriques et autres formes fantaisistes qui meublent les vides. Chaque étoile est séparée de sa voisine par ce type de figures qui forment des bandes horizontales et verticales. Le fragment inventorié sous le n° 50725 provient de l'un des panneaux latéraux du grand arc de la salle centrale, rectangulaire, qui était flanquée de deux salons carrés. Le fragment C, qui contient deux étoiles et demie, provient peut-être de la frise horizontale disposée sur l'arc. Un autre, le fragment A, à décoration d'entrelacs mêlée d'atauriques, appartenait sans doute au socle. Un troisième fragment, le B, décoré d'une rosace géométrique, provient des écoinçons.

L'aristocratie chrétienne était en admiration devant le raffinement artistique musulman. C'est pourquoi elle incorpora dans ses demeures des matériaux et des motifs originaires des palais andalous. Dans l'Atelier du Maure à Tolède, les murs étaient décorés de stucs identiques à ces fragments, avec des entrelacs géométriques tracés à partir d'étoiles à huit branches.
keywords: stuc ; modelé ; mudéjar ; Tolède ; Mauresque

ar.name: مصحف
description: في هذا المصحف فإن بداية كل سورة مبينة بسطر من خط مذهب يعطي اسم السورة وعدد الآيات فيها. ويمتد من كل من هذه العناوين عنصر من سعيفة نخل بطراز خاص جدا مرسوم بمزيج لوني بورغندي من الأزرق والأخضر والذهبي. وهذه الصفحات هي مما كان يشكل المجلد الأخير للمصحف ذو الستين جزءا. وكل من المجلدات الأصلية الستين تبدأ بجزء أمامي ذو صفحتين مذهب بشكل  مشابه للجزء الأمامي ( الذي هو الآن بشكل صفحة وحيدة) المشمولة في هذا المجلد.

en.name: Qur'an
description: In this Qur’an, the beginning of each *sura* (chapter) is indicated by a line of gold script giving the title of the chapter and the number of verses it contains. Extending from each of these titles is a highly stylized palmette element, executed in a palette of burgundy, blue, green and gold. These folios are from what was the final volume of a sixty-part Qur’an. Each of the original sixty volumes would have begun with an illuminated double-page frontispiece similar to the (now only single-page) frontispiece included in this volume.
