en.name: Entrance of the Hammam of the Mouassine Mosque (Marrakech)
description: The entrance to the *hammam* of the Mouassine Mosque in Marrakech is situated within an area of the city that dates back to antiquity. This area demonstrates the interconnection between water, buildings and the quality of life of the inhabitants of the medina. The Mouassine complex was constructed during the Saadian period in the 16th century. The architectural design of the building was conceived with the intention of creating a multifunctional civic foundation, thereby ensuring its versatility in terms of utilisation. The complex included a mosque, fountain, hammam, madrasa and public amenities. The entrance to the hammam is modest and integrated into the urban fabric, reflecting the traditional Moroccan approach to architecture where public buildings are an integral part of the city.
keywords: Water; Mosque; Photography; Marrakech.

ar.name: قطعة نقدية هدية
description: هذه القطعة النقدية التمثيلية الفضية الفريدة من الخليفة العباسي المتوكل (847 – 61 ميلادي) هي ذات أهمية تذكارية. وكونها المثال الوحيد المتبقي في العالم فهي الآن في مجموعة القطع النقدية لمتحف تاريخ الفن في فينا. وهي تتبع طراز القطع النقدية الساسانية و الوجه العلوي (الطرة) تصور بورتريه للخليفة والوجه الخلفي ( النقش ) تصور رجلا يمسك بخطام جمل عربي . ومضمون النقش : ""باسم الله ، محمد رسول الله ، المتوكل بالله "" وعلى الوجه الخلفي : "" في عام 241 هجري – 855/6 ميلادي ، المعتز بالله"".مثل هذه القطع النقدية التذكارية كانت توزع بين العامة في مناسبات خاصة . ونحن نعلم أن المتوكل كان يملك خمسة ملايين قطعة نقدية فضية صكت كي  يوزعها  بنثرها مثل بتلات الزهور بين الضيوف المجتمعين. وهذه القطعة النقدية يمكن أيضا أن تكون قد صكت كقطعة نقدية تذكارية حيث أن وجهها الخلفي يذّكر بإناخة  بيغا Biğāh  لجمل يركبه من السودان.
keywords: العباسيون ، المتوكل ، قطعة نقدية هدية

de.name: Geschenkmünze
description:
Eine besondere Rarität ist die silberne Geschenkmünze des abbasidischen Kalifen Al Mutawakkil (847–861). Das weltweit einzige Exemplar wird im Münzkabinett des Kunsthistorischen Museums aufbewahrt. In Anlehnung an die sasanidische Münztypologie ist auf der Vorderseite das frontale Bildnis des Kalifen mit doppelspitzigem Bart dargestellt, während auf der Rückseite ein Mann neben einem von ihm geführten Dromedar steht. Die Aufschrift lautet: „Im Namen Gottes, Muhammad ist der Gesandte Gottes, al-Mutawakkil bi-Allah“, dazu im Revers: „Im Jahr 241“ (Hidschra = 855/6 n. Chr.) „al-Mu´tazz bi-Allah.“  
Solche Geschenkmünzen wurden bei festlichen Anlässen unter das Volk gestreut. So wird etwa von al-Mutawakkil berichtet, er habe fünf Millionen Silbermünzen prägen lassen, um sie wie Rosenblütenblätter über die versammelte Festgesellschaft zu verstreuen. Das vorliegende Stück dürfte auch als Gedenkmünze konzipiert gewesen sein und nimmt mit seinem Reversbild auf die Unterwerfung der im Sudan ansässigen, kamelreitenden Biğāh Bezug.
dynasty: Abbasiden, Kalif al-Mutawakkil (232–247 H. / 847–861 n. Chr.)
keywords: Abbasiden; al Mutawakkil; Geschenkmünze

en.name: Giftcoin
description:
This unique silver presentation coin of the Abbasid caliph al-Mutawakkil (AD 847– 861) is of seminal importance. The only surviving example in the world, it is now in the Coin Collection of the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna. Following Sassanian coin typology, the obverse features an en face portrait of the caliph, the reverse a standing man holding a dromedary. The inscription reads: "In the name of God, Muhammad is his messenger, al-Mutawakkil bi-Allah", and on the reverse: "In the year \[AH\] 241 \[AD 855/6\] al-Mu\`tazz bi-Allah".  
Such commemorating coins were distributed among the populace on special occasions. We know that al-Mutawakkil had five million silver coins minted to distribute like rose petals among the assembled guests. This coin may also have been devised as a commemorative coin as its reverse commemorated the submission of the camel-riding Biğāh from the Sudan.
keywords: Coinage; coin; Abbasids; Abbasid coinage; al-Mutawakkil bi-Allah; al-Mu`tazz bi-Allah; Sassanian coinage; mint; numismatics; commemorative coins; figurative representation; al Mutawakkil; Gift coin

ar.name: زجاجة.
description: زجاجة كبيرة طويلة العنق ذات قاعدة تتسع إلى الخارج وحلقة عند العنق، وقد تم تزيين أغلب السطح بالمينا والتذهيب. يحمل عنق الزجاجة أشرطة متشابكة من المينا الزرقاء تخلق مساحات فيما بينها تم ملؤها بزخارف زهرية، وحول قاعدة العنق تظهر حليات دائرية تتضمن طيور العنقاء المتقابلة والمتناوبة مع حيوانات خرافية في وضعية المشي، أما الجزء الأهم في الزخرفة فهو نقوش كتابية حول الجسم، مكتوبة بخط أزرق طويل على أرضية من الأرابيسك الأبيض الملتف مع ضربات بالأحمر والأخضر والأصفر. النص عبارة عن تكريس لحاكم اسمه غير مذكور: "عز لمولانا السلطان الملك العالم العادل المجاهد". وقد تم تكرار الجزء الأول من هذه العبارة على الحلقة عند العنق، وتذكر الزخارف المتقنة لهذه الزجاجة بذروة صناعة الزجاج في سوريا ومصر في الفترتين الأيوبية والمملوكية. ويظهر بجلاء أن هذا العنصر قد تم صنعه لأغراض دنيوية، وقد يكون قد استخدم لتقديم المشروبات في البلاط.
زجاجة ذات عنق طويلة، مزخرفة ومطلية بعدة ألوان. يظهر عليها نقش نافر، غير واضح الملامح، وغير مقروء. على الأغلب فإنها صنعت للاستخدامات الدنيوية، مثل تقديم الخمر، وغيره من المشروبات، في القصور.
dates: النصف الأول من القرن الثامن/ الرابع عشر.

en.name: Bottle.
description: A large long-necked bottle with flared foot and neck-ring. Most of the surface is decorated with enamelling and gilding. The neck of the bottle has interlacing bands of blue enamelling which create compartments filled with floral decoration. Around the base of the neck are roundels featuring phoenixes in heraldic poses which alternate with striding griffins. The most prominent part of the decoration is the calligraphic inscription around the body. Written in tall blue script against a background of coiled white arabesques with highlights in red, green, and yellow, the text is a dedication to an unnamed ruler: 'Glory to our lord, the Sultan, the wise, the just, the religious warrior, the king'. The first part of this phrase is repeated above the bottle's neck-ring. The elaborate all-over decoration of this bottle recalls the heyday of glass production in Syria and Egypt in the Ayyubid and Mamluk periods. An object clearly intended for a secular purpose, it may have been used to serve drinks at court.

A large, long-necked glass bottle lavishly decorated with enamelling in several colours and gilding. The inscriptions, though prominent, are anonymous. The bottle was clearly made for a secular purpose and may have been used to serve wine and other drinks at court.
dates: First half of the hegira 8th / AD 14th century.
keywords: Calligraphy; inscription; animal decoration; phoenix; imaginary animal; zoomorphic imagery; arabesque

es.name: Botella
description:
Botella de gran tamaño, cuello largo con un anillo y pie acampanado. La mayor parte de su superficie está esmaltada y dorada. El cuello está decorado con bandas de entrelazados en esmalte azul; los espacios que delimitan se han rellenado con decoración floral. En la base hay medallones con fénix en posturas heráldicas, alternados con grifos en movimiento. Lo más destacado de la decoración de esta botella es la inscripción caligráfica que rodea el cuerpo, escrita en azul sobre un fondo de arabescos enroscados de color blanco con detalles en rojo, verde y amarillo. En cuanto al texto, está dedicado a un gobernante desconocido: “Gloria a nuestro señor el sultán, el sabio, el justo, el guerrero religioso, el rey”. La primera parte de esta frase se repite también más arriba del anillo del cuello.  
La elaborada decoración de esta botella da fe del auge de la producción de vidrio en Siria y Egipto durante los periodos ayyubí y mameluco. Objeto fabricado claramente con fines seculares, quizá se utilizó para servir bebidas en la corte.

Botella de gran tamaño y cuello alargado, profusamente decorada con esmaltados en diferentes colores y dorado. Las inscripciones, aunque sobresalientes, no nombran a ningún personaje. Sería de uso secular en la corte, para servir vino y otras bebidas.
dates: Primera mitad del siglo VIII de la Hégira / XIV d. C.

fr.name: Bouteille.
description: Grande bouteille à long goulot, pied évasé et anneau de goulot. La plus grande partie de sa surface est décorée d'émail et de dorure. Le goulot présente des bandeaux d'émail bleu entrelacés qui créent des compartiments meublés d'un décor floral. Autour de la base du goulot, des rosettes ornées de phénix en poses héraldiques alternent avec des griffons marchant. La partie du décor la plus remarquable est l'inscription calligraphique entourant le corps. Rédigé en écriture haute de couleur bleue sur un fond d'arabesques enroulées à rehauts rouge, vert et jaune, le texte est une dédicace à un souverain non nommé : “Gloire à notre seigneur, le Sultan, le sage, le juste, le guerrier religieux, le roi.” La première partie de cette phrase est répétée au-dessus de l'anneau de col. Le décor élaboré qui recouvre toute la surface de cette bouteille rappelle l'apogée de la production de verre en Syrie et en Égypte au cours des périodes ayyoubide et mamelouke. Objet à l'évidence conçu pour un usage séculier, il a pu être utilisé pour le service des boissons dans une cour.

Grande bouteille en verre à long goulot, délicatement décorée de plusieurs teintes d'émail et de dorure. Bien que remarquables, les inscriptions sont anonymes. À l'évidence, la bouteille a été faite pour un usage séculier et a peut-être été utilisée pour servir le vin ou d'autres boissons à la cour.
dates: première moitié du VIIIe de l’Hégire (XIVe J.-C.).

en.name: Monochrome roundel with the *Birth of the Virgin*
description: The use of monochrome painting in the roundels at the foot of the dome shows Mitelli’s and Colonna’s elegant taste together with their will to emphasise the contrast between the different worlds of the stories of the Virgin and the heavenly vision above. The scene represented in this roundel is strongly indebted to the classicizing style of Guido Reni.
place: Dome of the square antechamber of the chapel of the Rosary, Basilica di San Domenico, Bologna
artist: Angelo Michele Colonna and Agostino Mitelli
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: *Tondo monocromo con la Nascita della Vergine*
description: L'uso della pittura monocroma nei tondi ai piedi della cupola dimostra il raffinato gusto di Mitelli e Colonna e insieme la loro volontà di enfatizzare il contrasto tra due mondi: quello quotidiano delle storie della Vergine e la visione celestiale in alto. La scena rappresentata in questo tondo è fortemente legata allo stile classicista di Guido Reni.
place: Base del catino absidale della cappella del Rosario, Basilica di S. Domenico, Bologna
artist: Angelo Michele Colonna e Agostino Mitelli

en.name: The goddess Maat
short_description: The fragment comes from the parietal relief from the tomb of Sethy I (1289-1279 A.C.), discovered in 1817 and located in the Valley of the Kings. The relief is part of one of the most important group of the Franco-Tuscan expedition (1828–1829) and has been brought to Florence by Ippolito Roselllini. The relief shows the goddess Maat, recognised by the feather on her head.
place: Egypt, Valley of the Kings, tomb of Pharaoh Sethy Ist (XIX Dynasty)

en.name: Madrasa al-Hallawiyya
description: Across a narrow road from the northwest corner of the Great Mosque is the Madrasa al-Hallawiyya, rebuilt in the 6th/12th century over the remains of the Byzantine Church of St Helena. An inscription by Nur al-Din dates it to 543/1149, although the courtyard and the large dome above the Byzantine apse appear to be Ottoman. A separate chamber next to the dome contains the magnificent wooden *mihrab* offered to the madrasa by Ibn al-’Adim, an important figure in legal and political circles who served as qadi (judge) vizier (minister) and historian of Aleppo during the Ayyubid reign. Inscribed by the historian himself, this *mihrab* is one of the masterpieces of Arabic woodwork and calligraphy.

en.name: One Su‘udi Riyal
description: This silver riyal was struck at Mecca in 1348 AH (1929–30) by Abd al-Aziz ibn Saud, who had completed his conquest of the Hijaz in 1925 and at the time styled himself King of the Hijaz, Najd and its Dependencies. Unlike the purely calligraphic coinage of Sharif Hussein, it combines inscriptions with palm trees and crossed swords, motifs that anticipate the later emblem of Saudi Arabia. Its inscription names Mecca as the place of minting. The coin belongs to the brief years between the end of Hashemite rule in the Hijaz and the proclamation of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in 1932.

en.name: Ceramic panel with eight azulejos [tiles] (from the Odescalchi collection)

short_description: The Museum of Industrial Arts (M.A.I.) was established in 1872 in Rome as a collection of manufacts (glasses, majolica, sculptures, materials, photographs, metals, casts and other) from antiquity to 19th century, and as a training school for specialising artisans, as part of the process of revaluation of the so-called "minor arts". The collections of the M.A.I. included large samples of pottery, wooden objects, fabric, bronzes and ivories dating to Roman, Renaissance and Baroque times. The best part of this collection is on display at the National Gallery of Palazzo Barberini in Rome, while other pieces are housed in Castel Sant'Angelo and Palazzo Venezia. Within the series of the Hispanic-Moorish ceramics are some pottery with azulejos, bought by Prince Baldassarre Ladislao Odescalchi in 1880. The panel with eight azulejos dates from 15th and 16th centuries. It shows both geometric and floral decorations.

en.name: Carpet with sickle leaf design
description: In the 16th century, medallion carpets of Safavid Persia were much sought after, but by the century’s end and toward the beginning of the 17th century, floral motifs, spirals and palmettes began to gain appreciation. This long, narrow, “vase technique” carpet was probably produced in a Kerman (within southern Persia) workshop, during the reign of Shah ‘Abbas I (1571‒1629). Its field is made up of a dark-blue background, upon which is spread out an exuberant and dynamic vegetal pattern. This pattern is itself composed of several different planes of floral motifs in rich polychrome, palmettes and large sickle-shaped leaves. Compared to other examples of this type it has a narrower ground border, decorated with a frieze with spirals and flowers. In the centre of the field, there is an almost imperceptible inscription, probably the weaver’s signature, which is an extremely rare find in carpets from this period.

en.name: Saint Nicholas Square (Piazza San Nicola)
description:
The square, which is overlooked by the church of Saint Nicholas and the Municipal Building, was radically restructured in 1995–98. The restoration brought to light structures in *opus quadratum* from the late Republican period belonging to the podium of a three-celled temple, perhaps a Capitolium, the Temple of Juno or the Temple of Jupiter mentioned by Livy. It was on these roman walls that, in the early Christian age, the Collegiate Church of Saint Mary was built, to be later demolished in the 17th century by Alexander VII for the construction of the new collegiate church on Piazza di Corte. The remains of 17th-century walls are instead from the old monastery of the Christian Doctrine Fathers (F. Guglielmi, 1985). The parvise’s flooring is partially made of the basalt slabs from the 19th-century pavement of Piazza del Popolo in Rome.  
  
In front of the entrance to the town hall there is the Bella Flora Fountain (Fontana della Bella Flora), with a marble base, four bronze shell-shaped basins, and a bronze female statue. The fountain was built in 1886, and it has become the symbol of Ariccia itself, although its sculpture comes from the old municipal cemetery and represents a young deceased maiden, not the nymph Aricia nor the goddess Flora.

it.name: Piazza San Nicola
description:
La piazza, su cui prospetta la chiesa di San Nicola e il Palazzo Municipale, è stata ristrutturata radicalmente nel 1995-1998, portando alla luce strutture in opera quadrata di età tardo-repubblicana relative al podio di un tempio a tre celle, forse un *Capitolium*, il *Tempio di Giunone* o meglio il Tempio di Giove citato da Tito Livio. Sopra tali muratura era stata costruita in età paleocristiana la collegiata di Santa Maria, demolita nel ‘600 da Alessandro VII per la costruzione della nuova collegiata su piazza di Corte. I frammenti di murature seicentesche sono invece relative al vecchio monastero dei Padri della Dottrina Cristiana (F. Guglielmi, 1985). Il lastricato del sagrato della chiesa, eseguito nella sistemazione del 1998, rimonta parte delle lastre in basalto della pavimentazione ottocentesca di Piazza del Popolo a Roma.  
  
Di fronte all’ingresso del municipio è collocata la *Fontana della Bella Flora*, con basamento in marmo, quattro vasche bronzee a conchiglia, statua muliebre in bronzo. La fontana, costruita nel 1886, è assurta ad emblema stesso di Ariccia, sebbene la pregevole scultura provenga dal vecchio cimitero comunale e non rappresenti la ninfa Aricia o la dea Flora, ma una giovane defunta.

en.name: *Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey* (1784–1839)
short_description:
Portrait of Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey (1784–1839). In 1826 Mahmud II initiated the development of a modern army. This led to the uprising of the Janissary, which was quelled by massacring the rebellious troops. Under Mahmud II's reign, in 1821 the Greeks started their fight for freedom which was granted to them in the Peace of Adrianople in 1829.  
After the destruction of the Janissary, the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Mahmud II had only 35,000 badly trained regular soldiers in 1827. Due to the weakness of the Ottoman Empire, Ibrahim Pasha, the son of Muhammad 'Ali (ruler of Egypt), invaded Syria. On 20 February 1832, the Egyptian Army defeated the Ottoman Army at the Battle of Konya. This forced Mahmud II to sign the Peace of Kütahya and to cede Syria and Kilikia to Egypt.
keywords: Mahmud II, Sultan of Turkey; Egypt; Janissary; Konya; Ibrahim Pasha; Muhammad Ali; Greece

de.name: Jüngstes Gericht
description: Das in lichten, zartbunten Farben gemalte Hauptfresko thematisiert heilversprechend und sinnfällig das Jüngste Gericht als Ziel des Erlösungswerkes Christi, das mit dessen Leiden im Vorfeld der Kreuzigung begann. Gegenüber dem Tor zur Ewigkeit, vor welchem Chronos gestürzt das Zeitenende symbolisiert, ist Christus als Weltenrichter der Thron bereitet.

en.name: The Last Judgement
description: The brightly coloured main fresco promisingly and obviously thematises the Last Judgement as the goal of Christ’s redemption, whose passion began with His suffering leading up to His crucifixion. Opposite the gate to eternity, before which a toppled Chronos symbolises the end of time, is the throne prepared for Christ as the Judge of the World.
partner: University of Munich, Institute of Art History

en.name: Print showing a catafalque
names: *Castrum Doloris* of Johann Herbart Auersperg in St. Catherine’s Church, Zagreb
description:
Count Johann Herbart Auersperg was a General and Commander of the Military March. He was a descendant of the old, famous Slovenian Turjak Counts and a brother of Count Weichard, a powerful minister and favourite of the Emperors Ferdinand III and Leopold I. The catafalque was installed in the Jesuit St. Catherine's Church, Zagreb, when Count Johann Herbart Auersperg died in 1669.  
In the centre of the canopied hexagonal base with three steps is the sarcophagus, surrounded by six sculptures of famous Auersperg ancestors. Decorated with numerous candles and symbols in its entirety and signed on the bottom right *IC Mannasser.*  
There are also inscriptions, on the top left in a cartouche held by an angel: *EXCELLMO AC ILLMO ... Anno salut 1669 Aetatis 56* and at the top right in a cartouche held by an angel: *Ipso Die Exequiarum ... moestissimi erexerunt.*  
Following the fashion of European funeral ceremonies also in Croatia, luxurious catafalques were made known as *castrum doloris.* Count Auersperg's social position suggests that a famous Austrian or Italian architect could have staged the funeral ceremony depicted in this print. These architects were in demand at the time to construct various complicated and spectacular performances, usually organised by the Jesuit Order, and designed to enchant the eye and spirit of viewers with the use of impressive effects. A bronze memorial plaque also in the church commemorates Auersperg's death.

A Baroque catafalque was installed in the Jesuit Church of St Catherine, Zagreb for Count Johann Herbart Auersperg, General and Commander of the Military March, who died in 1669. The catafalque shown in this print is typical of a Baroque funeral ceremony of the type staged by the Jesuit Order, and designed to enchant the eye and spirit of viewers with the use of impressive effects.  
A bronze memorial plaque, also in the church, commemorates his death.
holder: Metropolitan Library, The Valvasor Collection of prints and drawings
place: From the Johann Weichard Valvasor Collection
keywords: Tomb; cenotaph; print; funerary architecture; theatrical architecture; ephemeral architecture; architectural sculpture; scenography; theatre

ar.name: صحن كبير مع زخرفة من الزهور.
description:
الصحن الكبير ذو حافة مسطحة، تزينه زخارف متعددة الألوان وخط كفافي أسود. وثمة شجيرة ملأى بالزهور والأوراق تخرج منها ثلاث باقات زهور على شكل سلال إلى جانب الزنابق والعيسلان على أعناق رقيقة تكاد تكون مستقيمة نحو الأعلى. أما باقات الزهور الكبيرة فتتخذ شكل سلال تدخل فيها السعيفات وأزهار اللوتس والقرع متضامة لتشكل وحدة متناسقة. وقد أتى ذكر ذلك على أنه "علم النبات الصنعي". وهذه الصورة هي جزء مما يسمى أسلوب الزهرات الأربع المكونة من أربع زهرات زينة، وهي الورد والقرنفل والسوسن والعيسلان، وهو أسلوب يشكل منذ حوالي عام 1540 المنظر الأساسي لأعمال الخزف التركية.  
ونرى على الحافة المعترضة منظر "الصخرة والماء" الذي يعود إلى تأثير صيني ويتشكل هنا من مناظر موجات بيضاء أمام صخور مرسومة بشكل لولبي. ويعود هذا المنظر إلى فن الخزف الصيني في القرن الخامس عشر. كان الخزف الصيني يجمع في البلاط العثماني ويستخدم كأوان للطعام حيث لا تزال بعض هذه القطع محفوظة حتى اليوم في قصر الباب العالي في استانبول.  
يوجد على السطح الخارجي للصحن ثلاثة أزواج من زهر السوسن وثلاثة مما يسمى "الكرة الثلاثية" أو منظر جينتماني الذي هو عبارة عن رمز للحظ يعود إلى الدوائر الحضارية البوذية. وهنا نجد ثلاث دوائر معبأة بنقطة ومرتبة على شكل هرمي ومتصلة مع مناظر لأشرطة مخططة كجلد النمر.  
والصحن مثال نموذجي لما يسمى أسلوب البلاط العثماني الذي تم تطويره في خان النقاش "دور الكتابة". وهنا ظهرت التصميمات المستخدمة في تزيين الكتب والأقمشة وأشغال التطريز والمعدن والخزف. وكان الكثير من صانعي الخزف في إزنيق يتعاملون بشكل مباشر مع فناني البلاط في السراي. كما كان أصحاب الحرف الفنية في ورشات البلاط في استانبول يأتون إلى إزنيق ويقيمون هناك لفترات يقدمون فيها المشورة لأرباب صناعة الخزفيات. وتبرهن حقيقة وجود الخزفيات العثمانية منذ القرن السادس عشر، على الأقل في دول أوروبية عديدة، على أن خزف إزنيق كان أجمل ويلقى قبولاً أكبر من "خزفيات الصين القيصرية".

كانت مشاغل الخزف في إزنيق، تصنع أطباقاً مُزيَّنة بالزهور، من أنماط مختلفة. هذا الطبق يعود إلى منتصف القرن العاشر الهجري/ السادس عشر الميلادي. ثمة على أرضية بيضاء، رشَّات من الورود والزنابق المتناظرة، مُنفَّذة عبر استخدام خليط ألوان الأسود، والأخضر الحشيشي، والأزرق المُظلَّل.

de.name: Großer Teller mit Blumendekor.
description: Der große Teller mit flachem Rand hat einen mehrfarbigen Dekor und schwarzer Konturlinie. Von einer Blütenstaude aus Blüten und Blättern wachsen drei Kompositblüten, Lilien und Hyazinthen an leicht bewegten Stengeln fast gerade nach oben. Die großen Kompositblüten sind künstlerisch gestaltet aus Elementen der Palmettblüte, der Lotosblüte und des Kürbis, die zu einer Einheit verbunden werden. Hiervon wurde schon als „Kunst-Botanik“ gesprochen. Dieses Repertoire ist Teil des sogenannten Quatre-Fleurs-Stil aus den vier Gartenblumen Rose, Nelke, Tulpe und Hyazinthe, das seit etwa 1540 das Hauptmotiv türkischer Keramik war. Auf dem quer liegenden Rand ist das auf chinesischen Einfluß zurückgehende „Felsen und Wasser“ Motiv zu erkennen aus weißen Wellenmotiven vor spiralig gezeichneten Steinen. Dieses Motiv entstammte der chinesischen Porzellankunst des 15. Jahrhunderts. Chinesisches Porzellan wurde am osmanischen Hof gesammelt und als Geschirr benutzt, wo es noch heute im Istanbuler Palast „Top Kapi Saray“ erhalten ist. Außen werden drei Tulpenpaare und dreimal das sogenannte „Dreikugel“ – oder Cintamani-Motiv gezeigt, das als Glückssymbol aus dem buddhistischen Kulturkreis stammt. Hierbei wurden drei mit einem Punkt gefüllte Kreise pyramidenförmig angeordnet und mit Motiven des Tigerfellstreifens verbunden. Der Teller ist ein typisches Beispiel für den sogenannten osmanischen Hofstil der im naqqash-chane („Schreibhaus“) entwickelt wurde. Hier entstanden die Entwürfe für Buchschmuck, Stoffmuster, Stickereien, Metall und Keramik. Viele Töpfer aus Iznik arbeiteten direkt mit den Hofkünstlern am Saray zusammen. Handwerker des Istanbuler Hofateliers hielten sich vor Ort in Iznik auf, um die Keramikmeister zu beraten. Das spätestens seit dem 16. Jahrhundert die osmanische Keramik in vielen Ländern Europas besondere Geltung hatte, beweisen türkische und Quellen des Abendlandes, die die Keramik aus Iznik als schön und besser als das „kaiserliche Porzellan aus China“ beschreiben.

Die Töpfereien in Iznik stellten zahlreiche Blumenteller in verschiedenen Stilformen her. Dieser stammt aus der Mitte des 16. Jahrhunderts. Vor einem weißen Hintergrund sind Gebinde von Hyazinthen und anderen Blumen symmetrisch arrangiert, wobei ein gedämpftes Farbschema aus Schwarz, Blassgrün und Abstufungen von Blau zum Einsatz kommt.
keywords: Türkei; Iznik; Osmanen; Quarzfrittekeramik; Unterglasurmalerei; Quatre-fleurs-Stil; Hyazinthen
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Large plate with floral decoration.
description:
This large plate with a flat rim is decorated with a variety of colours and black contour lines. Three composite flowers, lilies and hyacinths, grow, almost straight, out of a blossoming plant, on gently swaying stems. The large composite flowers have been creatively interpreted from elements of the blossoms of palms, lotus and marrow, all brought together to form a whole. This has been referred to as ‘botanical art’. This floral-design repertoire is part of the so-called ‘quatre fleurs’ (four flowers) style that is composed of four garden flowers – rose, carnation, tulip and hyacinth – and which, from around AH 945 / AD 1540, represented the main motifs of Turkish ceramics.  
Across the gently inward tilting rim is a Chinese-based rock-and-wave motif, composed of white waves rolling towards rocks drawn as spirals. This motif is derived from 15th-century Chinese porcelain painting. The Ottoman Court collected Chinese porcelain and used it as tableware, and the porcelain remains to this day in the safekeeping of the Topkapı Palace in Istanbul.  
On the outside are depicted three pairs of tulips and, repeated three times, the three-sphere or *chintamani* motif, which was a symbol of luck that originated from Buddhism. This motif consisted of three circles, each with a dot at the centre, placed in a pyramid formation, linked together with tiger stripes.  
The plate is a typical example of the so-called Ottoman Court-style that was developed in the *naqqash-hane* (writing-house). It was here that the designs for book decoration, textile patterns, embroidery, metalwork and ceramics were developed. Many potters from Iznik worked directly alongside the Court artists from the Topkapı Palace. Craftsmen from the art workshops of the Court in Istanbul travelled to Iznik in order to exchange ideas with the ceramic master craftsmen there. Ottoman ceramics were greatly valued in many European countries, from the AH 10th / AD 16th century onwards, proof of which can be found in Turkish and Western sources, which described Iznik ceramics as being as beautiful if not better than the imperial porcelain of China.

The potteries in Iznik made numerous flower plates in different styles. This one is from the middle of the 16th century. On a white ground, sprays of composite flowers and hyacinths are symmetrically arranged using a subdued colour scheme of black, celadon-green and shades of blue.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
Museum of Arts and Crafts, Berlin.

es.name: Plato con decoración floral.
description:
Gran plato de vuelo casi plano y decorado con tres flores compuestas (lirios y jacintos) de contornos negros y variado colorido cuyos tallos crecen, apenas ondulados, desde una planta en floración. Estas grandes flores compuestas son una creativa conjunción de las flores de palma, loto y calabaza, práctica que ha sido denominada “arte botánico”. Este repertorio floral formó parte del estilo *qautre fleurs* ('cuatro flores') compuesto por rosas, claveles, tulipanes y jacintos que, alrededor de 945 / 1540, representaron los motivos principales de la cerámica turca.  
El vuelo está decorado con el motivo de "rocas y olas", que consiste en olas blancas rompiendo contra rocas dibujadas como espirales. Este motivo se tomó de la pintura de la porcelana china del siglo IX / XV. La corte otomana coleccionaba porcelana china y la utilizaba como vajilla; esta porcelana se ha conservado hasta hoy en lugar seguro en el palacio Topkapi de Estambul.  
La parte externa está decorada con tres pares de tulipanes y, repetido tres veces, el motivo *chintamani*, símbolo de la buena suerte tomado del budismo y que consiste en tres círculos colocados en pirámide, cada uno con un punto en el centro y unidos por rayas de tigre.  
Este plato es un ejemplo típico del estilo cortesano otomano desarrollado en la *naqqash-hane* (casa de la escritura), donde se creaban los diseños que decoraban los libros, las telas, los bordados, la metalistería y la cerámica. Muchos alfareros trabajaron con los artistas de la corte del palacio Topkapi, y artesanos de los talleres artísticos palaciegos viajaron a Iznik para intercambiar ideas con los maestros ceramistas de la ciudad. La cerámica otomana fue muy apreciada en Europa a partir del siglo X / XVI, como lo demuestran fuentes tanto turcas como occidentales, que describen la cerámica de Iznik tan bella o más que la porcelana imperial china.

Los alfareros de Iznik fabricaron gran cantidad de platos decorados con motivos florales de diferentes estilos. En este ejemplo, del siglo X / XVI, ramilletes de flores compuestas y jacintos en tonos apagados de negro, verdeceledón y distintos azules se distribuyen simétricamente sobre un fondo blanco.

fr.name: Grande assiette à décor floral.
description:
Cette grande assiette à rebord plat est agrémentée d'un décor polychrome aux contours noirs. D'une plante faite de fleurs et de feuilles s'élèvent trois efflorescences composites, évoquant le lis et la jacinthe, qui se dressent presque droites sur des tiges à peine courbées. Ces efflorescences composites sont créées avec beaucoup de grâce à partir d'éléments de la fleur de palmier, de lotus et de courge. On a parlé à ce propos de “botanique artistique”. Ce répertoire fait partie du style “quatre-fleurs” élaboré à partir des quatre espèces horticoles que sont la rose, l'œillet, la tulipe et la jacinthe, un style qui constitua à partir de 945 H / 1540 J.-C. environ le motif principal de la céramique turque.  
Sur le pourtour du rebord, on remarque le motif “mer et rochers” inspiré de la Chine, les vagues blanches se détachant sur des pierres traitées en spirales. Ce motif est emprunté à la porcelaine chinoise du XVe siècle. Il y avait à la cour ottomane des collections de porcelaine chinoise, utilisée aussi comme vaisselle. Elle est aujourd'hui encore conservée au palais Topkapi Saray d'Istanbul.  
Sur le revers se trouvent trois paires de tulipes et, répété trois fois, le motif des trois boules ou motif *chintamani*, symbole porte-bonheur d'origine bouddhiste : trois cercles remplis d'un point disposés en pyramide et reliés par un motif évoquant les rayures du tigre.  
Cette assiette est un excellent exemple de ce qu'on appelle l'art princier élaboré par le *naqqash-chane* (la maison de l'écriture). On y créait les modèles d'ornementation utilisés dans l'enluminure, le textile, la broderie, le travail du métal et de la céramique. De nombreux potiers d'Iznik travaillaient directement avec les artistes du Saray. Des artisans de l'atelier de la cour d'Istanbul séjournaient à Iznik pour conseiller les maîtres-potiers. Jusqu'au Xe siècle H (XVIe siècle J.-C.) au moins, la céramique ottomane fut particulièrement appréciée dans de nombreux pays européens, comme l'attestent les sources turques et occidentales qui décrivent la beauté de la céramique d'Iznik, supérieure à “la porcelaine impériale de Chine”.

Les poteries d'Iznik comportaient de nombreuses assiettes à décor floral de styles variés. Celle-ci date du milieu du XVIe siècle. Sur fond blanc, des gerbes de fleurs composites et de jacinthes sont disposées symétriquement, utilisant des couleurs sobres de noir, vert céladon et différentes nuances de bleu.
keywords: Turquie ; Iznik ; Ottomans ; céramique en quartz fritté ; peinture sous glaçure ; quatre-fleurs; jacinthes
materials: Céramique en quartz fritté, peinture sous glaçure.
tags: Céramique en quartz fritté, peinture sous glaçure.

en.name: *Afshari* carpet
description:
Little is known about the rural rugs of Kirman so authors often describe them as *afshari* only for convenience and not as a precise label. The Afshari appear to be a minority population, although they may be the most important. They are a Turkic tribe with groups in the Caucasus, Turkey and Iran south of Kirman.  
Afshari products are seldom larger than about 170 x 200cm and they tend to be slightly more square-shaped. Some pieces have a striped kilim band at the ends. There are great variations in design, and many motifs found elsewhere are given a fresh approach, such as *boteh*, lozenge-shaped panels and medallion designs with flowers.  
In the central field on blue ground there are six “dragon palmette” motifs, six stylized floral motifs and numerous *boteh* and floret motifs. The “dragon palmette” motif is thought to derive from the “dragon and phoenix” motif of ancient Chinese origin. The palmette shape evolved from animal to vegetal. *Boteh* is the universal oriental rug design element. *Boteh* is Persian for “bush” and *buta* is Hindi for “flower”. It is thought to have originated in Kashmir in its curvilinear form. The form and content of *boteh*s are often distinctive for particular attributions and may be valuable clues to the origin of a weaving. The central field is framed with three borders. The main border resembles a floral meander on the blue background. The minor borders are also floral meanders on a white background. On the narrow sides the carpet has kilim finishes.
keywords: Persia; Afshari

en.name: Bektashi Dining Table
description:
The inscription indicates that the Aş Evi section, the most significant of the twelve houses in Bektashism, was constructed in 1560 by relatives of Malkoç Bali Bey, the Governor of Silistre, in his honor.  
The Aş Evi section, which is an independent building where the meals of the lodge are prepared, contains a room that is used by the Aş Evi Babası as a daily sitting room. In this room, he watches the kitchen work and decides on the meals to be prepared that day. It contains karakazan and halife boilers and kitchen utensils.  
The meals prepared in the Aş Evi were made available to the employees of the Dervish lodge and guests, as well as to the poor and the needy.

en.name: Virginal
description:
The maker of this glass-covered virginal is still unknown, and it has no known parallel among keyboard instruments, making it highly unique.  
  
The majority of the faces of the instrument are either enamelled or adorned with lamp-worked rods (tooled and fused in the open flame of a lamp or torch), whorls and florets. However, the inner lid is set with 18 panels which depict scenes from the Roman poet Ovid's work *Metamorphoses*. These intricately and exquisitely detailed scenes are framed within scrolling borders and each is labelled with the name of the characters who appear in the 25 books that constitute the poem. Included are Acteon, the hunter who, after catching sight of the goddess Diana bathing was transformed into a stag and killed by his own hounds.  
  
The uniqueness of the virginal has meant it has been associated with a glass virginal that was described as in the possession of Elizabeth I at Hampton Court. A German traveller named Paul Hentzner wrote in 1598 of 'a musical instrument made all of glass except the strings'. However, other contemporary descriptions of instruments at Hampton Court describe them being encrusted with jewels and inscribed with the Queen's cypher, which this instrument is unfortunately lacking.
place: Vienna; Adolfov / Adolf; Nový Bor / Haida
artist: Hoffmann, Josef (design); Meyr's Neffe (manufacturer); Johann Oertel & Co. (manufacturer); Wiener Werkstätte (client / customer)

en.name: *Ayasofya (Hagia Sophia)*
short_description: The majority of Turkish painters in the 19th century were Ottoman officers who had studied abroad. Hüseyin Zekai Paşa was one of those painters who paints in the western style. In his first works, he followed the painting tradition of 19th century by including thin paint dough and light colours. He made changes in his painting techniques through the Galatasaray Exhibition and turned into an impressionist, his work dominated by thicker brush strokes. In his paintings he combined impressionist colour techniques and a totality of composition with dexterity. Şeker Ahmet Paşa, Osman Hamdi Bey and Hüseyin Zekai Paşa opened the way for other Turkish artists – and in particular impressionists – in Turkey.
holder: Mimar Sinan Fine Arts University, Painting and Sculpture Museum
keywords: Painting; Hüseyin Zekai Paşa; orientalist Turkish painters
